Outstanding food and wine list. We had a reservation for 4 and had 2 additional colleagues join us at the last minute. Luckily there was a table that sat 6 and the hostess was very kind in accommodating a last minute request.

We decided to order and eat "family style" which was excellent. We knew that the Tea Leaf Salad was a given, and asked the waiter for his recommendations, and we decided upon: Lemongrass  Chicken, Basil Chili Beef, Burmese Pad Thai, Pumpkin Pork Stew, Veggie Kebat, and brown rice.  All were order as medium spicy.  Everything was excellent, and the level of spice worked well for the group.  We ordered a bottle of the Grgich Hills Cabernet, and a 2005 Turley Zinfandel, which the waiter decanted.  Both wines were great, and the Zin matched the spiciness of the food perfectly. Saweet!!!

Service was a bit slow as the place was packed on a Thursday night, but we had enough conversations going on that it was not an issue for us. 
The hostess came by as were finishing and asked what we had, and offered a few other choices if we come back, and she took a group picture of us-so nice.

Great atmosphere, good vibe, so folks, park your self-importance at the door, relax, have fun and let the evening flow.
The food was so tasty and service was swift.  Noise level (important for my husband with hearing difficulties) was manageable, at least at 5:30 p.m.
Both the food as well as the service were excellent! We had a great time
Terrifically interesting and tasty food, cordial, friendly and efficient service.  All of the right ingredients for a memorable culinary experience.

Been there many times and have to say, was disappointed with the food. Usually the garlic eggplant is a must and it was okay and the pumpkin salmon stew was not good at all. Had a strong fishy smell for salmon. Service was great as always, however.

Our 2 person table was very cramped. And the vegetable kebat was part uncooked, we mentioned this and they kindly cooked it more but not completely. We were tired of reporting it and just are it. Not worth the $. Nothing special for vegetarians.

This restaurant used to be nice with fantastic food. Off late, the food quality is terrible. The tea leaf salad which is a popular dish is brought and mixed in front of your by the server but i guess even on a not-so-busy day he was rushing to mix only to leave lumps of tea leaf mixture in some portions. The eggplant dish he recommend made me believe that i should never trust these recommendations from these serves, it was awful, full of thick soy, sweet, greasy and corn starch filled. We ended up leaving most of our dish.

Two of us shared the vegetarian samosas, tea leaf salad, and garlic shrimp and eggplant entree. The shrimp dish would have benefited from a little more shrimp and a little less eggplant, but we enjoyed all the dishes and left feeling fully satiated. The server was very informative and made sure that we didn't object to any of the ingredients. But we had to ask for our third dish after we had finished the first two and were left waiting longer than we liked. I did see a lot of take-out orders being picked up, so I wonder if that had something to do with it. We also had to flag down a waiter for more water and the check. So although the wait staff was very nice, they could be more attentive.  Overall, we enjoyed the meal and would go back.
Love the tea leaf salad!  Always consistently good.  We found the "fiery" tofu to be fairly mild.  If you order it, ask for some spice on the side.
As in our previous visits the food was good, the service personable and the price as expected. A really nice place to bring visitors.
Amazing food & ambience. Very good cocktails too. Loved it.

Yummy food but.... Chaotic service, from snippy hostess to soup coming out before the pre-dinner drinks.  AND then to top it off, they marked that we didn’t honor our Open Table reservation! Not cool.

I would only recommend this place because of the tea tree salad. This place is very cramped, noisy, and the staff are unfriendly. You can't go here on a date or business meeting. Don't pick this place if you are looking for a good dining experience. Get the food to go, you'll have a much better time. They only have a couple really good dishes. Even the staff will tell you some of it is not good.
Great Food and Great service. The flavors are intense and incredible! I cannot recommend it more highly.
Food, custom cocktails, and service were all very good.
Our  neighboring table had people that were talking too loudly and with the tables being so close the entire meal was too distracting as we couldn't hear each other.
Service was terrible - waited more than 30 minutes to get our check
Waiter made all the recommendations which worked perfectly for us.

Good service, blah (bland) food, good atmosphere.....
Will not be returning anytime soon.

Reserved table but they wouldn’t seat us until all four of us were even though it was just one parking and half the restaurant was empty so we around in the way of people going in and out of the entrance while our table sat vacant. 
Food was extremely salty. 
Passed by the evening before and saw people seated and eating having just been served their food at 9:45 at night while the waitstaff started stacking chairs onto the tables that weren’t occupied. Should have known better. Service in restaurants is increasingly being compromised as a get em in and out as fast as possible seems to be the new mantra.
Great except for the noisd
Outstanding food but service is a bit lacking
Always good food, great ambiance. tea leaf salad is the best! Parking and nearby road work makes getting to the place a challenge!
Food was great, service was terrible.  If you can’t keep up in the dining room and at the bar, reduce your reservations.  Also, it’s a small space, they are trying to fit in too many tables/covers.
Tea Leaf salad is still to die for. Mango swai was delicious, as usual. Fiery tofu vegetable kebat was tasty and had just the right amount of heat. I love the sunlight.
We had a very nice dinner ! Smooth and efficient service, great food !

I do not usually write review if the restaurant experience is as expected. We had a good experience with this restaurant before this visit but we are never coming back again. 

We were 20 minutes early but the hostess was able to seat us after 5 minutes so long as we promise that we will finished in time for the next reservation. We were seated in the middle of the restaurant but it was 20 minutes before the waiter took our order. He said he will bring dishes to the table as they were made. We waited for at least 20 minutes and we did not even have our appetizer. At one point our waiter told us our food was coming soon. In the mean time food was served to 3 tables with patrons who were seated after us. One of them was the table next to ours. They finished their dinner and we still have no food. Our waiter kept walking through the other side of the restaurant as if he did not want to encounter us. 

Eventually, my husband went to talk to the host and he just said that some dishes took more time than others. Instead of being polite and help us check on our order, he appeared to be blaming us. We did not order anything special. He said our lemongrass pork was what the problem but it was not the last dish to get served. We were almost at the point of walking out before our dishes were served. Later on, other staff came and asked if we were finished, wanted any dessert (which I planned to but decided against it due to the unpleasant experience). We then got the check from a different waiter. Once again we waited while many staff members walked by our table but no one picked up our credit card to process. In the end, we just put cash on the table and left. My husband still left a $10 tips as he said it was Christmas Eve. I gave $2 directly to the bus person who kept refilling our water glasses.

I had dined there previously so wanted my husband to enjoy it too.  It was my 86th Birthday so a very special occasion!  The welcome and seating were friendly and our server was outstanding through out.  He paced the meal well, and the low lights and intimate atmosphere we had selected worked perfectly - along with outstanding food!

The capper came when we asked for the check and were told that our meal had been comped!  We had not really mentioned our destination to anyone and could not ascertain who was giving us such a gift.   After coming home, I waited until near closing time and called - speaking to the nice young woman who had seated us.
She checked and found that two women seated near us had enjoyed watching our enjoyment and thought we were CUTE!   Hilarious and so noice!

We plan on describing all this to the local Palo Alto paper thanking them, and mentioning that we will contribute our same amount to Second Harvest!
What a lovely Birthday!

The food was delicious: tea salad, samosas, spicy shrimp, sesame beef, garlic noodles and coconut rice. The chicken curry was very disappointing. It was made with dark meat and had a very thin sauce.

Our server, Amy, was excellent.

I've always enjoyed the food here, especially the tea salad.  I also like that Rangoon Ruby can adjust the spices to your taste.  So, though my earlier experiences have been good, this one lacked due to being ignored for 100+ minutes.  I finally had to get up and go to the receptionist to get my bill and pay the bill.  I still like the restaurant, and I'll be back, because anyone (Eric) can have a bad day.
We celebrated our anniversary here. It was great atmosphere, service, food and cocktails. Would recommend.
I was a frequent patron of Rangoon 2 years ago and went back recently only to be served Pad Thai soup. There was far too much sauce and it was unpalatable. I will not be going back.

Food and service were just okay. I liked the restaurant but I have been to other Burmese restaurants where the food was better.  The waiter was nice but because they were so busy the wait for our beers from the bar took an inordinately long time. Would return but probably will go elsewhere first.

Cocktails are half full and most of the drink is ice. Save your money. Tea leaf salad is awesome. Eggplant and lamb are excellent. Hostess gave our request for specific table away despite confirmation on phone one hour before! Go figure. Bar disappointing but food is pretty good
It wasn't busy, so the noise level was fine. When it's busy, it can be very loud!
I love so many items--the garlic noodles are soooo good!

Tea was hot water and tea bag, more like Hilton breakfast tea than any authentic Burmese tea
Tea leave salad was best!
Noodles seems to have too much sweetness to it than much flavor to it.
It seems to have gone downhill.  The salad they are well known for  (tea leaf) has no spark.  It's just not as good as it once was.
I’ve been enjoying Rangoon Ruby and Burma Ruby for years and recommend them highly. The food is consistently terrific!

We enjoyed our dinner very much.  The only downside is that the restaurant is very noisy so it's difficult to hear your own conversation.  Food great.  Service terrific! I would go again and highly recommend you do too!
Very good food and wonderful service. Good drinks and active location.

First, note that the restaurant reported me as a "walk in" even though I had made an online reservation. This meant I received NO Open Table points --and I think they did this so  didn't have to pay Open Table a reservation fee. So they lied. It was so noisy we could hardly hear one another. Tables are squished together. Then I Googled them and discovered the owners have been fined MILLIONS for cheating workers of pay--unpaid overtime, taking tips from workers. Unsavory owners. I'm never going back to any of their restaurants.

Attentive but not intrusive service. Delicious Burmese cuisine especially the tea salad -- I wish I had some right now. The staff recommends planning to share each dish, and the portions are large enough to be satisfying. Rangoon Ruby is a great spot for an early dinner before a movie at the Aquarius theater across the street.

We had an enjoyable meal here, other than the fact that the receptionist ignored our request to sit by the window.  The drinks were delicious, followed by the wonderful tea leaf salad.  Then we had 3 of my favorite dishes, lemongrass chicken, mango swai, and eggplant shrimp.  The level of spiciness was perfect.
Amazing food and service!  Our waiter was outstanding.
The service was amazing. The food was great! You must try the tea leaf salad as you will not be disappointed! Must try!
The tea leaf salad is always so good! And the curries. Definitely will keep going to this restaurant when in Palo Alto.
Excellent food as always. Tea salad if fabulous, lamb kabat wonderful. Many great items on the menu.

For the second time in a row, one of our main dishes arrived 15 to 20 minutes after all the another dishes. It was impossible to get the attention of wait staff, and even things like the rice to go with the main dishes didn’t arrive for an additional 10 to 15 minutes

Really good meal - there were three of us  We had the tea leaf salad which was very good.  We ordered 3 different chicken dishes  and some coconut rice and everything was excellent.

We got there at 6 pm with a reservation.  By 6:30 it was completely full - that tells me that the food was good.

We come back again.

Food was very good. Tea leaf salad had great flavor. Also liked the lemongrass chicken and walnut shrimp. 

Service speed is always interesting to assess. Too slow is bad. You want efficient and attentive service. However, it can cross a line when it is clear that efficiency and speed is not about giving you a good experience, it is about turning the table. Felt this from the minute we sat down. This was a Saturday evening. I could tell by the drive of the waiter to take the order and get it to the kitchen that we were going to have to fight to be there for longer than 30 mins. I told him 'we are not in a rush'. A minute later came our salad. No problem they are pre-prepared in the back for serving but zero thought that we may be out for an evening meal, not to race off to somewhere else. About five minutes later came our entrees. We had literally been in the restaurant for about 15 minutes and were served the full meal. Actually there is some irony because despite the fact we ordered rice, somehow they forgot to bring that. Waited several minutes, probably 10, before that showed up. It was just paced so poorly that I cannot imagine going back.

Then the bill comes. They have added an "ACA Surcharge" of $3.50. I asked the waiter what it was and he said it was to cover the additional cost of Obamacare (Affordable Care Act). wtf? Have no idea what political message this is intended to send but I am totally annoyed it is being sent to me through the bill (or at all for that matter). Add a $1 to each entrée if you must but to call it out and emphasize they are asking me to pay it is pathetic. 

Great food but I will never go back and if anyone asks me, they will hear about this experience.
We had to wait for 25 mins to get out table. Food and service was outstanding
The curry beef is not very flavorful and it doesn't have any vegetables.

This is one of our favorite restaurants in Palo Alto, but on this particular night, the service and food were both disappointing.  The service was extremely slow.  Perhaps the kitchen is understaffed.  And the food was really bland.  We like a little spice, at least.  But we will go back, in hopes that it was just a off night.
The food, as always, was delicious. Our server was attentive and quite pleasant. We appreciate not being rushed, as we had not seen our friends for a while. It was nice to relax and catch up.

It was an excellent experience--as always!  Their food is unusual and interesting.
Always fresh.  I go early because it gets a bit noisy for an older person with some
hearing issues when the restaurant if full.

Food tasted old and not fresh. We went with the waitress recommendations and the chicken dish tasted old. The fish dish was extremely salty but no real flavor. Also, usually the waiters ask what spice level you want and she didn’t, so we ended up with no spice at all which was unfortunate. We didn’t think of it when ordering so partially our fault for not asking but they always ask.

As a true food lover looking for unique culinary experiences, I am pleased that this has become one of my family's all-time favorite restaurants.  My teen-aged kids love their tea leaf salad and the sesame beef,  and their samosa soup is amazing.  Every dish I have tried at this restaurant has exceeded my expectations.

Recommended by a friend.  Entree choices varied, many of them.  Husbands pork curry came in large chunks(we had no knives)and was not tender.  My lemon grass chicken was a better choice.  Drinks were average if expensive.   It was noisy, tables crowded together,  kitchen or service slow.
Amazing food and service, good value!

Rangoon Ruby was not nearly up to the quality of food and service that we expected based on going there three or four times in the past couple of years.  The food was poorly prepared and service was uninspired.  No longer recommended, there are other options.
The Waiters were so nice to us in preparing dishes and answering our questions about how they made some of their famous dishes. The yellow tofu and tea leaf salad were amazing and not to miss.

Rangoon Ruby and its sister restaurant Burma Ruby are my favorite places for a lunch or dinner.
But after being very popular and hard to get a table, I find that it is much easier to get a reservation.
Part of the reason is that food quantity and quality has fallen off and service is slow and not very attentive.
The tea leaf salad seems to have shrunk in size. I think they have to retool and rethink their strategy...for the prices they charge they should improve service and serving sizes
Felt the prices were high for the size of the dishes. Overall food tasted very good, service was a little slow especially when coming to take our order and bring our drinks.

Good food, but the tables were very close together so much so that I could hear more of the next tables conversation then I wanted to. If they weren’t so concerned about maximizing their profits and took out a couple of tables and opened it up a bit it would make  it a much more pleasant experience.
The Rangoon Ruby team went out of their way to accommodate our short noticed increased party size. Service was terrific and food did not disappoint.

Great food and great service as always. They do need to not hire inexperience kids at the reception. We specifically asked for a quiet corner since we were dining with a newborn. She didn’t have that note from OpenTable in her system, plus we got the cold shoulder as we disrupted her seating arrangements despite a near-empty restaurant. She was very unhappy that we didn’t call after our reservation online to check with the restaurant about the newborn. If the food and service wasn’t great, this would have been our last visit to our favorite restaurant!

The tea leaf salad is not to be missed. Four of us shared three entrées that was really more than enough the mango shrimp sesame chicken and eggplant and shrimp dishes for all wonderful save a little bit of room for dessert as you will not be disappointed. Service was really excellent.  The restaurant can kick crowded and tight so just be prepared but the service and food are worth it
Excellent service and nice ambiance. Highly recommend the tea leaf salad and the mint jalapeño chicken.

Super tasty food with plenty of fresh variations to satisfy most tastebuds. House special cocktails were great, as were the ginger salad, beef and pork entrees. Wait staff nearly perfect. Very enjoyable meal. Well, done, Rangoon Ruby!

Good Asian fusion. Reasonable use of spice bit consistently amped way up on sugar in the sauce. Interesting blend of ingredients. Too tea leaf salad. Very noisy; don't go if you intend a quiet conversation.  They place the tables very close together so not a lot of elbow room. Attentive service. $30 pp for lunch with only sparkling water.

As always, place was busy and thriving. Food was great! I made a reservation for my friend’s birthday— their bday dessert presentation is unique! They serve ice cream with a huge, eyecatching lit flare!

We ordered:

*Tea leaf salad (so many different ingredients/textures)
*Vegetarian Palata (I like the original chicken one, but this was tasty too.)
*Fried tofu (seemed like Taiwanese style w/ chopped fried garlic)
*Samosas were given on the house! Thanks!
*Basil chili beef (my fave!)
*Ruby shrimp
*Vegetable Kebat
*Indian Burmese rice
*Jasmine rice

Drinks: tito’s Mule, crazy coconut in an actual coconut, hibiscus mojito, and non-alcoholic Surfer Punch

It’s pricey, but a fantastic experience for birthdays, and trying out Burmese food for the first time. Service was accommodating.

The tea salad and Burmese Pad Thai were delicious.  But the curry lamb and chicken dish were disappointing.   As we had a late dinner on Father's Day, all the waiters were extremely busy.   It took us four times before we got more water.   Hope the service will be better on a regular evening.

Been here a few times and why return, might you ask ? It was all because the v first time we came it was splendid and the service was better and they made an effort on my daughters birthday. The next time, we were so disappointed when we returned for another family member's birthday. The food made us ill, the service was bad and they forgot dishes we had ordered and never made up for that. The food didnt taste as well, either. We left a message for the manager but nothing was returned. A few years later, and only because our love for Burmese food had grown after finding a new place to haunt, we mistakenly went again. I was horrified that we had ever liked it. It was dirty and noisy. The bathroom ( even though we went there at 5 pm) looked like it had suffered a night of nightclub goers who were drunken to explain the lack of cleanliness. I would be surprised if the kitchen has been checked out. It was so filthy. I really can't believe it, to be honest. The service was poor and they made us feel like they were doing us a favor giving us food or drink. Our rice was forgotten but luckily they didnt seem to add the dish to the bill so we didn't complain. The food was nothing like our new favorite Burmese place. It didn't feel as fresh or as tasty as it used to be and definitely nothing in comparison to our new find. The samosa salad was fairly good. 
We didn't get offered dessert and felt guilty asking for the menu and after we decided what we wanted, no-one came back to take the order so we just quit and asked for the bill back. Not going back. I would be surprised if this wasn't a new owner and or chef since our very first visit a few years ago. It is a shame. We had hoped that the last two times were bad luck and were willing to give it a shot, again. Bummer !!

We had a lovely Father's Day lunch. I had booked with some concern about the service based on other OpenTable reviews, but we got water within the first minute, tasty food came out at the same time,  and our server was efficient, positive, and knew the menu without being overbearing. We plan to eat there again.
Good food, service was excellent
Food was awesome!  However, our server was not organized.  He had to get our order again since he threw away the paper where he wrote our order.  Then he had to be reminded about my beverage order.
We have eaten here several times before, but this time the food was very disappointing.  The shrimp with mango had very little mango and the chicken curry lacked flavor.
Food fabulous. Service very slow. Way too noisy.
Love this place. Very tasty food with efficient service.

Made a reservation beforehand, got a table in no time however:

1. Server got both of our orders wrong
2. After taking back my plate for a replacement, replacement order took about 30 mins to come
3. The replacement server brought out was wrong
4. Kept one of the original incorrect orders at the table to not come across rude, but turned away the replacement order and told the server to not bring anything else out because it would take too long.
5. Server marked "DID NOT LIKE" on the receipt and zeroed out that item. Nice of him to remove the item, not nice of him to lie on the receipt.

Don't think I'll be coming back to this place.

The worst mothers day experience.  
1. Slow
2. Did not see my waiter most of the time
3.  Did not get anything asked like napkin, check, drinks etc.
4. Food was simply ok, nothing special
5. Will not come back for mothers day again
I was there celebrating birthday.
Food was excellent as always. Service was a little less friendly than usual.
Super yummy, but a bit crowded. Hard to walk to the bathroom without getting in the way of the waitstaff.

Lacked taste.  Tea salad and veggie curry.  Wait staff seemed untrained and kept bumping into table(at least 10 times).  When arrived, told I had no reservation even though I had Open Table confirmation emails.  Had really great experiences before, not sure what happened.
Love the food here.  Always enjoy the tea leaf salad and the sesame beef . I had a grand aunt who was Burmese and the Burmese beef curry reminds me of hers.
The food, our server Eric, and our overall experience was excellent.  Highly recommend.

Very good meal, as usual.  We love the tea leaf salad - always good.  In addition, we had the mango swai and the lemongrass chicken, which were both delicious.  Service was good, and the ambiance is nice.
Very tasty food, excellent atmosphere and pleasant ambience
Order the calmari appetizer and the shrimp with eggplant
Excellent food.  Super nice staff.  Service a teeny bit slow, but attentive and nice.

Met two friends for out of state and they were very pleased.  Especially liked the tea leaves salad (specialty).  Noodles were good.  Whiskey sour was good also.  The noise level increased as the restaurant filled after 7:00pm.  Parking was a bit of a challenge.  Would certainly return.
Great food, bad attitude from maitre’d and apathetic outlook from server. Who do these people think they are?
Just an all around great experience! Next time in the Bay Area, it will be a “must do”.

The food -- there were four of us and all hungry -- covered a spectrum from very good to amazing. The starters, esepcailly the salads, were more impressive than the main courses, but that seems to have become the new norm in California restaurants. The wines were way expensive but at least of appropriate quality. It was the crowding of the tables and the conversation-killing noise that disappointed me. Why must gourmet dining be victimized by shrill whoopee and (ugh!) background music? I'm sick of loud restaurants! Most of the civilized world does without what Open Table coyly calls "energetic" noise levels. Why can't America learn table manners? Or rather, why can't restauranteurs have a little mercy with table spacing?

Seems overrated. Even the "spicy" dishes were somehow bland and over-salted at the same time. The cocktail was good but took forever to be served. Best thing is the tea leaf salad, which is worth trying.

If you're going to the movies at the Aquarius Theater right across the street, this is a very convenient place to dine beforehand. The food is excellent, the menu varied, the service excellent.  The prices are about average for Palo Alto ... in the mid-range.  My only gripe is that it's a small place and they try to cram as many customers in as possible. The tables are so close you can barely move... but other than that, not a bad choice for a pre-movie dinner.

Nice variety of options for GF dining, and the server took care to communicate to the kitchen our needs - as one diner had celiac disease.  Our food was delicious and our food sensor test always indicated that food was GF.  The service was excellent all around.  A nice dining experience
Customer service can greatly improved, often rude!
Great food; excellent service (didn't have to ask for water refill once); very accommodating of our needs.  Highly recommend.
Delicious food, excellent & attentive service. Always a great time at Rangoon Ruby.
The food and drinks are always great here. It's a bit loud on a Friday night, weekdays are usually better.
Great and attentive service. Food was okay.
Excellent food, very nice Valentines Day menu. Staff were especially helpful and went our of their way to explain ingredients as well as wine pairings.
Great food as always. Love the variety of flavors on the menu

We like this place and it's sister restaurant on University in Palo Alto.  
One downside:  this is the second time we've been here when the food comes way too fast.  
We came here with another couple to enjoy the interesting dishes (like the tea leaf salad) and to catch up with old friends.  But the meal felt too rushed.
Just love this place.  The food is so unique and awesome!
Authentic Burmese food and particularly their tea-leaf salad.

The food is always delicious - especially the coconut noodle soup and the mango salad. Yum! Other favorites are the coconut sticky rice, pumpkin and salmon stew, and green beans. Their bar drinks are also really good. A great place for a delicious meal and a fun night out.
Fantastic food as always. We keep getting more friends to this place as we love the food here!!
As always the fermented tea leaf salad was the highlight of the meal, but the mango chicken was also quite delicious!
It was Christmas Eve and very busy and crowded. Lots of families. Everyone was celebrating. Beautiful to see such happiness. It was like a big party. Food and service was excellent!!
Return again and again

Very tasty and interesting!  We come to this restaurant and their sister restaurant on University Ave (Palo Alto) somewhat frequently.  In the past we felt very rushed here, but the service this time was MUCH better.  Attentive, prompt, but not at all rushed.  
Everything was good!  The salads, appetizers, entrees.  All sharable and interesting.  
Extensive wine list and cocktail list, and they also made several other cocktails not on the cocktail menu.

I loved all of their non-meat options, including many tasty tofu dishes.

The food is good but they do not know what they are doing.  Forgot the tomatos in the salad.  Only put 4 shrimp in Pad Tai when there are supposed to be 6.  You need to get your act together as when done right the food is good.

We were greeted and seated right away.  Our table was off of the main entrance and there was a cold draft but upon mention, the host closed the door.  Server was quick, very attentive and the food came in no time.  My friends who have never been to this restaurant were very impressed.  Food was delish as always.  We had the green tea salad, chicken crisp, beef basil, shrimp walnut and shrimp curry.  Tons of food for the four of us.  Can't wait to go back!
Tables are way too close together,  hard to talk,  hard to hear...really uncomfortable.
Birthday, the waitress was really nice but the remaining folks bringing in food from inside were rude and unfriendly.

I really loved the food here, the only thing is that it was my our first time there, and we would've loved that our waiter had mentioned that plates are big and good for sharing, we had so many left-overs, but apart from that everything was super good!

We had the tea leaf salad, nan gyi dok, and the lamb curry which was recommended by our server. All were delicious! In my opinion, worth coming here over Burma Superstar as there is no wait and they take reservations.

Was eager to check this restaurant out based on reviews.   My greatest complaint is that the entries were lukewarm at best and one had cold chicken mixed in with warm - unpleasant.  The noodles were over cooked, as well. Though table side presentation was very nice.  Just ok for two @ $100, could have done better elsewhere
Amazing flavors! This is a find. The selections and diversity is perfection. From the tea salad, Calamari appitizer's, Coconut rice, and diversity of fish, chicken and meat dishes, this is a winner!
Overall very good. Service was a bit slow and in attentive.

It was a little weird that the wine selection was on an iPad.  This was a cool gimmick but didn't really help us decide what to drink and cluttered the table.  The staff was very attentive, but this could have been because they could clearly tell we were on a date.  We both ordered the pad thai, which was very good if somewhat simple.  Wasn't expecting much more from that dish.  The prices are a little steep, but I moved to the Bay recently so it could be that I am just experiencing sticker shock.  Great ambience.  Cool decorations.  A little noisy for a date.

What a find!!!!
We were visiting family, and they suggested we try Rangoon Ruby's out.  What a delightful experience, the food was memorable!   We ordered the shrimp with walnuts, crispy chicken,  and several other dishes, and all were delicious!  We can hardly wait to go back!!! 
I strongly recommend you try it out!!!
I was expecting a bit better. Expensive for what we paid. Around $50 per person. May go again if I am in the area. Overall, average at best.
Yummy food! Loved the tea leaf salad. Lots of options for a vegetarian.

2 things happened
A) Server walked by table and serving spoon fell of and server was not even aware it happened. Serving spoon was on floor and we ended up using existing silverware to serve ourselves
B) I had mentioned in open table it was someone'e birthday and I thought there might be some dessert or something but none of it happened
Too noisy, excellent food and service

Unfortunately, our experience was NOT a delightful one.  It started off okay, but went down hill.  My friends took me to Rangoon for my birthday.  I had heard about it and was excited to try it.  When the food arrived.....I did not get anything.  The guy said, "Is there anything else I can help you with?" when he dropped off my friends' dishes.  I said, "Uhm, maybe you can bring me some food."   The FIRST WAIT -- We had already waited for their dishes and then THE SECOND WAIT --we waited another 10 minutes while we watched other tables receiving food and the guy noticed us still sitting there and says, "Your food should be coming shortly".  My friends would not start without me since they thought the food was almost there.  THE THIRD WAIT -- Another 15 - 18 minutes and the Walnut Shrimp meal arrives.   It didn't look appealing and it did not taste good (in all honesty).   I had my friend try it and she wouldn't even eat it after tasting one.

I really don't know what was really happening, but I wish we could have just been told the truth about the situation and I could have ordered something else.   My friends were annoyed and their food was cold.   Anyway, it really put a damper on my birthday celebration ----  a long wait for a NOT tasty meal!   Sorry Rangoon Ruby, I can't give you a high rating.  I really wish I could.....

Also, we felt a little unable to relax because they seem to want you to get out of there so that it can be closed down before dinner service.  We literally left and went to a coffee shop.   I got home and needed something to eat -- I was totally hungry!
It was amazing. Ambiance was great
Fantastic food, and smiling, fast service. A little noisy, but manageable. Have already been back a second time!
What's the point of taking a 930 reservation when you want the customer out by 10?  Bad practices.
You can't go wrong here! Great service, authentic food, and a nice ambiance. With the exception of some rice dishes needing to be served faster while its hot, Ragoon Ruby will never disappoint.

This is our go-to place when we want a meal before a film that starts at 6-7pm, because of its service, quality and location. The tea salad is known widely and very popular, and my spouse had that, but this time I tried the Burmese Pad Thai (Pad Burmese?), which was very good and something I will get again. Those who like tropical drinks have a nice selection from which to choose, but they are pricey. Stay with tea and one entree and  a couple gets out for about $30.

Very busy on a Tuesday evening. Good service. We were seated quickly with our reservation. The host and waitress were friendly and helpful. Tables are a bit close together so you're eating very close to your neighbors. The food is ok. We tried the popular dishes recommended by the waitress and they were a bit underwhelming. I found many of them to be a bit too salty for me. Ambiance is nice and energetic.

You get your order in a heartbeat.  Servers give you full attention and respond to your needs with out most cooperation.  The family is a fan of the tea leaf salad.  First time to order a lamb dish from this place and it was amazing!!!

We were happy with everything altogether.
Loveless Burmese such as tea salad, fun curries and stir fries.

The food quality is degrading by the day (or maybe it was our bad luck). Food was super oily and flavorless. The calamari was absolutely inedible, garlic noodles were a let down as well. The only saving grace were the Burmese Tea and the chili swai fish.

Had dinner with 2 of my friends at the restaurant on a Friday night. The waiter was okay, not very personable. The restaurant needs better ventilation/ air circulation.
Our eyes were burning, probably due to the fumes from the spices. The food was okay. What bothered me was that the waiter just brought out our check without asking if we wanted dessert. They also added a 20% gratuity to our bill, which didn't make sense to me since there were only three of us.
Delicious food for reasonable prices. Definitely try the tea leaf salad.
I love this place! The food is delicious and the staff really kind! Some of my fav plates: basil chili beef, beef kebat, pumpkin salmon, samosa, palata! Yummy!!!
Amazing food and service, as always. The tea leaf salad is incredible and the walnut shrimp is to die for. Highly recommend dinner here!
Awesome meal. Helpful servers. Tea leaf salad and coconut rice are both craveable.

As has been said repeatedly, this is a wonderful restaurant with fabulous authentic Burmese food; but they really jam the tables together.  With the noise level, it was hard to hear conversation among our group of 5.

From the warm reception by the charming hostess to the outstanding service from our attentive waiter, this was a first-class dining experience. Better half had the famous tea salad  and I had the Samosa salad; both were, as expected, delicious to the last morsel (clean plate club). We started with the lettuce wraps, which we split,  and asked for more hoison sauce, which appeared in seconds. I wondered to myself if perhaps we should have stopped there, because I felt satiated, but I pressed on and was very glad I did. The Samosa salad was new to me but the waiter had recommended it; he was right.
We had a movie date around the corner at the Stanford Theater and we made it with time to spare.
Interesting, well-prepared food - our second visit left us with a similar impression as our first - we'll be back!
food was great!  don't quite have their act together in terms of reservations.  alot of waiting for  while the hostess are trying to figure out who is on first.  i'd try again .
A picky friend recommended this spot. (We all have that friend, who doesn't like eating at subpar places hahaha). The food was orgasmic - so rich and full of flavor with each bite.

What a great place to gather. The service was fantastic!  Our server was attentive and informative.  The food was delicious!  Samosas, pad Thai , lemongrass pork, crispy chicken were among a few of our favorites this visit.  Will definitely go back!

Same high quality, well-seasoned food that one would exoect from one of the "Burma (superstar)" restaurants. The Burma (Ruby) brands in general, attempt to provide a more upscaled dining experience in its contemporary decor and higher prices. While Chihuly chandeliers tastefully line the ceiling, the noise level and floorplan made it less enjoyable of an experience. The waiters must squeeze through a maze just to get to your table! We were also seated so closely to the couple next to us, I felt like I was a part of their vacation plans discussion!
Service was great,food tended to be average and a little greasy
Food was good, flavorful, and served at an easy, unrushed cadence.  Appetizer of Salt and Pepper Calamari was done just right without overcooking. Entree choices are excellent.
The food here is very good but the service was inconsistent. Don't make a reservation after 1:30pm or you'll be rushed to order before the kitchen closes. Too harried.

My friend is vegan, so we had two tofu dishes, one with pea leaves and the other was a curry with lots of different vegetables.  Both were delicious, in fact, if my boyfriend liked tofu, I would order them again with him.  The service was very attentive,  and the ambiance was nice because we had a window table.
I now know that I love Burmese food. Great spot in Palo Alto for any occasion. It really picked up around 7:30/8:00pm.

The Basil Chicken was much more spicy than one of our party expected and I felt we should have been told so in advance by the server. All the dishes were great, given that, and we loved the creative menu.  Will definitely go back.
The curry chicken and curry lamb were blah. The salmon was good and the spicy pork was great.
Food was great. Service was ok. Seating was way too close and cramped.

On this visit, we tried the chicken salad, which was a nice change from the tea leaf salad. The chicken had a sweet and spicy sauce.  We also had the mango swai, but it was a little mushy. The owner recognized us and gave us free drinks, a nice gesture.
Will return for sure!
Absolutely awesome. Love Rangoon Ruby!

Been at the Resturant more than 30 times.  Service and food is good.  I love the eggplant dish with prawns but this time it was only few little shrimps in a dish.  The pumpkin chicken was not the same.  Beef with basil was ok this time, chicken Berta I was dry...For the price they charge for each dish they should improve the quality of their meat and seafood.

We love the tea salad, fresh coconut juice (in the coconut), and coconut rice the best. Other favorites include the pumpkin pork stew and fiery tofu and vegetables (or string beans). We were seated in the front window, and apart from loud dining neighbors who were right next to us, we had a delightful visit. Our water glasses were never empty (to quench the fiery food!), and our waiter was very attentive.

This is the second time dining at this location.  Felt wlecomed at entering the restaurant, throughout the meal and acknowledged by reception and management when leaving.  Food and drinks were delicious - worth the special trip into town.
Very tasty food both vegetarian and non-. Fermented tea leaf salad is a highlight, of course, but there are others!
Delicious food, great service. We wish it were a bit less noisy. How about some attractive cloth hangings to soak up some of the acoustic energy?
The food is wonderful just great.  Would return there for sure.
Wonderful, warm setting. We could talk easily without shouting. The food was unique and delicious.

An after dinner play, Calligraphy at the Theater Works Center. Had 2 cast members and family members who had not been here! They loved the food! Manager adjusted reservations from 4 to 7. Which was nice for us.
Great service; however, the seating is too close and the loud noise doesn't help or create an environment to have a conversation.

Once again, a great meal at Rangoon Ruby in Palo Alto.  Very creative cuisine and excellent service.  Highly recommend the tea leaf salad, something you don't find every day anywhere else.  The calamari appetizer was also excellent and the basil chili beef was very good.  
We have been disappointed with the vegetarian samosas in the past so did not do them this time.  The service from Amy was terrific.  She made sure that the dishes came out when we wanted them and did not all come out at once which did happen a few months ago when we visited.  We will be back and we recommend you come too.
Usually, we have better service. Our waiter was slow to take our order, and then neglected to ask us the level of spiciness. One dish came out much too spicy.

Service and food were excellent. The only drawback was the noise, the restaurant is very loud.
Cocktails are great...a wonderful way to taste Burmese cuisine.
Extremely flavorful food, fun cocktails, and quick service if you need to make a movie or performance near University Ave/Stanford campus.  Definitely make a reservation.
Only negatives - very noisy and drinks were expensive.  Food was great!
Must try the tea leaf salad and country style lamb

I have heard of Rangoon Ruby, and finally tried the location in Palo Alto, and I must say that I was disappointed. I made reservations and specified that it was for a birthday, and yet when the check was returned with my credit card, it was handed to my guest and he was called by my name...so not a very astute observation, but by then it was super clear that what they wanted most was to flip the table.

The palata was heavy and dense, which was sorely disappointing. Please try Burma Cafe in Daly City to see how this dish should actually be done. Also disappointing was the pricing, in which the vegetarian was more expensive than the meat, which is pretentious at best. I ordered the eggplant and garlic for an entree, and with the speed that the dish was brought out, it was obvious that it was neither fresh nor well put together. The dish was overall bland, I had a couple of bites and took the remainder with me somewhat under duress. The leftovers were much better the next night as the flavors had time to meld. The initial serving was overly sweet with no depth, and drowning in sauce. My nephew had a beef dish that he was pleased with, but we still opted for moving on to the gelato spot on the corner for dessert. Dinner was OK, but the gelato was sublime. 

The restaurant states that it charges an extra 3% for ACA, and considering that there are four hopefully knock offs of Dale Chihululy chandeliers in the space, that also adds to the overall pretentiousness of the chain. If you could swing for the real thing, I would guess you wouldn't be pointing out that we also get to pay for you to be offering basic insurance for your staff. The acoustics were horrible, the tables stacked super close to each other, the service fair, and the food mediocre. Skip it and try someplace else.
One of our favorite restaurants in Palo Alto. Don't miss the eggplant and the coconut rice. Also pad thai with shrimp is delicious.
Great food and amazing service! Parking is a bit of a challenge due to the popular location.
Great food. Tables too close to each other! Very crammed!!
Wonderful evening meal.  We were visiting from out of town and found this restaurant via OpenTable.  It was a delight! Food was delicious, wait staff very attentive and nice atmosphere.
The rose for Valentine's Day was a nice touch

We've been here many times because we like the food. Staff is always friendly and appropriately attentive. This time the food was a bit off and lacked the usual wonderfulness (not adequately spiced, uneven cooking, etc.).  We'll visit again but be more careful to specify a greater degree of HOT in the curry.

Rangoon Ruby is consistently delicious, and I love to go here because there are plenty of vegetarian options and gluten free options. Also, a nice list of cocktails and beers.  They have had some staff turnovers in the past year, which is sad because I always appreciate it when staff remain for long periods because I assume that longevity means that they are treating their people well.  I hope their turnover doesn't mean that they are not good to their people.
Excellence

Never a miss. This is my go-to if I want to impress visiting friends. 
The owner happen to be at the PA location and he's such a joy to see.
Food is great, it was a busy night and our waitstaff came to our table, always apologetic for us waiting, which was not very long at all, but we appreciated how attentive she was and sensitive to the timing.

I just crave the marinated tea-leaf salad. 

The flavors are just amazing! 

We also had the calamari appetizer, but that was kind of plain. 

Wonderful curry with rice.

Had to send back the soup twice because it was lukewarm. Server asked if we wanted wine and immediately left. Had to wave down a server several times. Tables are so close together you could hear person next to you better than the one across from you. Food was bland
Great food, special dishes and amazing wine list. The service was immaculate. One of best restaurants in the area for sure!

For the Burmese Tea Leaf Salad this restaurant shines.  If the other two dishes I had ordered were all I ate I would not give this restaurant a positive review.  The fish with cumin and chili was covered with cumin, almost still in powdered form, and no taste at all other than uncooked cumin.  The Mixed Vegetables were completely ordinary. Mushy, bland, uninteresting.  I had hoped for good vegetables.  I will return for the Tea Leaf Salad again and again, but stay away from some of the other offerings.
Dirty plates, aluminum foil in noodles.

The Burmese tea leaf salad is wonderful. We also like the garlic noodles with duck. My son liked the pumpkin salmon, which I found a bit bland. We also had the calamari appetizer, good with tender calamari and jalapenos, and the fiery string beans and tofu was OK, nothing special.  The cocktails are expensive ($13) and interesting, but quite small for the price. Service was a little chaotic on a Friday night, which is always jammed. At one point they took our appetizer plates away, served our hot main dishes, and left us without plates until we flagged down a waiter. This is my second  dinner at Ruby's, and I like the interesting food but I think ultimately the prices are high for what you get, but that is almost always the case in Palo Alto.
The food and service was amazing (as always)!
Very tasty! Our server was very knowledgeable and we were seated promptly. It's a very busy but fun restaurant.
Always a great spot for Asian dining. The flat bread with the coconut chicken curry appetizer is one of our favorites. The chiligrean bean dish with the coconut rice is awesome.

We took some vegetarian friends out to Rangoon Ruby, and we had a great meal. The vegetarian options were delicious, so our friends were happy, and we had some delicious chicken know suey as well. The tea leaf salad, which was tossed at the table, was excellent. Service was prompt and friendly. We will definitely be back.

Went there as tripadvisor had categorized it as 'family friendly'. The restaurant is not great for toddlers and infants as the seating is cramped, noise levels are high and the staff (had not read our special request for a highchair) did not seem enthusiastic about having small children on a busy friday evening. Other than that food was good and portions, generous.

Not family friendly!!! They put my stroller outside, where it could have gotten stolen without asking me. When I had a difficult time getting through the aisle because this place is so narrow, the manager at the front just stood there and didn't offer to help whatsoever. Terrible service where people with kids are treated like a nuisance.  The food is nothing to write home about, and drinks taste like sugar. Yet another overrated overpriced Palo Alto restaurant that doesn't live up to the prices they charge.

Service only available upon request. 
No soup bowls for the soup, couldn't even get our server to come to hear our request for it. It was fun for the entire table to sip out of one common bowl that the soup was made in.
Excellent food and service. Hard to find parking nearby though.
They checked us in but didn't give us our OpenTable points

Great food, good service, our water glasses were refilled regularly. The only inconvenience is the lack of space. Rangoon Ruby's entryway is minuscule, so we stood at the bar while waiting the few minutes for our table. Even there, we were in the way of servers coming from kitchen to tables. Once seated, we had to remind table-mates not to gesture during conversation & suffered some near misses with full trays passing by.  But I guess the trade-off -- fewer tables = fewer spots -- means I can at least get a reservation at my preferred time.
Very good food.

Burmese food is a nice change to more traditional Chinese or Thai food. It is a cross between the two, with some Indian influence, and a flavor profile all of it's own. This is why we like to go here, for the food. The atmosphere is really too noisy to have a conversation, and the tables are packed in tightly making it impossible for intimate gatherings. Also, the waitstaff pushes people through quickly, and the kitchen will prepare all dishes within minutes of one another, so your salad and appetizers often arrive within like 3-5 minutes of the entree dishes, not allowing for proper pacing of the meal. In addition, they've started putting bottles of Voss water on the table, for which they will charge you $5 if you open them. We almost did this, before noticing the price sticker on the bottle, which was equivalent to a hotel mini-bar and tacky! Also their cocktails are super sweet, so we prefer to grab beer at one of the local pubs prior to coming here.

We get dinner here often enough to understand how the waitstaff is trained, and to much back with their pushiness. It's worth it for the food. Our favorite is the Tea Leaf Salad.

This is my first time having Burmese cuisine.  I liked it very much. We ordered the Tea Salad, Mango Salad, a chicken curry and a pork dish.  All were well done and I would recommend them. A minor gripe is that there really isn't much on the wine list for less than $60 a bottle.
Server was very polite. Food was generally good. Loved the tea salad! One thing wrong: my hot tea wasn't hot.

My mentee (college sophomore) was craving flavorful food after a quarter of dorm meals - so Burmese cuisine was an excellent antidote.  We started out with the samosas, which were relatively light and not as greasy as some I've had in other restaurants - so it was a good appetizer.  The must-order was the tea leaf salad (my barometer of Burmese eateries).  I would rate this one at 8 out of 10.  The ingredients were fresh and wholesome, but the tea leaf wasn't quite as savory as the tea leaf salad I've had at another Burmese restaurant.  My mentee had NAN GYI DOK (a dish of rice noodles with coconut chicken curry) - which she said was ok.  I didn't taste it, but the noodles looked a little overcooked.  I had the Rangoon Chicken with Lemongrass, which popped with umami flavor and paired beautifully with the jasmine rice.  My mentee mixed some of the chicken with her noodles and enjoyed it.

Ambiance-wise, it was very loud.  Good for people-watching (and listening to our conversations at adjacent tables).  The parking in downtown Palo Alto was a challenge, as usual for a Friday evening.  The decor was contemporary and well lit (not too bright, not too dim - I like to see the food I'm eating).  We were a little taken aback by the light fixtures hanging from the ceiling (they looked like masses of white snakes) - so that was the only minor detraction from the atmosphere.  

Overall, I would recommend this restaurant to a friend - just make sure to book a table in advance and allow ample time to find parking.

Second time there, and again a wonderful meal with great authentic Burmese cuisine.
The tea leaf salad was amazing as well as the lamb and chicken curries we had. Highly recommend checking this place out!
small portions, high price, not particularly interesting. Great wine list and great cocktails
One of my favorite spots in Palo Alto.  I would recommend this spot.

Food was decent and showcased a relatively uncommon regional cuisine  so I give it points for that. But the lunch proved more expensive than I expected. I think they should serve half servings of their salads at reduced prices so that a solo guest (which I was) can sample that and go for a lunch meal. As it was I paid as much for a salad as a lunch entree, and just the salad would not have been enough. Also, though I hate to sound snobbish  I've had better Burmese food in East Coast restaurants (NYC, Philadelphia).

Terrific food and fabulous service. We have been before and have loved it every time.  This time, we were late due to traffic and had theater tickets that compressed the time we had to eat dinner.  Our waiter made everything happen quickly and we got in and out in record time but never felt rushed.  It was my birthday and he even brought ice cream with a sparkler candle for me, unexpectedly fun!  We highly recommend Rangoon Ruby's.

The tables are too close together (12" apart!!!) and the staff insisted on seating everyone next to each other instead of spacing parties out when the restaurant opened and then filling in the tables in between as needed. The staff was so attentive to the point of being annoying. They cleared the plates so quickly that I still had a serving spoon in my hand when they took its dish away! I just laid it on the table, having no place to put it. If the environment wasn't already hectic enough, the manager had a contractor measuring the the built in benches against the wall during the dinner rush! That shows no respect for the customers! The food was okay but not good enough to justify a return trip.
Waiter was not up to par. A little tardy and a bit clumsy. Handed us our water glasses with water dripping down the sides. Motioned us to hand over our plates to him during table clean up.

Delicious Burmese food, excellent service and a lovely room, complete with chandeliers by Dale Chihuly.  The food was carefully crafted with fresh ingredients which produced complex flavors and a delicious meal.

The table where we were seated was along the main walkway into the restaurant. The space was a little tight so occasionally my chair would get bumped by people waking by, but it was manageable. The food was very fresh and flavorful. The service was friendly and attentive. I was pleasantly surprised when I was served a birthday dessert of a scoop of ice cream with a fireworks sort of candle in it.  Fun, unique and dramatic presentation!
Server was very attentive and kind.  Made good suggstions.  Food was OK - not outstanding, but fine.  good selection of wine.

We were a party of 4, and while each of us had eaten Burmese food, none of us considers him/herself a food expert.  We ordered family style, sharing chicken, pork,vegetable and seafood dishes, and paired the food with a very nice Riesling.  Desserts were excellent.  We all came away very satisfied with our meals and vowing to return.  I have a favorite Burmese restaurant in Burlingame (Mingalaba) which I prefer, but it is hard to get into because it doesn't take reservations.  RR is a very good substitute, although the prices are on the high side.

We were a group of 6 friends celebrating a birthday. Granted that our reservation was for 8:30pm, we did start late. However, we felt rushed and the food was served and cleared too fast for us to savor the meal. We left by about 10pm, which is not late by any standards, but the staff had already begun mopping the floors, putting away chairs and wrapping things up for the night! That said, the food was great but we all wished we had more time to enjoy it in a more relaxed setting.
Space is too cramped. They have filled maximum furniture to fill maximum humans. It's very difficult to move around or even go to the restroom without moving people sitting on other tables.
Very disappointed in the food and service. I have been to other Burmese restaurants in the Bay Area and the food does not compare at all. Poor texture and little flavor.
Tasty food, portions on the smaller side. Tables are very close to one another and it feels crowded.

Toned-down Burmese cuisine for newbies.  Far from the true pungent, dynamic cuisine that Burmese cuisine really is.  This is closer to Chinese food, really.  Adjust expectations for authenticity and you will be fine.  The atmosphere is very pleasant.

Service was uneven.  Had to flag people down to get help.  They also messed up a simple bill split into two, overcharging us x 150%-- an innocent mistake, but unacceptable nevertheless.
Great food! Attentive and polite servers. Noise level high so difficult to have meaningful conversations. Otherwise, fantastic experience. Would go again.

The food was cold. The hot tea was really cold and this was my second time going there because I had such a good experience the first time. The second visit was a disaster and I will not go back.

The quality has really dropped !!
During the dinner it was a good experience. Post service they billed us incorrectly and they have not been very helpful with the correction.

I always enjoy the tea leaf salad, and the chicken with lemongrass was delicious too.  However, the sooji dessert was a waste of money.  It was overpriced and didn't taste very good.  Even the accompanying mango ice cream did not have much flavor as mango ice cream usually does.
I really enjoyed the tea leaf salad, service was great, garlic noodles were great, the food overall was alright. I have had more flavorful Burmese food at other restaurants.

Dark room, needs more light and better ambiance
prices are expensive and portions are on the smaller size
tasty food and ok service

If you have never had the tea salad here, you have not lived. It is savory and exotic as well as healthy.  This latest visit , we had the walnut prawns. Wow.  Even tried the mango salad. It was very refreshing and light.  I wish the tables were a bit further apart because you can hear  the conversation at the next table, but other than that, this is the place for well prepared quality food.

Having dinner with a friend/business associate from southern Cal.  We were impressed with the variety of choices and interested in trying new dishes.  All were delicious.  
Driving down and parking was a pain.  The traffic was horrific. 
I would never go there without a reservation.  Great experience.

Not Vegetarian friendly - vegetarians can find chunks of meat in their food sometimes.

I overall liked the food. Tea Leaf Salad, String Beans and Tofu, Eggplant, and Black sticky rice for dessert. However one overwhelming disappointment spoiled the experience - I am a vegetarian, and there was a large piece of shrimp in the eggplant. I would have appreciated if the chef spoke to me and explained how it happened. I am pretty sure they mix cooking vessels, this will never happen if cooking vessels are separate for each dish. They did reverse the charge for that dish and gave a dessert, however what would really help is that the owners take the time to make sure this does not happen again, and to explain here on how this happened.
For some reason the table was not ready at time and we waited outside for 20 minutes.

Food was great ,  service was great .
We had the Tea salad and some sea food .
Will come back for sure .

The Palo Alto location of this offbeat Burmese cuisine purveyor creatively packs its clientele into a very small space. What we liked: our cocktails were creative and delicious.  The table service was excellent with tablecloths and cloth napkins arranged traditionally. Our server was mostly attentive and our orders were delivered as requested.  The food was good and it was definitely different. Our server and hosts made sure we knew our presence was appreciated.  What we didn't like so much: the iPad wine list was a mystery that we ignored. After ordering, our waiter left the large menus at our table.  In such a crowded space, they were difficult to arrange.  I ordered the pumpkin soup and what arrived was large pumpkin chunks in an oily, mildly seasoned red-orange bath, probably 1/3 of a cup of liquid altogether.  The flavor was alright.

Great tasting food with excellent service. There a variety on the menu that vegetarians are not forced to order the same-old-same-old. If there is one negative, the portions are a little small for the price, although the exception is their signature tea leaf salad. One order will easily satisfy 3 people, as a starter. It was a little loud, later in the evening.
Great option if you tired of the normal indian or thai fare

I have never had Burmese food and I must say everything we ordered was excellent! It reminded me a bit to Singapore or Malaysian food - so I thought I might like it. It surpassed my expectations by far!
Good service. Not very genuine Burmese food but well executed dishes overall.
Very good good, attentive service, only  a bit too noisy - still we will go there without hesitation.

I've been to two of Rangoon Ruby's restaurants and have been impressed by their cuisine. Well prepared, delicious entrees and desserts with an excellent service. Although the portions of food served are smaller. 
The noise level is high and tables are packed quite tightly. 
Would be better with less people and more space so one can enjoy the food more and be able to have good conversations with less noise.

This restaurant was one of the greatest. It is now sad shadow of itself.
The wonderful Tea Salad was a big disappointment.
The 3 great rices they had are now poor imitations (although I did not
have the coconut one this time).
The main entrees were not bad, one might have been called very good.
However, it is just not like it used to be.

Also notice the restaurant was not totally filled as in years ago (weekdays
as well as weekends).  So, I guess people are voting by not coming.
Although the sister restaurant on University Ave might have some bearing on this.

The prices are rather high but now the total value has dropped due to
the level of the food.  SAD SAD.
Great tasting food and beautiful presentation. They did get our order slightly wrong, but nothing big which detracted from the overall experience.
Great food and service.  Both the bartender and our waiter made sure everything was as we liked it.  Great variety of dishes.  The herbs and spices are very fresh tasting.

It's kind of OK, not my favorite. The tea salad is their big thing, and it's good, not great. However, if you're going to the Aquarius Theater to catch a movie, this is a great choice, since it's right across the street.
Very good food , service was friendly and timely on weeknight prime dinner hour.  Deafening noise level !  When the crowd thinned out it was a little quieter.
Food is too greasy/oily

Food was very unique. Wonderful flavor combinations and presentation.
Service was very good. However, the space became very crowded. Julianna could wiggle through the tiny space between tables. But our server had to pass some of our dishes over to us because we were blocked off when everyone was seated. None of the other table patrons were willing to move their chair in to make space. Loved the food but not sure I would go back. It was awkward walking to the restroom with all the tables so close together. At one point I couldnt hav e left my table because there was no way to get out.

Unfortunately, after some good meals here, I took some business colleagues for dinner. One hour and five minutes after we sat down at our reserved time, the waitress tried to clear the table. We told her we were still eating, and she said that they needed the table in ten minutes. I said there must be some mistake, thinking she would speak with the manager to figure it out. Ten minutes later, she came back, cleared the table, and gave us the check. I said that we hadn't ordered dessert, and she said they needed the table. We paid and I asked the hostess to speak with the manager; she shooed me outside. The manager came and told me that the hostesses and waitress were new. This treatment bothered me enough that I called the next day. The manager told me she would speak with the owner and get back to me. She never did. This is about the rudest experience I've ever had in a restaurant. Can't go back.
Awesome as always! We go there for the great food and service

Pro: Tasty burmese ethnic menu that is authentic to the country and at the same time very palatable to our taste.  Variety is rich and it is an adventure to select different items.  Disadvantage: busy, busy with seats close together and lots of noise.
Food was salty and  non tasteful.  Service was super slow.  Waitresses were absent minded and non attentive to customer requests even when restaurant was less than half full.  Very disappointed.
Enjoyed our vegetarian lunch. It was just a casual lunch with family. We will def. visit again.
Fantastic food! The only issue is that it's pretty loud as well as tight.

As always, a good meal!  We always order the Tea Leaf Salad, and it's always yummy.  We tried the Lemongrass Chicken, which was good too.  Nice flavors - a hint of lemon and basil with pea pods and red peppers, a little spicy.  Yum!  The service was a little too efficient.  They are eager to take away your plate as soon as you finish, and sometimes before.

We have been here many times. Food is good and portions are also good. Servers are attentive. Tables are packed together. Makes for loud close quarters. Tea leaf salad, walnut shrimp and Burmese fried rice are some favorites. Kind of pricey, but what isn't?
The salad recommendation was great.  Great food.

I'd never tried Burmese food, so eagerly booked at Rangoon. Glad we did. The food, in general, was good. I think we could have ordered more brilliantly, but what we did was fine, tasty, interesting. Only issue is that we sat next to a table with 8 kids and 3 adults. The adults sat together. The kids made a ruckus near us. It made it hard for us to settle in, enjoy, talk. Not sure how you could prevent such a fate yourself. It's why I probably would not return. The place is noisy, pretty much lacking in ambience. But the food, worth a try.
Chicken curry flatbread appetizer was amazing. Tea Leaf salad off the chart.

Had a relatively large group which they accommodate well.

Food is always outstanding.

The Teas Salad is a MUST!!!

We had walnut shrimp, chicken, fish and beef dishes at our table "family style" and all were great.
Amazing!  The food was delicious.
Watered down drinks and poorly cooked food of inferior quality ingredients.
Great as always! Food and service are simply amazing! Thanks!
Took my mom, grandmom, & cousin for dinner. They all loved it and even though they were under staffed I didn't feel I was not looked after.
Excellent menu at a very reasonable price. Loved the tea salad and the different chicken dishes. Service was impressively fast!
Great food and atmosphere!  Highly recommend!!
This was my second time but was a but disappointed by the food and the service.
"Green with envy" is one of the best cocktails I ever drank in my life
Food was exceptional and our server was friendly.

The wait staff will do a great job of talking up every dish on the menu, but don't be fooled: nothing is all that special and some things are downright inedible. Their signature Tea Leaf Salad was so salty that we couldn't finish it. This trend of overdoing the salt continued into the Garlic Noodles with Duck main dish. Altogether, we were unsatisfied with every single thing we ordered barring, of course, the Palata. Despite the glowing reviews, Rangoon Ruby is startlingly mediocre.

What's going on here? We waited half an hour for the food, it's good but not up to par. We weren't offered an explanation as to why our food was delayed so much and the restaurant wasn't near full! Disappointing...

The food was fantastic. The best was the tea leaf salad. The Garlic noodles were a little disappointing so skip that. Everything else was yummy! Service was not that great. In a two hour period we had three different servers so it got a little confusing about placing an order etc. Overall I highly recommend the place.

I brought my mom here for a Mother's Day dinner. Location was perfect as we just came out of the movie theater across the street.  Food was delicious, especially the tea leaf salad. Our waiter Constantine was very attentive and at the end of the meal, he presented us with a fragrant rose in recognition of Mother's day which was a very nice touch.
Got overcharged compared to the tip I gave. Really good food

We ate and left as soon as we could. The noise level was intolerable. We measured it at 90 decibels which is being right next to a loud rock band. This restaurant needs to seriously consider some sound-dampening technology - floor, ceilings, walls!
The tea leaf salad. It is good. Get it.

We have gone there often, but this time it felt like we were being hurried up. We just could not have a comfortable conversations without the waiter intruding on us and trying to get us to order all the food and trying to get us to leave. Not a good place if you want to meet friends & enjoy your food & conversation. Best to just eat very quickly and get out
I've been three times for business and it's been great each time.  Delicious food, pleasant staff, good upbeat ambiance.  Of course, the Tea Salad is a must!

Love the fun flavor combinations in Burmese food. Minted jalapeno pork was awesome.  Tea leaf salad was great.  The banana cocktail was good...very tropical.

We sat outside -- great to sit in fresh air and watch people walk by.

Good service!
Have loved this restaurant in the past but on a recent visit, the service was deplorable and the food only marginal.  I think opening up all over is diluting once great service and wonderful cuisine!
The food is well prepared and every dish is delicious.  You can't go wrong with anything on the menu.  Rangoon Ruby is one of our favorite restaurants and we keep coming back.
food was great... ok in terms of price, service was good even though the place was busy and packed
Awesome place... must go again and again!
Food was excellent -- wonderful flavors; just the right amount of spice.
Fantastic food and services, as always!!!
Good food.. Loved Ruby Rainbow salad n samosas.. 😊

Beyond irritated That after making a reservation two days in advance, we were given a table near the door which was exposed to cold air every time the door opened. And only by complaining were we switched to a warmer table. And we have dined there a dozen times and are frequent open table reservationists.

I had dinner here and ordered the sesame beef with a side of steamed Jasmine rice.  
The food was excellent as well as the service.  I wouldn't hesitate to return to this 
restaurant and can highly recommend it to others.  However, I think the rice and a 
salad or vegetable should have been included in the price.
Tables are too close to each other and we hear conversations from every which direction.  I wish it were a bit more spacious.

name: Los Gatos Parkside
description: Our mission is to share our passion for sustainably sourced ingredients. Los Gatos Parkside is all about freshness. Chef Noe Briseno and our team bring their passion for sustainably sourced ingredients to create an approachable menu showcasing the seasonal bounties of the Bay Area. We pride ourselves on using fresh, organic & locally sourced ingredients whenever possible.
address: 145 W Main St,  Los Gatos, CA 95030-6811

reviews.text: Both Lexi and Melanie were fabulous servers. They helped us all feel like home.
It is consistently always a good experience at Parkside. The food is excellent the service is wonderful and they’ve created a beautiful atmosphere.

We visited Parkside a couple of years ago when they opened and I didn’t feel they had enough interesting lunch vegetarian options for me. On Wednesday PM of this week, we went back with our son and thoroughly enjoyed the experience!  We started with the avocado toast (which was out of this world), and we loved that it was spicy. I ordered the vegetarian ravioli: delicious. Our son ordered the New York steak— he thoroughly enjoyed it coupled with  the tasty mashed potatoes. My husband remarked that he cannot wait to go back because he enjoyed his short ribs so much!  For us, the wine list pricing was high $$$. Our server was excellent and answered several questions to our satisfaction. The crème brûlée was the perfect finish to our meal. For diners sensitive to noise, I would suggest NOT sitting in the booth area next to the bar or in the bar area.

I’ve been here on numerous occasions and it’s always been really good unfortunately this time was a bit of a let down .
Rib appetiser’s were good although lukewarm- my wife and her freind had the Cauliflower and it was cold-
2 of us had the salmon entree and it was excellent although the jam preserve was a little much. Our other friend had steak frites and he enjoyed it . My wife had the pasta and it was rather bland and anaemic looking, and warm not hot.
We ordered a bottle of Sancerre only to have it bought to us with red wine glasses ? ( happened before)
I genuinely hope the service and quality isn’t slipping over time - the thing that worries is that it wasn’t even busy .
A great place for a girls' night and to celebrate a birthday. The outside with heaters is a perfect place to relax and the food and service was excellent. Will come back again!
The food was good. We were happy that we got an appetizer since the main course portion was on the smaller side.
Went for lunch and will definitely be back. Great menu. Good portion sizes. Wonderful service!
Service was very poor, changed, waitresses midstream, wrong drink was served, steak was served a medium well when it was ordered, medium rare￼
The food and drinks we excellent! Service was kind of slow and our server was not very attentive. We sat in the parklet patio and the ambience was lovely.

Disappointed this time.  I have been several times in last 2 mos and unfortunately tonight was disappointing.  Espresso martini glass had lipstick on it when it came to the table.  Water had bugs in it there when poured.  Sat on patio which the manager came to take drinks but as the night filled the patio our server spent most of the night helping her friends at the table near us with beers and a few shots.  Took an hour to take our food order after apps.  Dinner was good, husbands drink came out while the bar was “slammed” but wine took another 20 min to arrive after dinner was done .  Prior experience is what made me recommend and return so frequently but  really disappointed this time.  We still tipped but should have gone  💯 to the guys cleaning / clearing they were great.
Server was good but spilled a little bit of my drink
Great lunch—fried chicken sandwich and a chopped salad with chicken—delicious!

Great service and felt very welcome by the staff
Great venue for date or family gathering

This was our 2nd time we had brunch with friends at ParkSide. Both times the food was excellent. The 1st time the noise level was fine (we were early);  this time early aftrnn after a private event had left the noise level was acceptable.
Certainly we'll come back soon at early times &/or at week days.  Thanks ParkSide your service is always great!  Charly

I had a expresso martini which is literally a glass of baileys. When it’s served, I asked the waiter why it’s cream color, the waiter said “that’s the color of expresso martini”.
