Got to restaurant early and were seated immediately.  We had the lamb chops, coq au vin, linguini with shrimp.  We had to refrain from licking the plates. The food & service were excellent.  A diverse menu. I have already recommended La Fontaine to friends. I haven't stopped raving about it.

It took the server 10 minutes to greet us. Table was missing utensils and bread plate and we had to remind staff to get us these one at a time. Not all of the menus were given to the table and all guests.

We had a nice Mother’s Day lunch with my family. Restaurant was surprisingly empty when we first arrived but it started to fill out later. Squid appetizer was amazing as was the lava cake. My gnocchi was so so. Pretty pricey for the quality of food but service was excellent.

Excellent service, excellent food in a vibrant area.   Our server always had a smile on his face.  Staff cleared our plates efficiently and kept our water glasses filled without asking.  I enjoy coming here, especially on special occasions. Will be returning to enjoy another meal.
Always great food, great service.

Food was mostly good. but the flies and peeling paint in the restaurant was a turn off. 

The portions were small and the risotto was under cooked so we had to sent it back. The people were nice, but not attentive to us, even though we were 1 of 3 tables on a Sunday night. I had to ask the water to be refilled and they seemed to want to push us out by constantly asking if we are done with our food while we were talking. and eating 

$100 for 2 appetizer, salad, 1 entree, and a desert seems way too pricey for this place. Would not recommend and I would not go back again.
You absolutely can't go wrong at La Fontaine, it is our go to place before we head over to the MVPAC.
My sisters & I enjoyed our time w/you on the 27th of April. Attentiveness was excellent & service was great.

La Fontaine is a very nice place for Sunday brunch. It’s quieter than most restaurants in the neighborhood, an easy walk after the Mountain View Farmers Market and the Eggs Benedict are a perfect dish for brunch.

We came here before a Theatreworks show so arrived around 5:30 before the restaurant was busy.  The staff was very welcoming and well trained.  I had reserved a table outside, but it was a little chillier than expected so we sat inside.  We all had drinks, appetizers and a main course.  The food was good - based on our meals, I think your best bet here is to go with pasta.  I had chicken paillaird and it was a bit dry but the pasta dishes looked amazing.  The portion sizes are generous without being huge.  I feel like La Fontaine is a bit of a hidden gem along Castro Street and well worth checking out if you like Italian or French food.

Excellent business meal! The service by Judith was excellent and perfectly attentive. The meals were prepared correctly and were delicious. I recommend the Beef Wellington! Only downfall was the espresso machine was out of service.
Absolutely my favorite restaurant!  Great food! Great Service.  One tiny negative - its can get really noisy at times making it difficult to communicate.
From the staff, to the appetizer we had, the main dishes, to the outstanding dessert, everything was top notch!

Our meal and service (female server, Dani?) were exceptional, especially considering the size of our group (7 women).  Everything was served promptly and correctly -- even the silly "extras" that some of the guests asked for.  We'll be back!  Our one annoyance is the noise level.
One of the last quiet places to have dinner with my spouse on a busy Friday night!  Thank you!

The service and fare was spectacular!
I truly enjoyed my visit and will definitely eat here again when I am in the area!
I will be recommending La Fontaine to all!
Best Italian I’ve ever had, this place is such a treat. Best best best. Everything on the menu that I’ve tried, has been the best version of that dish, that I’ve ever had, anywhere.
La Fontaine is our favourite restaurant for special occasions. This visit was for my birthday.
First time there for a girl's night out and we were very happy with the food. Service was good but a bit slow but I think it was just Friday night!!
Nicest service ever. They were very attentive, but not pushy. I had an excellent lunch ever served by equally wonderful, pleasant people.

Just one little comment. In a restaurant with a French name, it would be nice to have a choice of a few more French wines. Luckily, there was a very decent Sancerre and that did the job. 
La Fontaine is quite fun and I plan to go back.
Delicious octopus, perfectly cooked. Inventive entree (fish bowl). But an Italian restaurant that has no cappuccino? How can that happen?

We had burrata, grilled octopus, carpaccio and the special, halibut. The halibut was falsely advertised as "pan-seared", when it was prepared regularly fried. It was ok, but not outstanding, and the vegetables and mashed potatoes that came with it were lukewarm - maybe they're been sitting on the plate, waiting for the fish to be cooked? The burrata and octopus got very high marks. Nicely presented and flavorful. The carpaccio was good; just the right amount of, thankfully small arugula, capers, and dash of dijon mustard. Our servers were attentive and prompt, the general atmosphere is cozy and not too loud.

Service was horrible, our dinner took 2.5 hours for entrees and dessert. We had to track down the server just to place our order. The meat entrees all ordered medium came out cold, extremely underdone and purple in the center and had to be sent back. The coffee we ordered never came and at that point we just wanted to leave. The food feels like frozen items that are heat and serve. Never again.

La Fontaine has 3 of the most interesting (and delicious!) salads that I've ever found in a restaurant.  So if you're trying to be good and eat salad, this place gives great choices.  But I have to admit, I find it difficult to pass up their Sole Almondine.  Buttery, with lemons and capers, perfectly cooked fish.  Just add a nice white wine and it's perfect!

Food was excellent, quite noisy when we first arrived, super packed as well. By the time we wrapped up our meal with affogato (not on the menu, but very well done by request) and port it was quiet and perfect for conversation.
Items are over priced given that food was average. Ambience also good noting extraordinary.

The worst experience I had recently. Waiting time for entre is too long, too crowded in the restaurant, we had to seat in the middle of restaurant and too close to others tables, also people comes and go all time around the table.
Love this place place. Great food, great people

Went for a nice brunch on a Sunday at 1:00, there were about 6 people there. We ordered 2 Bloody Marys, and 2 Eggs Benedict. They have several types of Benedicts to choose from, so we thought it was their specialty. The manager made the Bloody Marys, since there was no bartender. He had no clue what to do. They had tomato juice and lemon juice and a few olives, that tasted rank. We had to ask for hot sauce and vodka, which he charged extra for.  Then came the Benedicts. They are made with regular bacon, which was barely cooked and very floppy. They eggs were almost hard boiled, the hollandaise, was orange and had the consistency of velveeta (it was obviously from a jar), and the has brown were frozen pre formed patties that were soaked in oil (served without any seasoning). No server, only the manager and 2 cooks, so the service was poor. It was hands down the worst brunch I have ever had. It’s not a cheap restaurant, the bill was $70.00!

Ordered 4 plates with my Afghani girlfriend. I grew up with a Catalan grandfather and Sicilian grandmother, and have dabbled extensively in French cooking. 

The veal meatballs with polenta were so so. I can make better meatballs, as can my girlfriend in an Afghani style. The smattering of polenta was a bit of a joke. Nobody loses money by giving a healthy scoop of polenta.

The beet salad with arugula was very nice, but slightly underdressed. My partner added some of the balsamic and olive oil intended for our bread, but I refrained and tried to get hints from the citrus vinaigrette. Decent amount of goat cheese but I always want more.

My Grandma made Gnocchi. I make Gnocchi. These were no better, but plenty good. They were swimming in a bowl of cream sauce with mushrooms. I'm glad the sauce was light, and it thickened when I warmed my leftovers.

The Salmon Wellington was very nice. Bed of risotto was understated, but nicely cooked broccoli and cauliflower to accompany, and it was my partner's favorite. I wanted the puff pastry to act more puffy, especially since I was departing from my avoidance of wheat. But the dish satisfied flavorwise.

Hasi had never experienced Creme Brulee.  She noted that the top was like a layer ad ice. I enjoyed the infusion of Grand Marnier. Slam dunk. Espresso was tasty.

Attentive service. Even at 9 on a Sat night I expected more of a crowd, but was happy to be with my beautiful date in a comfortable space.

We drank little, but the Chianti by the glass at this date is a beauty.

Just made some polenta to repace what was missing, but otherwise you must check this place out. Trust frankmaestro and do it.

Great food, friendly service, nice presentation.
Clean and quiet restaurant.

Haven't been to this place since the last name change. Won't be back. the food is abysmal. greasy rubbery calamari, bread that i would not feed to the dogs - stale and looked like it was leftover from another table. seafood tastes like it was cooked and reheated over and over again. several shells "decorating" the plate were empty. I heard the server take a plate of shells from the next table saying " we need these for tomorrow". I thought he was joking... NOT. tomato sauce was flavorless. the place was packed. I have no idea why. it was BAD.

My reservation for 5 ballooned to a party of 10, and then to 12 w 4 children to celebrate a friends' birthday. 
Changes were handled smoothly and service was fantastic. They were total pros, taking the kids' orders immediately and serving them first, no fuss at all about half orders for them, making napkin creatures amusing the kids, even helping one cut up his lamb chops. Our wines by the glass were excellent, Starter salads were fresh, bread w oil tasty, escargot was good as well.
One friend felt her braised short ribs were not flavorful enough, but the rest of us really enjoyed our dinners. Orechiette w bacon and peas, pistachio crusted lamb chops, prawn linguine, and a seafood dish w mussels were quickly polished off completely. 
They presented a lovely tiramisu w candle for our birthday Doc and were overall patient and friendly all around.
Definitely worth coming back for more.
It was our first time & this place did not disappoint. The food was good & the staff was super friendly.
Christmas Eve dinner

Beef Wellington was the best we've ever had.  So tender and incredible.  Worth the money.  How come I can't cook a steak that well?  If you don't like truffles, do not fear the truffle mashed potatoes.  Just a hint of truffle flavor and wonderful.

Service was outstanding. We will go back again and again!

Truly a great little-hole in the wall as it feels like. 
But it is one of those holes, catering to fancy taste. 
French and Italian dishes are just delightful.
Poulet Aux Champignon was so well crafted; chicken is tender and juicy with the most creamiest sauce!
Such a lovely place.

We had a lovely dinner at La Fontaine.  The wine list is excellent, the food was fabulous, and the service was excellent.  It's very popular so was noisy and somewhat difficult to hear my companion.  The lighting in the evening is also quite bright; the atmosphere would be much better with dimmer lighting.  I'll definitely return but more likely for lunch than dinner.
Decent experience. Expected a mellow vibe instead the place was loud and more lit up than we expected. Middle of our dinner, we smelt something bad (guess from restroom). Bad experience..

Went to LaFontaine before the theater with the kids. I was nervous because they don't have a kids' menu.  But the staff was GREAT with the kids. Our server did napkin tricks that made the kids laugh and feel welcome. And the kids could choose any of the pasta dishes and get a "kids sized" version for a kids' sized price.  I love it that the kids could choose whatever they wanted off the pasta menu and so weren't stuck with the 3 or 4 typical "kids menu" types of dishes that most restaurants offer kids.
I myself had the rack of lamb and it was excellent.  Cooked perfectly and nicely seasoned.  Overall, very impressed.  We'll be back again without the kids!  But how nice to know that kids are welcome too!
The food is good, but not exceptional. The service is very good.
Very tasty food from the appetizers to the desserts, with great entrees, one of my favorite places

The waiter got my order wrong, but fixed it without fuss and gave us a dessert to make up for it, and that helped. I got a message from OpenTable that I never showed up for my reservation, but I did. I don’t know for sure if that was the fault of the restaurant or OpenTable. It was sorted out after I reported that I did indeed check in for my reservation.
  The food is simply prepared and tasty. There is a nice pan European vibe. It was busy, but not too loud.
We were a group of 6, including 3 year old twins. The staff was very friendly and accommodating.
Great food. Repeat customer. Delicious. Underated.

Tried this restaurant and was very satisfied . Can see how it was awarded best restaurant or something in local paper. Service was quick and to the point. Would definitely go back again . Had the branzino very good , the skin was crispy and the meat was moist , perfect.
The food was amazing as always. The service not so much.
I've been here a lot, and every other time has been great, though this time was only "good" b/c my steak was overcooked :(  Oh well, it happens, usually it is perfect, this time it wasn't.

I had a relative bad night with my guest, but as he walked out on my birthday dinner and left me to my tears the staff pitched in to help me in my sorrows including hugs from my waitress! I shall never forget this evening spent with total strangers :) God bless you guys! XOXO

We have eaten here before and enjoyed it. Unfortunately the service this time was extremely poor. One or two servers for the entire dining room. The door host was also not great. No smile or welcome. It’s too bad because the food is good.

There were four of us celebrating birthdays.  Our reservation was 5:15 on a Saturday evening, so it was quiet which is how we like it.  The restaurant gradually filled and had the typical din of most places by the time we left after 7:00.  However, that included  an enjoyable jazz trio at 6:30.  The service was attentive and not overbearing.  The dishes were attractive and delicious, though most were similar to those in many Italian restaurants.  I had the lamb chops which were creatively and perfectly prepared.  There were two orders of shrimp with pasta which did not disappoint.  Next time I want lamb, I will head back to La Fontaine.
Great service, food was incredible... highly recommend this spot!

Had a very nice dinner at La Fontaine before theater.  Since it was the first time for us, we stuck to their recommendations and had the Seafood Pappardelle and the Beef Wellington.  Both were lovely, and the pasta was really, really good.
Excellent food.  Very good menu.  Reasonable prices.  Friendly and accommodating staff

Our food was very good but service needs some work. Perhaps they were short-staffed? The persons that brought the water & cleared dishes also brought out the food and they had no idea who ordered what. Correcting service mistakes would allow things to run much smoother. The manager (owner?) was very helpful and also took our order. Of course he was overly busy. The only real downside was being seated next to a large group that was ridiculously loud. Make it difficult to carry on a conversation at our table:( Bottom line, we will give La Fontaine another try.

Small, narrow restaurant that when filled becomes extremely noisy. Excellent crab cake appetizer. My veal saltimbocca was very good, as was the accompanying fresh vegetables and mashed potatoes. However, some in my party felt the food was overdone. Portions are ample. Nice presentations. Service is excellent. Kudos to the Maitre’d, Duman!
Their crab cakes with caper aioli are amazing! I also like the beet salad.

Great food. Friendly staff and great service. 
There were 6 of us and we all ordered different dishes. We all loved and enjoyed our dishes.

Food is good every day Italian fare. Nothing spectacular, no strong flavors, but still decent, and good range of choices. I’ll probably go back again in the future, but wouldn’t say you *have* try this place. Food was hot, and service was very good (and speedy).
Not bad at all. It was during the annual Mt.View street festival so it was more crowded then usual, but fun friendly atmosphere.

We enjoyed our meal very much but we were close to the musicians and the music was quite loud, making conversation difficult.  The musicians did a great job - so you just have to be prepared to listen rather than talk, especially at the tables in the front.
I found this restaurant while looking for a place for dinner before going to Theatreworks with my daughters. We all absolutely loved our meals - delicious!
One of my favorite restaurants.  i LOVE their beef wellington, and always get an affogato for dessert! Highly recommended.

Our party of 8 was seated promptly at a specially-arranged table in advance of our theater preformance.  Our waiter, maybe owner/manager, was delightful with a good sense of humor.  Most of us ordered the braised short rib, and we unanimous in our praise.  Wish we could make 'em like this at home.  I'd recommend this to anyone - a great mix between French and Italian.  Thanks for a delightful evening!!
Food was outstanding and the service even better.
I was really disappointed in the Salmon Wellington.   I was expecting a lot more.

The service was slow. Waited over 40 minutes to receive food. The food tasted ok, not worth the money. The food was prepared with too much pepper as if they added the seasoning to quickly add flavor and get the dishes out. Will not return

I was visiting my brother, who's been wanting to try this restaurant, so we used this opportunity to go out as a special occasion. I enjoyed the taste of my dish (the mushroom truffle ravioli) but it was lukewarm. My two dining companions both disliked their dishes, one is severely lactose intolerant and so ordered the only dish that automatically came without cheese, and found it much to spicy. The other ordered a shrimp and prawn dish, and also complained that it was near-cold.

We had a wonderful family (6)  dinner early (5:00) Friday.  We were the first patrons arriving at 5 and were seated at the nice front window table.  Food and service was excellent and left with full tummies.  I forgot my leftover dinner in the restaurant.  😮🤤.  This was our first time here.

I was so pleased with coming to this location for a special dinner date with my husband! They seated us promptly and never had to worry about getting a waiter's attention all night! Granted, it was a Tuesday night and not all that busy, but it's always nice to be looked after.

We ordered the Burrata and Prosciutto appetizer, which was on the Specials menu to start and it was divine. The heirloom tomatoes were perfectly ripe, the burrata was creamy and smooth, and the prosciutto (not sure if it was truly authentic prosciutto di parma, but who cares) was salty and complimented everything perfectly. If I could make one adjustment, I'd add maybe a little more prosciutto to balance how much burrata there was. It went well with the complimentary focaccia and olive oil/balsamic dip.

For dinner, I got the Alaskan Halibut and my husband got the beef wellington. I don't say this lightly when I say this is one of the better beef wellingtons we've ever had. The gravy it came with was the perfect compliment to the buttery puff pastry and the perfectly seared and tender beef. It also tasted great over the truffle mashed potatoes (to be honest, I didn't taste much truffle but that wasn't my priority when tasting this dish) and the various vegetables that it came with. The gravy even made the Brussels sprouts taste good, and I'm not a huge brussels sprouts fan.

As for my Halibut, it was delicious! Again, the sauce was a great compliment to everything on the plate: the parsnip mash (which tasted more like potatoes to me, but I didn't really care), the asparagus wrapped in more prosciutto (these were great since the asparagus was grilled and then baked with the prosciutto!), and of course, the perfectly seared halibut.

For the price, it was an upscale dining experience that didn't break the bank. I'm very pleased with La Fontaine and will probably be back in the future!

My wife and I enjoyed the best of Italy and France: Cavatelli Meatballs for her, and Steak Frites for me. Both were excellent and the portions generous. We topped off our experience with Panna Cotta and Tiramisu. They were yummy, but I’ve got my eye on the Lava Cake for next time! Plus the service was superb. The Birthday Girl was very happy.
This is my absolute favorite restaurant in the south bay! The service and food are always fantastic.
I never knew this restaurant existed until a friend recommended we go there.  Now it's my new favorite restaurant.  The food, service, and ambiance was delightful; what a find.

My wife and I had dinner at La Fontaine for a periodic "date night" meal.   We selected the restaurant based on the menu on line, and we were not disappointed.    We began with the Crab Cakes, served with arugula and delicious sauce.  We asked to split a salad, and the kitchen staff did the split and presented us with two plates.  The salads were dressed with a delightful light house made dressing.   She had the Risotto with sausage from the specials menu, and I had the pasta with chicken breast.  Both were delicious and beautifully presented.   We again opted to split dessert.  Again, the kitchen did the split for us and served us two separate cups with chocolate gelato.   We each had a glass of the Malbec, which was a good wine choice for both entrees.    Service was attentive but not overbearing.   The window table was delightful.   I highly recommend this restaurant for special occasion dining.

Love the tasty food here. Some of our favorites include the chicken avocado sandwich and salmon sandwich. It comes with generous portions of thin, crispy french fries and a wonderful house salad with tomatoes, olives, grated Parmesan cheese and slices of red onion.   We just love this place and it's very classy with reasonable prices and excellent service.
The food, the waiter, the maitre d' were all amazing. I don't know how we missed this gem for the last 6 years!

Good restaurant, good food - but just good, not awesome. We've paid about $150 with tips for 2 adults and for this place it didn't worth it. Might be OK for just one occasional visit, but there's nothing special, won't go back.
Food was delicious. Favorite dish is the chicken and avocado sandwich. It comes with house salad and thin crispy fries. Also the salmon sandwich was outstanding. Love the ambiance.
Love this place. Always great food and service!  Our favorite restaurant wether it’s just the two of us or with a group.
Reasonable place for downtown Mountain View re menu, ambience, noise level, etc., for a business meal.

The crab cakes were outstanding . . . beautifully crispy and totally flavorful, with a lovely sauce. I will go back just for the crab cakes.  The special salmon Wellington was underwhelming.  The puff pastry just wasn't puffy!
Terrible service. Food nothing special. Will not return to this place.
Love there beef wellington n affogato for dessert

Visiting from out of town looking for an early dinner. We could not have been happier stumbling by accident upon this small bistro. We sat outside in the shade, great for people watching but not the quietest space.  The food and service were outstanding, especially for the price point.  The meal was not cheap, but we have paid two times as much for inferior food and service.  Going back tonight (2 days later).  The ginger carrot soup was as good as any we have had.  The goat cheese appetizer was superb!  The octopus was cooked and seasoned perfectly, not the easiest to pull off well!  Service was attentive, but not hovering, and the waitstaff was knowledgeable.
We frequent La Fontaine and have brought many friends. This visit was particularly outstanding in every way. Everyone loved their appetizers and mains, especially rack of lamb

Tried this place for the first time. Liked the overall experience.. not too fancy nor too casual. Food was average, menu selection was limited for my taste. The chocolate lava cake is a must try! Will go again for an evening out.

I had the duck and my friend had the lobster ravioli, and we were both very pleased with our tasty dishes.  The desert was a chocolate lava cake which was superb.. the bread pudding which had been our first choice was already sold out as the daily special.. 
I recently had 2 unsavory experiences with San Francisco restaurants and am pleasantly happy that this dinner at La Fontaine was perfect!  Fabulous food, lovely outdoor seating, and amazingly skilled food servers.  I am having better luck with restaurants in my own back yard, like this one.

The service here is terrible.  The server was more interested in completing his conversations with a friend at the bar, ignoring our hand waves - or racing across the room, staring straight ahead and avoiding eye contact.   The food was good, but overpriced.  I ordered the Salmon Wellington, since this is a bit complicated to make at home (I assumed that like Boeuf Wellington, the salmon would be "en croute" - wrapped in a crust.)  To my surprise, the only "crust" was a token piece of dough along the side (I suppose this was a "witty allusion" to the actual recipe.)  When I queried the server as to a mistake in the order, I was told "this is the way the chef does it".  Finally, the interior is somewhat "industrial" - NOT the place for a romantic date.
The food was superb and the waiter attentive and fun to chat with. Very noisy on a busy Friday night!
Nice restaurant in a very lively part of town. Reasonable pricing, sizable portion, attentive service.

This place was fantastic! The staff were all very helpful, attentive, and knowledgeable, but not so chatty that it interrupted our date night. The food was authentic and clearly prepared fresh, after we ordered. 

As a native of the East Coast, I've been very disappointed with everything that calls itself Italian food out here so far. La Fontaine restored my faith in the Valley's cuisine!

It was great to see the same staff that gave so many wonderful nights, during our visit to MV after our move to Texas.
I was like being at home.
Went to La Fontaine for brunch for the first time.  The food and service was great! Highly recommend.
Our foursome enjoyed every dish. A little loud there, but food and service were great.

Food was fantastic.
Every dish that we ordered came out pretty well.
The service was excellent and the food was even better.  There was good variety.  The desserts were delicious.

Mother’s Day dinner. Food was ok, over priced. Husband ordered lamb shank with polenta. Polenta was very very bland no taste at all.  I had Rib-eye steak with fries and mushrooms sauce.  Steak could use more mushrooms sauce.  Overall it was just ok, nothing to brag about.

This was our first visit. We were made very welcome. Our server was informative and cheerful. Also he was not daunted by our garlic allergy - a definite PLUS! We regret that we did not discover his name. The salads were really fresh and the pastas innovative and tasty.
Nice people. Why does this message have to be fifty characters long?
The service was very good and the starters were great too. We ate of the menu of the day and the short rib risotto was great. The wine list was nice as well.

When you are handed a menu of the day, that has oil stains on it, its not good.  When you mention to the waitress that you would get rid of such a thing, and they ask you why?  You know you are in a place that doesnt really understand.  Service was ok, but we had three different meals, and they were all mediocre.  Beef Wellington, snapper, and one other.  None were horrible; none were good enough for me to go back.  Sorry, but this place just didnt impress me.  Tiramisu was good.

Food was amazing. Tried ravioli, La caprese and tagliolini cabrese. Appropriate portion size at the right temperature. I love the staff. So friendly and very attentive.
Must try place. Would love to see more vegetarian options.
One of my favorites. Beef Wellington is outstanding
My shell fish tasted terrible.
The beet salad was good, but the seafood pappardelle was very good, with a decent amount of seafood.
The food is excellent!; especially the fish which is what I had. The Lava cake desert is a delight!!!
One of our favorite places! The staff is friendly and is knowledgeable and makes great recommendations .
La Fontaine was lovely. The burrata and lava cake were delicious!
Great food and service!
Love the chicken sandwich here that comes with a house salad and thin-cut fries.
One criticism is that the vegetables were almost cold.  Barely warm.
I'm a huge fan of their steak.  The goat cheese appetizer is also delicious.

My friend and I have been coming here for the beef wellington dish for over a year now, it has become Our Place when life has been stressful and we need a break. The staff are always exceptionally kind and attentive. 

The food...the FOOD! The beef wellington is always cooked to perfection and, more often than not, my friend and I finish every morsel on our plates. The pre-meal focaccia is delicious as well. We also have never ordered a dessert here that we did not love. 

Just an amazing establishment overall!

I was surprised that this restaurant received a four star rating. To me, it was overrated. We started with a calamari appetizer, but it was hard and over fried. At $12, we thought it should be better. When we noted the poor preparation to the waiter, instead of offering an apology or remedy, he said "Really? Everybody usually likes it."  To be fair, the entrées were good, but not worth the price (lunch for 2, no drinks, 1 appetizer, $75 with tip). Later, a friend told me this isn't really an Italian- or French-run restaurant, but one run by Turkish people. I have no problem with any nationality, but I prefer to support more "authentic" restaurants. I'm sticking with Aldo's in Los Altos for Italian and Left Bank in Menlo Park for French.

The service and ambiance was  very nice. There was low key live music too. However, the food itself was overpriced. The meat was cooked correctly but the sauces were very disappointing. So too was the wine recommended and the bread/dip.

Valentines special menu was very nice and the free gift a nice touch. Food was good although steak was warm not hot. Felt a bit rushed but understand why. Have been here on other occasions and it’s consistently good.

We celebrated Valentine's Day at La Fontaine. The special menu for the day had many excellent choices. The service was attentive and included a gift of a small wooden box of chocolate kisses. We greatly enjoyed our meal.

Came here to celebrate a special occasion with my wife.  Waiter put in the wrong order for duck breast so I got my dish while my wife waited an extra 20 minutes for hers. I felt really bad eating without her but she didn't want my pasta to get cold. In essence we each ate alone while watching the other eat. Decent food but terrible experience.  I really wanted to like this restaurant on Castro.

Food was pretty tasty but took exceedingly long to come out of the kitchen (even the wait staff acknowledged that and apologized).  Both of us got a pasta dish and they were decent but not spectacular.  Overall, a little bit pricey for what we got and how long it took us to get it.

All our selections were very well prepared and delicious.  The spinach, strawberry & mango salad was fresh and tasty.  Fruit was perfect degree of ripeness.  Vinaigrette carefully balanced.  The Fried Calamari Starter was lightly but fully dipped in a tasty batter and fried to where they weren't greasy and they stayed hot a good length of time.  It is served with both tartar sauce and a spicy chili type sauce.   Next time we'll remember to ask for two sides of tartar and skip the heat.  Our entrees were both very pleasing:  Linguini with prawns: 4 or 5 hearty sized prawns very well prepared, which means they managed to keep the prawns very lightly cooked so they remained succulent.;  Breast of duck: a generous serving with a very tasty cranberry+ other fruit sauce, not too fruity nor too saucy.  The duck itself extremely tender and tasty, cooked on the rare side but definitely safely cooked.  Five plump little medallions of the duck, served over wild rice.  We will definitely return to this active restaurant, but first we'll find out the better times to come to hopefully avoid tables of 6 and 10 business women and men, which kept the noise level more "energetic" than we care for.  Prefer not to have to shout across a small table in order to talk to our dinner partner!  Service prompt, alert but non-intrusive.
Absolutely delicious! Can't wait to go back again!
Four of us had tickets to Theatre Works and had a difficult time deciding among the many different entrees.  Wine choices were great.  We certainly will be back to try something new.

We’ve only visited a few times but each time the food, drinks and service were great. The staff are considerate and attentive but also genuine. Quaint and comfortable atmosphere, we’ll be going back soon.
Good food. I had the pistachio coated halibut which was quite good. My wife has a pasta but was disappointed in that she thought it had way too much sauce. Service and ambience were fine.
The special lamb shank is fall out of the bone,  cooked to perfection.
The food was a bit pricey given it's quality.  Small restaurant with a bar.  A bit noisy.  My friends and I had to lean in to be heard in our own discussion.

Had a good meal for our Anniversary. Staff seemed shorthanded on a Monday as there was a big party. got a little loud but not too bad. Food was excellent and service attentive despite the bigger party.The beef ribs were particularly good as was the puff pastry covered in chocolate for dessert.
Ate here prior to a theatre date - service was fairly quickly & the FOOD WAS EXCELLENT!  I love staff - very giving and sociable .
Always a pleasure to eat here. Crusted Goat appetizer is always good.  Lots of variety on the menu to choose from.

We've been to La Fontaine many times, and were very happy to be recognized by staff, especially since we haven't been there in some months. We were less happy with the quality of our meals this time; we brought 4 friends with us, and no-one was particularly impressed with their food. We've super loved it in the past. Half the table ordered the Salmon Wellington, and somehow it didn't please so well. One person ordered chicken paillared, which was dry.
The beef wellington was delicious, as was the clam chowder. The portions are a bit small and the prices are a bit high, but it was definitely worth it for the meal that I had.
Very nice!  Sat in the front in the window.  Not too loud, service was great & a nice selection of food.  We’ll be back!

We had a family get-together (grandparents to grandchildren) for a Sunday brunch at the restaurant.  Wonderful, top-notch service.  Our table ordered everything from Belgian Waffles, French Toast to Omelettes, Pasta, and sandwiches.  The food was awesome for all except the waffles.   It was harder than normal and a bit stale tasting.  The desserts were off too -- tiramisu was old and stale, creme brulee had an after taste.  Everyone else loved their omelettes, pasta, and sandwiches -- these are all highly recommended.  Drinks were also very good.  The server even went out of her  way to make sure we got our coffees, lattes, teas, and specialty drinks.

Took my staff for a holiday lunch.  Our table wasnt ready & we waited 1/2 hour.  Once served everything was delicious.  Unfortunately the kitchen closed before we were finished, so no dessert was available. Coffee only.   Big short coming.  We missed out.

We started with the crab cakes, which were fantastic. Split the Caesar salad which was topped with anchovy filets... if you like ancovhies then you’d love this salad. Then for our main course we ordered the beef Wellington and the special, pistachio crusted halibut. 

Both out of this world! The beef Wellington was incredibly rich and melted in your mouth... and the halibut was perfect. All of the extras paired well together and the Sauvignon Blanc sauce was on point. 

Ended the night with a nice espresso and the lava cake... great way to end a great dinner. 

Also, our waitress was amazing!
Food was AMAZING! I'm so glad the server was able to split my dinner with my date, even giving us our own plates.

We were given 2 different special menus. One was old and from the previous day. Our appetizer was served after our soup and salads. They forgot to acknowledge the birthday we were celebrating even though I put it in the reservation. The food was just okay.

Food was good but sitting next to bar was a nuisance. They have this tiny and noisy  door on bar which is used by staff every 30 seconds. We were sitting next to it  and it spoiled whole experience.  We could get view of overflowing trash can whenever door was opened.
Good food, good sevice, would come again. Thank you La Fontaine! I’ll recommend this place to my friends, without a doubt.
Dishes were a disappointment. Did not resemble the pics shown on website.  VERYexpensive for mediocre dishes.

Service was generally poor. Our waiter seemingly looked over at us and our empty plates then failed to stop by even though he wasn't attending to any other tables at the time. The only one who paid any attention to our table was the very polite person who kept our water glasses filled and cleared our plates.

The portions were good for us which means they would be much too small for anyone else as we usually take home leftovers from any other restaurant.

The saving grace was the food was well prepared and very tasty.

Noise. Packed. Great food. Good service. Limited but good wine list. Cocktails were short on alcohol. Not a place to linger due to noise and how tightly it’s packed. Popularity speaks to the good food it has, but once again...noisy and tight. 

Especially when the music starts playing... time to leave.

It was our first time at La Fontaine -- we have wanted to try it. We had a great time.  We were celebrating my Aunt's birthday and we all enjoyed the food, the energetic dining room, and the service - Nick was fantastic and did a great job taking care of everything.

This was our second visit to La Fontaine.  Although the menu had changed, once again every dish was outstanding.  Service was excellent.  It was crowded and lively, so the noise level was fairly high.
Prices are on the high end, but the delicious meal was worth it.  Two of us had the pistachio-crusted lamb chops (heavenly) with wonderful roasted potatoes and somewhat overdone mixed vegetables (the choice of vegetables was perfect, and their being overcooked was the only negative for the experience).  My sister had the halibut special, which she said was delectable. My husband had the capellini, which he loved.  I had the eggplant gratin (divine) and two of us had the caesar salad, which they deemed excellent.  The basil lemon drop and blackberry mojito were unusual and lovely.   We were all too stuffed for dessert!  I can't wait to return.
It's a really out standing experience in the restaurant. Food was delicious. It was my girl girlfriend's birthday, she was happy there.

La Fontaine was OK, but too expensive given the quality and quantity of food served. I expected excellence (given the price tag and the reviews) but it was just OK. Actually a little meh. I won't go back.
Waiter service was good, but we had to wait close to 1 hour past our reservation time to get a table. A glitch in the reservation system we were told.

Staff was extremely patient with us.  We stayed a long time chatting.  
Lunch menu was good.  Lots of variety.  We all enjoyed our food.
I would go back, esp. with a group.
We've been here twice now and the food is consistently good.  The service is outstanding.  The wait staff is friendly and engaging.
Great Food and wait staff, will go back the next time in town.

Service was attentive without being obtrusive throughout.  We shared appetizer, salad, pasta, and main course and they made the effort to divide the dishes where feasible (salad and pasta) and provide sharing plates otherwise.  This was a nice complement to the food.  The burrata and tomato appetizer was very good but had perhaps twice the balsamic vinegar it needed.  The Caesar salad had particularly strong anchovy fillets (I do prefer the anchovies integrated but understand that many people don't care for anchovies even though they are essential to Caesar salad), very crisp lettuce, and properly prepared croutons.  Again maybe a little more dressing than was needed.  The mushroom ravioli pasta course was spectacular -- with 6 large raviolis it was a lot even when shared as a pasta course.  The beef Wellington was one of the most tender pieces of meat I've ever encountered, properly medium rare throughout.  However, the crust was a bit soggy rather than flaky -- really the only significant disappointment of the meal.

The food was ok. I thought the special sole was bland. The waiter was very good and brought me melon and prousutto which was ok. Melon was not done enough. But they tried. I wouldn't return as there are too many other restaurants to try!
VERY disappointed in the lack of service. It was as if our waiter forgot about us.  Our food was cold when we finally got it, and it was definitely NOT worth the money or our time to dine there.
Service was slow but the food wasn't bad.  Took quite a while to place my order but the seafood pasta wasn't bad but the clams were really small.  The restaurant was extremely noisy.
Nick the bartender is great! Food is solid across the board

The restaurant was clean and everything, but my steak had an odd flavor. Do not get me wrong, I'm almost positive that I'm just not used to the spices in the food. Other than that everything else was delicious.
The food is not hot, not even warm. The bread is cold, the seafood is also cold.

Great menu options - plenty of pasta combinations, fish and seafood, and fun cocktails. I found the gnocci a bit bland, but the ravioli and focaccia with balsamic dipping sauce were awesome. Loved the basil lemon drops!
Very noisy inside, but we moved out to the sidewalk tables and had a great time.  The octopus appetizer was the best.
Too noisy could'nt hear myself speak.   Never go again.

Every time I bring anyone to this place it is always excellent. This reservation I asked for a quiet table. They noticed this request and went the extra effort to call me. It turned out they had an entertainer playing so he made a note to give us a table away from the music. Nice.
We wanted a new culinary experience in Mountain View before the play at the Performing Arts Center with Theatreworks.  This was a find!

We visit La Fontaine frequently and it never disappoints, good food and wine in a nice setting. I recommend the octopus appetizer, tasty and tender. The meat balls, both appetizer and entree, are fabulous!!

My wife was craving some Beef Wellington.  I searched for restaurants in the South Bay that served it, this one came up with some great reviews.

La Fontaine's version of Beef Wellington is a bit non-traditional.  Instead of the beef being completely encased in a nice fluffy pastry, it is "wrapped" in some type of pastry, leaving both the top and bottom of the meat exposed.    I can speak to the flavor of the dish being excellent.   The beef (prime filet mignon) was superb, a perfect medium-rare.  Was served with portabella mushrooms on top which were very succulent and earthy. The puff pastry... Was soggy.    

Really, we came for what we thought would be a traditional beef wellington... ended up with something that tasted pretty damned good, but was not what we were looking for.

Eric and Hassan make the dining experience wonderful. Excellent presentation and great service. The service staff are friendly and inviting. Nick mixes the cocktails and offers suggestions. 
Be here many times and will continue because of the people and food!
It wasn't too busy when we arrived. Salads we decent and our main course (both had different ravioli entrees) was delicious! Service was great.
Great food, large portions are a very reasonable price.

The food and service was Excellent!!!
Specially that beef wellington, the meat was very juicy.

My wife and I had dinner here.   After splitting a very good salad, we each had an entrée.  
I ordered the steak frites (a rib-eye steak with shoe string potatoes), while my wife ordered
the duck breast served on a bed of wild rice  and asparagus.  Her duck breast was fine.

Unfortunately, my steak frites was a major disappointment.   First, it was much smaller
and thinner than at any of the number of times I had it in the past.   Second, it didn't have
that wonderful taste that it had previously.   Third, the potatoes were short - not long and
slender shoe string potatoes, as they were in the past.  Fourth, I received a very small portion
 of ordinary, small French fried potatoes.  Fifth, because the price of the steak frites went from $15 to $33 over the five or so years I've been dining at La Fontaine, I found my entrée to be a very poor value and will never order it again.
Great food and outstanding service--prompt, attentive, courteous.   A great place to gather before the theater.
Very creative list of menu items, prepared well.  We really enjoyed the meal here.
We had a very nice dinner among friends, we will definitely return.

Service was pretty slow where food and drinks came out at different times for different people.  Drinks didn't taste good and had to be sent back.  Portions of the food was cold for a few people.  For example, the meat would be hot, but the vegetable and potato was cold.  This was an expensive meal and wasn't worth it.

Food was fantastic - vegetarian friendly.  Started with the caprese and the strawberry-mango spinach salad - very fresh.   Thoroughly enjoyed the mushroom truffle ravioli and the tagliolini calabrese - had a nice kick.  Tiramisu was great though I'd skip the chocolate flourless torte - too sweet and not that yummy.   Dinner made up for the subpar dessert.  Service was decent.   Only real negative is the place is VERY loud.  Wish we'd sat outside.
The bread and bruschetta was delicious but my steak I ordered was extremely fatty.
Was good food, little pricey, as we had booked for a Bday occasion, expected a lil something for the bday person, but looked like they had no indication.

I like eating outdoors and it's a great vantage point for soaking up the downtown mountain view vibe.  Met with an old and dear friend and had a remarkable, lingering conversation. Service was attentive and personable without being overbearing.  Nice menu and well prepared food.  Don't miss the octopus!

We celebrated our friend's 85th and it was a perfect place to get together for a delicious dinner. The food was very tasty and our waitress, Nestle was so friendly and attentive!  It was a wonderful evening where we can talk since it was quiet, even on a Friday evening!  We need more restaurants like yours.

Had a Caesar & also the beet salad. Both had the Beef Wellington which was excellent. There are only 2 other places that serve a Wellington: San Jose & SF. Shared Tiramisu fir dessert which was light and tasty. Only disappointment was when we tried to order espresso, they said the machine was broken.
I ordered the special buratta appetizer followed by the papardelle pasta with seafood entrée.  Everything was excellent including the service.

They were understaffed for Mother's  Day . It made our experience less than nice. All our other visits to this place were very good. Our food was overcooked, lukewarm( sat out before being delivered). Appetizers were delicious. Staff was courteous. When we arrived there were only two people seating and taking orders although it was busy. Disappointing experience.
Really great service. Overall the food was very good - yummy spinach gnocchi and delicious cheesecake! Good wine and a nice ambiance. The prices weren't outrageous either.

This was my first time at La Fontaine, but it won't be the last.  We were having a birthday lunch for six and wanted a quiet table so we could talk.  Our server was very accommodating. We all ordered delicious salads, each one different, but all well dressed and in just the right portion size.  Then he brought the birthday lady a piece of tiramisu with a candle, gratis, which was a pleasant surprise and which was enjoyed by the celebrant - with tastes for all.
Excellent service, excellent food, and overall fantastic experience. Would highly recommend!
Food was good, not exceptional, but pricey.  Service was slow, but friendly.  A good meal, but not outstanding.

We we're there on a Friday evening (and have been there a couple times before).  Our surrounding diners were couples of old friends, or out  on a first date night.  La Fontaine is appropriate for both and very comfortable.
This place is my favorite for special occasions, in this area. Staff is nice and food is good. Their Filet mignon is perfect.
This was a family get-together and the over-all experience for all of u;s was very satisfactory. We would definitely return.

We have eaten here many times and the food was always very good. I always like to get the Pistachio Crusted Goat Cheese  honey caramelized onions, crostinis. You must get this appetizer! (You might need an extra piece of bread or two and be patient as it takes a few minutes to create) My wife had the Burgundy Braised Short Ribs  boneless rib meat, porcini mushroom, creamy polenta and this was very good and very tender. I had the (special) Veal Saltimbocca, which I have had before and was just as tender as I remembered.

If you go and the night is warm(ish), sit outside and 'people watch'!
Significantly better than average food for a reasonable price, with attentive service.
The salmon was perfectly cooked. The noodles were under cooked, but the seafood was also perfectly cooked. Overall, we had a good lunch!
The food was very disappointing. Our pasta was served aldente and tasted like catsup had been pored on it. Also used cardboard anchovies on Caesar salad. Disgusting

The ambience and service were both decent, but the cuisine was decidedly pedestrian for the price range. I was expecting something a little more modern and Californian, what I got was a fine Italian restaurant from the 1980's - from the tablecloths to the rich heartburn inducing sauces. Also I was annoyed that the menus looked mottled and had stains on them - suggesting they hadn't updated it in quite a while.

It was quite nice for lunch.  Delicious entrees were available with terrific service.  The tables seemed somewhat close together, although it was not crowded when we were there for an early lunch.  Choosing a good time if you want to maintain a conversation would be important.

We have been going here for over a year for special occasions. Our family has varied tastes and requirements such as vegetarian etc. The service is always excellent and everyone is so friendly.   They will gladly modify dishes, suggest alternatives, or even make just what you want.  Their dishes and desserts are creative, presented beautifully and always good.  The kitchen is a little slow but we don't care because, as a family, we like to take our time to catch up and enjoy being together. The atmosphere is very Italian/European. It has become our go to place.

We ( I and my husband) went there to celebrate International Women's day. This is classic French cuisine - excellent quality , creative recipes , friendly service. We ordered Cordon Bleu and Salmon Wellington, so tasty! Crème Brulee in dessert just fantastic, so  everybody should try it! 
The only thing we  wish there is some relaxing French music  ( Gainsbourg, Guetta etc.), it would make this place a real French ambience.

Poorly managed-- restaurant did not have my on-line conformed reservation, ordered glass of pinot noir and wine had been open for at least 1 day, food was somewhat above average and overpriced, even at 75% occupancy, one had to shout to hold a conversation.
The restaurant was very clean and we were seated promptly. The service was very good and the food was  considered excellent by all of the party. Would certainly recommend the restaurant.

This  was our first meal at La Fontaine, and it was excellent.  A nice mix of traditional French dishes with some variations on classics. I had lamb chops encrusted with pistachios, and the they were perfectly done, mild and flavorful.  My wife had the risotto, and it was also excellent. The service friendly and helpful. I'm looking forward to going back and sampling more of the menu.
Goat cheese was amazing. Service was great

The food and wine was really great. Beef Wellington, stuffed salmon Wellington, broccoli soup, caprese salad. The portion sizes were fine, but it was so tasty I wanted more, lol. The only bummer was the noise level (which I did see on other reviews) as there was a large boisterous group there. Overall, great place, just expect to talk loud so your date can hear you.

We enjoyed a very nice dinner on Valentine's Day, and though it was very busy, our server was very attentive and  helpful.  The seafood risotto was excellent, as was the sea bass, and the seafood paglia e fieno.  The tuna crudo appetizer was also excellent.  So happy we made a reservation and happy to have dined there on such a special occasion.

Had the salmon with a light crust wrapper) and the lamb with pistachio crust.  Both were excellent and the portion sizes generous.  Service was also very good.  Going to now bring a group here for dinner.
Third experience with this restaurant and it continues to be excellent for a business dinner or a nice evening out. Definitely make reservations on OpenTable since it does get busy around 7pm.
The ambiance is always pleasant and conducive to conversations. The menu is varied enough to be interesting but familiar enough to be comfortable. Service is always superb.
Love this place!  We have never anything we haven't liked. Their drinks are delicious as well. The staff is friendly and nice.
Food and service was amazing! Definitely looking forward to coming here again.

Overall it was a good experience for our party of 10 that became 12! Very attentive waiter that brought mostly everything out at the same time. Great birthday cake surprise with my friend's name spelled correctly from my OpenTable note! Usually I don't think the restaurants see my notes so they get an extra star. 
The wine was nothing special. My beef wellington was good but not in the top ranking since that's my favorite dish. I would come here again and try something different. Everyone at our table was happy with the food and enjoyed the pasta and seafood. Dessert was good. 
No complaints! Girl says Do.

This was the first time we dined at La Fontaine. We were a party of three there to celebrate a family member's birthday. We selected the restaurant because the Italian/French menu sounded interesting, and the restaurant was reviewed so positively by other diners.

We ordered two house-made pasta entrees and the pistachio-crusted roasted lamb chops with a fig balsamic sauce. However, some of the food was not prepared correctly and the kitchen did not coordinate the service of our food so our experience was negative. 

The server brought out the lamb entree but then we were kept waiting a few minutes before the other two entrees were served to us. When the lamb entree was served initially, it was not even hot, the accompanying vegetables were lukewarm and the dinner plate was not warm to the touch. Only the roasted potatoes were hot. This was a disappointment because the lamb was roasted properly to a medium rare as we requested, and the fig balsamic reduction was flavorful and probably would have been delicious if it had been served warm. 

Both pasta entrees were served hot but, unfortunately, the white wine in one of the pastas was not cooked out so the pasta had a "raw" alcohol taste to it. We decided not to complain because it was a birthday dinner, and we didn't want to ruin our evening. 

On the positive side, we found the staff to be friendly and attentive.

We enjoyed our meal here. The food was great. My only issue was that the service was a bit too fast. All of our courses came out remarkably fast. For a fine dining experience I thought it should have been paced a bit slower. We were dining on NYE so perhaps they were trying to turn tables over quickly.
A lovely early New Year's dinner.  Food was delicious and the service was attentive,  professional and friendly.

I went to La Fontaine for lunch with a friend today, and the lunch menu was both interesting and very reasonably priced, especially for Mountain View. Castro Street, where La Fontaine is located, is packed with restaurants--many of which have been there much longer than La Fontaine has--so perhaps that explains why there were so few other patrons there today at such a nice restaurant with such good food. It was also a weekday, although this is a holiday week. Having so few patrons today was a pity for the restaurant staff but made it nice and quiet for us to be able to talk at our nice table by the window. The food we had was excellent (a salmon panini for me and a portabella panini for my friend, both of which came with great matchstick "pommes frites" and a very good although small Caesar salad).  We also both had  cream of broccoli soup--the soup of the day--which was excellent and not too heavy. The staff were friendly and efficient, and the restaurant is quite charming. I would encourage other people visiting Castro Street to try this restaurant, especially for lunch, since the food is very good and the prices really a bargain. This was my first visit, but I'll definitely try it again.

On top of the service being great the food was unforgettable and you can tell the chef really cares. I had ordered the fresh pistachio encrusted halibut entree off the dinner specials but they were out of halibut so the chef let me substitute it with salmon. One of the best dishes Ive ever had.
Great food and service!
Excellent dining experience.  The food is delicious and expertly prepared.  Nice presentation.  Service was excellent as well.  This would be a lovely choice for date night or a special occasion.

Great place for lunch or dinner. This dinner was another experience of excellent food and attentive service. Make sure to reserve a table on OpenTable as I did and got seated despite a full restaurant of customers. A bit loud with that many customers, but we were able to have a good conversation during this business dinner.

This is one of my "go to" places for business lunches and dinners. Never too loud and therefor easy to carry on a conversation. The menu is pretty broad and the food quality is very good. Prices are reasonable , ambiance leans towards fine dining, and the wait staff is attentive and professional. If you have not visited before I recommend you give them a try. You will not be disappointed.

We used to frequent this restaurant in its previous reincarnations but food quality and choice deteriorated and we stopped going there. This was our first visit of its new reincarnation as La Fontaine and we liked the changes. The food was delicious and the service was great, almost "old world". We especially enjoyed the gnocchi and the stuffed chicken. Their by the glass Malbec was also quite good.  We will be back.

Very nice. I like the vegetarian options.  Mushroom ravioli w truffle oil. Well balanced.  
Crab cakes were good according to my sister. She said they're worth coming back for.  Dessert flourless chocolate truffle. Subtlety of flavors,  it was smooth, rich goodness.
My gnocchi dish was incredible.  The best I've ever head.  The menu had great choices.  The wait staff was very friendly.
Excellent service, excellent food. We had the Bruschetta, Strawberry Spinach Salad, Salmon Wellington and Cordon Bleu. Everything tasted great.

Don't order the seafood.  It was not fresh, nor did it taste good.  I had the seafood risotto special, my friends had the cod stuffed with crabmeat special and the branzino, and we all agreed that the fish did not taste fresh.  The dessert special, however, of apricots stuffed with marscapone and rolled in crushed pistachios, was delicious.  The service was OK, and the atmosphere was OK.  Nothing to write home about.
One of the reasons we went was my birthday and I love lava cake. What they served was tiny and did not look like the picture online!

We've enjoyed dining at La Fontaine quite frequently during the past year and have brought many friends to share this new favorite. However, dinner with 3 friends celebrating a birthday on October 30 was, for the first time, quite disappointing. The salads (both beet salad and spinach and strawberry) were not dressed enough (or at all) and were pretty tasteless.  I shared the trout special, which was not nearly as tasty as previous fish dishes have been, and my friend said the gnocchi was "OK." 

Our server was very attentive, and our window seat was comfortable and quiet. My husband and I will return to enjoy more favorite dishes from the menu, and give it a second chance,  but I doubt that my 3 friends were impressed enough to come back.

We went on a Monday evening. Our reservation was for 6:30pm. We arrived on time and the restaurant was pretty empty but eventually it filled up to almost full. They had only two servers and two cooks that evening to serve around 50 people. By the time our main course came it was already 7:30. I really like their grill octopus appetizer and in the future, I'll definitely order it again. My wife had rack of lamb. The lamb was tender and cooked just right, but we both found the sauce needed improvement, so it was just good but not excellent.  We shall not order it again. I had Chicken Cordon Bleu. It was good but not excellent, yet I may order it again. Next time we shall try their pasta.

The food and service were very good. Nice menu. It was a Saturday night around 6pm and very noisy.   Nice but unexceptional ambience. Dinner for two with one drink was about $100 with tip/tax and no dessert.
Great restaurant -- We had an excellent Italian meal here with friends.  The pasta is freshly made (a rarity) and everything was delicious.

Enjoyed a nice lunch.  Calamari Fritti was perfectly cooked and not greasy at all.  Seafood papparadelle very good with a generous helping of scallops, clams, mussels and prawns.  Service was good.  Only issue was that we were the only ones in the restaurant for the first half hour, then a group of five came in and the host seated them right on top of us when every other table in the place was empty...and they were a loud group of people.  If we hadn't been as far into the meal as we were, I would have asked to be moved.  Kind of a spoiler.  But, again, the food was very good and worth the trip from Redwood City.
Our new favorite restaurant in downtown Mountain View. Our third visit. Can't wait to go again.
Good service and food. The beef and salmon wellingtons were a pleasant offering that we don't usually see on menus much. Seafood risotto very creamy. Nice restaurant amid many on Castro Street.

The ambience is great as you can talk and enjoy the evening without too much distraction. The staff is very accommodating and so fun to talk to. Chef came out and greeted some of the guests which indicates a loyal following.  It is  always a good sign when staff including the chef comes out and greets long time customers. Makes it more intimate and more welcoming.  Food is as awesome as I can imagine - appetizers and the main course was super delicious.  I can't ask for anything more....

Good food.   Seemed like they were short staffed that night, so service was slow.  That said, staff was good quality.  Ambiance was nice but noise level was very high.  They should talk to an acoustics consultant to see if the could add some sound absorbing material to the walls or ceiling.

We live in the East Bay and have a son in Mountain View. Thus we chose La Fontaine among about 6000 restaurants in a few blocks area of downtown MV. Weekday evening. Parking and traffic are unspeakably dreadful (lots nearby but endlessly packed and many folks trolling around desperately looking for spaces). 
That said La Fontaine was acceptable. The name implies French but check the menu before you go. It's trying to be Italian and French. 
We had an octopus appetizer that was quite good and a green salad. Mains were linguini w/shrimp; what turned out to be a somewhat weird and very heavy pasta (cavatelli) with good meatballs; cordon bleu (misspelled on the menu tho correct on the website). All ok but no real reason to go back when there are hundreds of restaurants within walking distance (and we have been to one really excellent one across the street). The wine list is not on the web so I can't check to see exactly what we had. There are a few choices by the glass and we had both a white and a red by the glass that were satisfactory.
Service was quite good though I could see that our waitperson had a huge service area + making his own drinks at the bar.

We went here before a concert in Santa Clara. It was our first time dining in Mountain View and we were not disappointed. Wait staff was incredible and the food was even better! The calamari appetizer was great and the sauce was very good. My boyfriend got the Burgundy Braised Short Rib, well cooked and delicious. I got the Steak Frites. Also very good - cooked perfectly and full of flavor. We sat outside on and it was a great start to our date night!
Our favorite place in Mountain View. We go there regularly because of their excellent service and food quality. My favorite dish is the Chicken Cordon Bleu.
Food was great , Risotto and salmon salad excellent. Good service attentive wait staff

We went there for a weeknight celebration of my daughter's birthday.  Most of the food was decent with room for much improvement--the steak frites were good and the fries were excellent, the capellini pomodoro was tasty but the pasta was way over cooked, my beet salad was okay but not well-seasoned, same for the crab cakes. And the dishes are really expensive and the restaurant, not crowded at all, which is a bad sign in downtown Mountain View. The staff were very nice, however.
Awesome food and service, however the bartender was a no-show and none of the rest of the employees "knew how" to make a drink. Bad management there.

We consistently love this small, quiet, surprisingly not very busy restaurant! We've now returned 8-10 times, usually to introduce friends, to this little known gem on Castro Street. Not one dish has been a disappointment. This time the server overheard us mentioning the birthdays we were celebrating, and she brought us a complimentary dessert and port wine without our ever having requested a birthday surprise. Highly recommended!

A big disappointment for us.  10 minutes after our first course was the table next to us, which arrived after us, was served with their entrees, including one dish we had ordered.  15 minutes later the waitress volunteered that our entrees were on the way.  15 minutes late nothing.  We asked for our check.  No explanation or apology from our waitress or the manager, who was standing nearby.  Did the kitchen lose our order?  Had we not ordered enough drinks?  Had they run out of lamb and were waiting for a new shipment from New Zealand?  Well, at least we enjoyed the excellent soup and crab cakes.  So we went down the street to the new ramen place to finish our dinner.
Good service but mediocre food.
Mostly undiscovered gem on Castro St. in Mtn. View.  Food is very good -- Italian-French fusion.  Not crowded and consistent (we've been here three times).

We sat outside for lunch, which was very pleasant.  Service was good.  The calamari was nicely done, not greasy.  Grilled salmon pannini was very tasty as were the salads. There are many options for lunch so we will return.

This was my second trip to celebrate birthdays wth special friends. The service was admirable. We enjoyed our waiter"Owner", who was friendly, knowledgeable, and charming. The food was delicious, and served in a timely fashion. We had a table in front of the window, enjoying the passing of individuals on Castro Street.  A very pleasant experience.
Food was very good.  Great ambiance for a special occassion.  Good service. Not too noisy.  Good  experience when you want good ambiance and don't mind paying for it.

I greatly enjoyed the food at this restaurant. I had the Chicken Paillard, and it was great! I was a little worried about ordering chicken, as sometimes it can be plain without a sauce (due to gluten/dairy/sugar food restrictions, I am limited in what I can have!). This chicken was very flavorful and the steamed veggies were not just your basic veggies! They were very good, and I definitely would order this again. They accommodated for a large group (13 of us) for lunch, and it was pretty empty at 11:30am, so we got the staff's full attention. A little pricey, but it's a nice ambience, and they had good service.
The food is excellent.  I'm a huge fan of the rib-eye steak in particular.
Went for Happy Hour - nice prices for drinks . Fabulous asparagus. Great special for dinner so ate dinner & wonderful ice cream with Kahlua for dessert.

We have eaten here before and found the food to be just as good as I remember. We sat outside and the train noise was barely noticeable. The sidewalk crowd noise, however, was just above average but still not loud enough to force us inside. The wait staff was very attentive and polite; even when I ordered the wrong meal and they replaced it.
Wewill definitely go back again and again as the food and service is way above average.
The soup is very average and does not have the flavor of real Italian Vegetable soup. The meatball sauce is not authentic. Looks like it is from a can.
The bouillabaise is delicately seasoned and well balanced, creating a rich broth. Great variety of seafood in it and a generous portion.

Game hen entree was well prepared, but lacking in side dish. Pasta was dish was decent but sauce was not high restaurant quality.  Appetizers were prepared in typical manner, but ingredients were not top quality.  Sidewalk dining was very nice on a warm evening, and service was respectable but not at level of a 4-star restaurant.  Not what we expected based on price and previous reviews.  There was nothing extra compared to lesser restaurants in the area.

Impressive food, relaxing ambiance, moderate price.  The steak of my Steak Pommes Frites order was extremely tender and flavorful (I believe Sous-Vide).  Le Fontaine also is in a great spot. Castro street's multi-ethnic eateries and eclectic shops do a great job of reflecting the unique techie-foodie culture of the Silicon Valley. I Definitely will be back.

The kitchen knows what it's doing....
The waiters could be more charming!
One of the best on Castro Street. They will make any dish that you want that is not on the menu
We enjoyed the service and it was fast. We will go there again to try something different.

Just want to try out ! 

The weather is quite warm outside, having a glass of cool Sauvignon blanc and a glass of Chardonnay helps cool us down. But it works just for a while, we're not sure that their a/c is broken or the higher volume of alcohol in our blood makes us feel so warm. 

Appetizer today is calamari and bruschetta. Calamari is good but bruschetta is great - fresh and juicy tomato go along well with our white wine. 

Entrée - Salmon wellington is good as well as saucy/juicy Seafood pappardelle. First serve of seafood pappardelle is under cook - some portion of pasta is not cooked well. But it's not a big deal since they responded fast to take it back and serve us the new one. 

Will come back to try other dish. 

PS. Nice wine will taste better when serve with a nice fine wine glass.
Very nice restaurant with good menu for lunch. Quiet place during lunch to have easy conversation about business with client.
Great food and atmosphere!  Highly recommend!!

The restaurant looks great and the waitstaff is attentive. The bar looks like a lot of fun. The steak frites was very, very grisly.  The bouillabaisse was very good. Disappointed in the burrata and grilled octopus. The mango sorbet and chocolate fondant desserts were good. Overall, ok--but could have been better, I think. Strictly speaking, not really a French restaurant. Euro perhaps.

Made a reservation but got sat outside due to max capacity inside. They said they called to let me know there was no more available seating inside, but I never received the call. Otherwise service was okay and food was only fair.

We were sort of surprised.  The restaurant was full  and very loud but not in a good way.  The food was average, our waitstaff was quite good, but it was expensive.  I had two dishes with pastry crusts, and both times it was tough and chewy.  My wife had ribs and they were mushy and didn't have much taste.
Exceptionally good French toast.  Also like the hangar steak with peppercorn sauce, and fries with truffle oil.
Great French toast
Great experience for pescatarians.  Bouillabaisse and branzino were both great.  Pana cotta desert was a nice finish.  Service was there exactly when we needed it.
Great place for lunch outside on Castro St. Tasty, light dishes that don't put you to sleep. And great service. Will definitely be back.
The food was excellent, nicely seasoned; salad lightly dressed, and the service was superb. Definitely a place to do again!

This is a nice quaint French restaurant but you would. It know it from the outside. We enjoyed our appetizers. I had the escargot - excellent. My husband had the liver pate - fabulous. My husband had the filet for dinner and it was cooked just perfect. I had the sole special which was also good. Unfortunately we were too full for dessert but next time we go we will definitely have dessert. For the 2 of us including a $75 bottle of wine the total bill including tip was $200.
service and food were awesome! Levent was our server and his recommendations were spot on.  Can't go wrong with the Lamb and beef entrees.  Can't wait to go back.
We were expecting a better experience given the restaurant's ratings, but the food was bland and the service was slow.

We have eaten here twice before going to the Mountain View Center for Performing Arts.  The food is excellent and the service is great, too.  My husband wanted a dish he had eaten there before and, although it wasn't on the menu, the waiter found a way to accommodate him.  The restaurant was very busy when we went -- there was a large multi-table party with parents and young kids -- some screaming .  This detracted from our experience but it wasn't the restaurant's fault.  We will eat there again because of the great food and service.
Food was great, service was very nice and the atmosphere was also very nice. A little loud, it was hard to hear my friends right across the table from me.
Thoughtful service. They remembered our wine preferences from last time. The Cordon Bleu is my personal favorite.  My girlfriend likes the Salmon Wellington.
Came here with a co worker. Food was delicious and and the service was excellent. I will be sure to come back to this place the next time I'm in MV

Since we had a reservation, the table was ready by the time we reached. The waiters at the restrauant are very helpful and helped us with our orders.
The service was fast. 
Food was just Amazing. Tastes great. 
Only complain about the restraunt is that it was too loud.

Since trying this restaurant we've been back twice.  The food every course was all well thought out, prepared and presented.  We had apps, Salad, soup, two Mains, and desert.  I had a pistachio crusted lamb chops that were prepared perfectly and I've never seen crusted chops before super tasty.  My wife had duck that was the best duck either of us have ever had.  Not greasy, not dry, super tender, super delicious.  My only knock on this restaurant is that they cramp two tops way too close together you almost have to share your neighbours conversations.

Serving sizes ranged from small to medium but what they lack in quantity they made up for in flavor ten times over!
The oysters were tiny but exploded with flavor and were fairly affordable.
Great place for a romantic dinner. Best meal I've had in months.

The restaurant had a special menu for Valentine's Day which was fine, but the offerings were somewhat limited. e.g. just one salad. Food was nicely presented and prepared and we enjoyed it. Wine list was very sparse. Fortunately we brought our own and didn't have to settle. Corkage at $15 is reasonable.

My husband and I dined here for the first time on Valentine's Day and we didn't have a good experience at all. The portions were very small for the price. My husband had the surf and turf but only 2 shrimp came out with his filet mignon. Our server didn't know the menu when we asked questions. She didn't ask how well his steak was cooked or brought a pen to pay the bill.

We went to la fontaine because we wanted to get some good home made pasta.  
Apps were OK, Pasta was alright at best, and not impressed with the desert.

Would not recommend, not special.
Excellent dinner with one glitch. Waiter didn't warn us how long the dessert would take.  It seemed to be longer than the main course.

Perhaps the most remarkable thing about this place is the service. Everyone was so helpful, friendly but not intrusive. The food is excellent. We went on a Saturday night and probably will not do that again, as it was there were several very noisy groups there, but on a weeknight, I'm sure it is delightful. There really was no way for the restaurant to control the noise.
I appreciate that my request was honored. I found the restaurant on Yelp, and I am pleased that we all felt it was a winner.

Mountain View's Castro Street is a dining center of Silicon Valley, with dozens of restaurants of every ethnicity. We were not familiar with La Fontaine, but were intrigued with the idea of "French-Italian Fusion" cuisine, so we went there for a lunch for three, and followed sometime later for a dinner for six. At lunch we were the only patrons. At dinner the restaurant filled, and was a bit noisy.
