Everyone enjoyed their meals, from the pistachio-crusted goat cheese or the crab-cake appetizers, to the duck or seafood or boneless short-rib main courses, to the dark chocolate-torte dessert. The only (minor) complaints about the food were that the duck was more well-done than the requested "medium rare," and the gnocchi was a bit too soft/mushy; but everyone enjoyed all their meals. Service was always quite good. Cost was a bit high-- about $50 per person with a few shared appetizers and desserts and not much wine-- but worth it. We will definitely go there again.

It's been over five years since we've eaten here, but it's still fabulous.  We both ordered the starter salad with house dressing which is always good.  Also, their house bread is delicious.  The salmon wellington was a very generous serving, served with risotto and vegetables, cooked to perfection with a light sauce.  We finished with profiteroles and ice cream.  We love this neighborhood restaurant, still great after it's many years in this location.  The only negatives were the air conditioning was set too cool.  I had to keep my jacket on during dinner.  And the lighting was too dim.  I had some difficulty reading the menu.   All the food was stellar however!

The fact that the entire restaurant was empty at noon should have been a clue.The wait staff was attentive and polite, but, one of them wreaked of cigarette smoke. 

We ordered Calamari for appetizer which was very tender but overly salted. I ordered Steak Frites which came prepared rare (I was not asked how I wanted it prepared) and extremely salty. The fries were also salty; and I like salt! They did offer to bring me another but by that point I was done.

Seated immediately. The wine we ordered was not available but we were offered an alternative that was excellent at the same price (lower end of range). My seafood pasta was excellent. My wife's risotto was very good. She is an amateur chef and has made risotto many times. She felt that the broth in which risotto was prepared should have been more flavorful and it was more tasty with added salt, which she rarely uses at home. My seafood pasta was excellent. The calamari appetizer was very good.
Service was excellent. Our waiter was very attentive to our needs and concerned that we enjoyed our meal. The major negative of the restaurant is the noise level. For those of us over 60 who like a quiet dinner the noise was quite intrusive. I would certainly go back if the noise could be better controlled. Overall I think it is one of the better non-Asian restaurants in this area.
Cordon Bleu is really good
Wonderful food and a delightful waiter!

I have been to this restaurants on many occasions and decided to come back for New Years eve with my girlfriend. The food was exceptional and great tasting, particularly their pasta and the sauce they use. We ordered a new years special meal and it was absolutely amazing. The waiters are very respectful, polite, and fast. I highly recommend this place to anyone!

Family went to eat at 'La Fontaine" for New Year's Eve as I had read some very good reviews.

Unfortunately, had not realized that menu would be vey short on that evening so I could not order what I was looking forward to eat.

Food was disappointing and servings were very small. Even though , there were 5 of us ,they gave us 4 stuffed dates for appetizers. 

Not impressed, will not be going back.
The service was slow, the food was not that great and the place was incredibly loud
The Place is very small, and the host and hostess look new to their roles. Very busy and they were having trouble with their grill. Maybe was an off night, but the service was really choppy!
Had French colleague that was pleasantly surprised and enjoyed it.

We recently celebrated a special birthday  for my mom and invited a group of family and close friends.  Everything was perfect.  The food was delicious and beautifully presented.  The service was outstanding and made us all feel special.  I wanted it to be a perfect day for my mom and it was.

This is our third dinner at La Fontaine, and we have been more than pleased each time. The menu is divine, the food delivers on its promise, the service is always friendly and professional, and the quiet atmosphere is calming.
The cuisine is delicious and very consistent! My favorite specials are the lamb shanks and the toasted almond crusted sole!
Good food but slow kitchen, very few diners yet it was a three hour dinner!

Made reservations for 5 and they still made us wait 30 mins for our table. They had plenty of tables open but purges they were understaffed for the night. At the bar we received okay service from the bartender but the Manager who was standing there was extremely rude. For that reason, and for average food we will not be coming back.

We have been there many times and food and service were excellent.  Asked friends to join us for Sunday brunch.  They put us outside because of wedding party inside of about 15.  Service was TERRIBLE!  WAITED 1 1/2 HR TO BE SERVED.  Many requests ignored.  If food not good, would not go back.

they took veal off of the menu it
 was my favorite
From the soup, appetizers to the entrees and desserts; everything was tasty.  The flavor of each dishes show that the chef is well rounded.  We would definitely come back for the food.

Nice place to dine. The menu offers good choices and the food is tasty and delicious. The celebrate birthdays with a complimentary piece of Tiramisu cake. That's a nice touch. Friendly and attentive staff.

I have been here several times and have liked it each time.  They have a very nice diverse menu.  I have tried their salads with  various protein, the paninis are tasty and I love their very thin fries.  It's a great deal to get a panini, salad and fries for $9.  Other menu items are also good.  I have gone here with large groups to celebrate a birthday or just with two of us.

Attentiveness of staff was outstanding.  Someone came by our table every few minutes to makes sure we had everything we needed.  Food was good but menu was somewhat limited.  I will go again but will try something different.  Had the Beef Wellington which was fine but not my favorite presentation of this dish.  Dessert was excellent and enjoyed the wine by the glass menu as my wife likes red and I prefer white.

Overall nice restaurant and very clean.
That was a rather large party going on at the same time of our visit but it was just handled so beautifully everyone was so professional and every table mattered

This used to be a nice, quiet restaurant where you could order French-Italian dishes that are still cooked very well.  One also used to be able to carry on a decent conversation with your table mates.  Not any more!  The live music is turned up to such a high volume that you can not hear your table mates speak nor understand what they're saying unless you know how to read lips.  The sound is simply cacophonous!  We were sitting at the far end of the restaurant well away from where this noise was being produced.
The bouillabaisse was amazing.

We love this restaurant.
Their margaritas are great and their customer service is the best!
We tried the restaurant for the first time, had a really nice dinner and will definitely go back again.

our party of five all agreed that we would return for both the food and the service.  I  would not call the food exceptional, but it was definitely better than just “good”. I had the seafood risotto and the portion was excellent and the flavors were very good.

LA Fontaine never fails us. We have had intimate dinners for two and larger parties for eight and each time we are treated to a nice meal by a caring and thoughtful restaurant owner. It's a relatively small place with a mix of food choices. I wouldn't consider the food spectacular for a true foodie but we always enjoy it and find something to keep everyone happy. Nice cocktail menu too.

We did a surprise birthday, just a small group, while the food was great our service was not.  When the dessert came out, there wasn't any recognition of my friend's birthday, not a candle, not a happy birthday to her.  I even said to our waitress and pointing out who's birthday it was but there wasn't any celebration.  We had to ask for refills on our ice tea, ask for our coffee that never showed up when our desserts came.  I'd come back because the food was delicious but the service, at least the lady we had, would make me think twice.  The appetizers, especially calamari was really small portion compared to the price you pay.  Something to think about.

We went to this new restaurant in Mt. View, CA on a whim to try a new place to eat. Reserved via Open Table. Located on busy Castro St, our reservations were for 6:30. We had a hard time finding a parking spot and called the restaurant to advise we would be late. No problem was the reply. We sat outside and had the option of a heat lamp if we wished. As for the food, we decided to try a new Hors d’Oeuvre called "Pistachio Crusted Goat Cheese with honey caramelized onions and crostinis". This is to die for! Do not pass this up. For dinner, I had the Veal Saltimboca, presented flat, not rolled as I was used to. Excellent and Tender! Served with a small amount (just enough) of mashed potatoes with truffle flavoring. My wife had the Capellini Pomodoro with prawns (extra cost). Lots of flavoring but she requested more sautéed garlic which was promptly served. Wine was a Pinot Gregio and a Sonoma-Cutrer Chardonnay (nice and buttery smooth). Too full for dessert (next time, we may skip the delicious bread and dip to we can have dessert!). I would go back just to have the same order as I had this time but I will try something else on the menu as it just has to be as good as what I just had.

This was our second time at La Fontaine.  Our lunch the previous week was memorable with two delicious chicken dishes so we came back for brunch.  The French/Italian fusion really works.  The crab benedict was delicious and the wine selection well chosen and reasonable.  The ambience made us feel we were in the City without the hassles and the service was excellent.  We will definitely return.

The service was not pushy or rushed. Food excellent. Bread could have been warmer. 
Cannot wait to come back.

Experimented to try and find Italian style that have variety. Met need to try gluten-free pasta - any sauce and chose basil/tomato with eggplant.  Just the correct amount of spiciness to balance tomato sauce. Had appetizer platter which would recommend since sampling of all excellent small plates meals.

La Fontaine reminds me of having dinner is a great restaurant in the Bastille district in Paris, only missing someone smoking next to you.  Food is excellently done.  Risotto was packed with seafood and flavor.  Pasta was cooked al dente.  Special was beef or salmon Wellington which were both very hearty and delicious.
Good salads, vegetable appetizers, and vegetable sides make it easy to eat healthy.  Prices were fair, but portions should increase 10%, 15-20% more for the sides.

We have been to La Fontaine several times and food was quite good.  This last time, however,  there was absolutely NO seasoning in my Bouillabaisse sauce nor  any of the seafood components. 
 My husband had the boneless short ribs and said the meat had no taste to it.
Finally, the temperature of both meals was a bit cooler than we have experienced.

There was no problems with the service

Our second dinner at La Fontaine was not as good as our first.   My glass of wine was served in a large water glass.  The shared appetizer crab cakes needed more flavor.  We had to ask for more bread.  The fish for one of our dinner companions was too well-done.   The veal saltimbocca was merely slices of veal with prosciutto on top.  The sauce, however, was very good.   It was very noisy, even though we were at a table in the rear away from the bar.  Carpeting on the floor might help to absorb the noise.  There are certain things we look for in a restaurant where the average main course is $24, and this time La Fontaine did not quite measure up.

Went as a large group. Food was fantastic. Fees ingredients. The veal cutlet was awesome. Decent choices for vegetarians too. Service was very indifferent. Not patient enough. Did not serve us bread till the end.
Over all a good experience. Food is above average.
I think of this as a romantic spot but they were very sweet with my kids when we went for brunch the other day.

This was our first time to eat here and I was expecting a good meal, but not a great meal.  It was a great meal and the service was excellent.  They let us dine while keeping an eye on the table in case we needed anything.  

I found the food to be creative and delicious.  A 3-course meal without alcohol should costs about $50/person.  Well worth it considering the quality.

We had not been here before, and were attracted by the curb appeal and attractive façade.  Our table for six was nicely set and ready when we arrived.  The menu was unique andf varied, and each of us ordered something different, and everyone was most pleased with their meal.  Service was great.  I'd definitely recommend this place.

OK, this was our  second visit to  La Fontaine .  The food was very good,  the server was attentive, and on a Tuesday night it was packed!  Who would have thought , in Mountain View such a scene  would exist on a Tuesday!  Palo Alto, yes, but not here..  OK it was impossible to find a place, the garages were all full and it was just by luck that in circling the lots a couple pulled out and we got a space!  Did not start the evening off well.  The reservations were fine, we had a decent table, and an attentive server.  However the stars were the bus boy - who was right there with water all the time -- and another server (short young woman with a pixie haircut who was constantly on the move, and always had a smile. ) who on her way back and forth had time to get some lemon slices for us -- that our regular server seemed to forget about, but it was busy in all fairness. Now the food.  We had the octopus and it was the best I have even eaten.  Not rubbery at all and very moist and tender.  A  winner.  One diner had the rib eye,  very nice, but a tough and salty though.  The other had the short ribs and those were excellent.  The side veggies were not done to my taste, but perhaps for some they would be fine.  All in all it was a nice experience aside from the parking hassle.  We did however strike Mountain View off our dinner location list - there are just too many great places around that have adequate parking nearby and are not  so crowded.

We visit Mt. View 4 or 5 times during the TheatreWorks production season and enjoy trying the many restaurants near to the Mt. View Civic Center.  While the food was not outstanding at Lafontaine it was more than good.  Service was attentive and not rushed.  Mt. View is not our home area and I wouldn't necessarily travel down the Peninsula to dine at Lafontaine.  However the food quality and experience was definitely more than good and will be on our theatre rotation.

We went on a Thursday night, and though it was not crowded, the service was pretty slow. It was very difficult to find parking in the area, as many of the nearby parking garages were full. The food was so-so. The menu looked really good though. I would recommend to others looking for a pricey meal, but not sure I would go again.

Food was mediocre service terrible
Couldnt complain because the owner speaks no English!!!

Party of 4 for dinner Saturday. Meals were all very good. Service lapsed ~1/3 way through. Our server stopped coming by to check on us. We saw here waiting on other tables, near the back of the restaurant (our table was closer to the front), and sometimes walking behind the bar. We had to flag the attention of other staff to get a steak knife and to order more drinks. Not sure if she thought another server was covering our table at some point.

Their octopus appetizer is very good.  Excellent selection of main courses.  Their meat-oriented dishes are very good (cordon blue chicken, ribs, steak).  The boullabaise not so much, lacked flavor depth and saffron.  Nice staff.  Good wines.

The food at La Fontaine was very good. Fresh and inspired combinations, and all of it was very nicely prepared. The service vacillated from very helpful to inattentive. Overall the experience was good but not great. Worth going again to see if they can be better on a less busy night.
This is not an Italian restaurant.  i was disappointed.  I come from Boston where we have real Italian restaurants.  Lots of them.

Visited La Fontaine for a birthday dinner and we very much enjoyed the experience.  MIchelle, our server, was friendly, knowledgeable, and very attentive.  The restaurant is small, and we were having an early dinner during the week, so when crowded, it probably could be very noisy, although the tables are nicely placed.  The food was terrific: saltimbocca, cordon bleu, crab cakes, and caesar salad all excellent.  A good mixture of French and Italian.  A complimentary birthday dessert(tiramisu) with candle was very well done, along with a duet, "Happy Birthday..."  Food presentation is creative.  Did I forget the bread?  Also was excellent.  A standout on a street with many restaurants. We will return!!

We look for a new restaurant to try once a month and had tried just about everything on Castro.  We were please when La Fontaine opened up but hadn't yet had a chance to try it.  We found the steak to be outstanding and the salads exceptionally good.  The seafood pasta was a little underflavored but still good.  We had a very pleasant evening and an excellent meal.

Very warm and welcoming as soon as we entered the restaurant.  Service was the perfect mix of attentiveness while not being overwhelming. We were there for lunch and ordered the Chicken Panini which came with the House Salad and perfectly cooked string Pommes Frites. We were also served soft, warm focacica with dipping oil while waiting for our meals.  The open faced Tartines sounded delicious and we will try those next time.
used a travelzoo voucher for this visit.  Had the strawberry spinach salad which was excellent. the steak frites was delicious.  overall, a great meal that we enjoyed!
The food is delicious.  We had the crab cakes appetizer, burgundy short ribs, and salmon in pastry.  All were superb.  Our server, Michelle, made the evening fantastic!

Tried La Fontaine for the first time and loved it.  We started with the crab cakes and they were a good size and very tasty.  The salads were generously portioned.  The main dishes were a hit.  The seafood pasta was delicious with the sauce not being too overpowering.  The service was excellent.  We will definitely return.
Excellent food and service. We will be back for more
Very attentative wait staff and the food was outstanding - beautifuly presented as well. An enjoyable experience and will go back.

The food was very nice. The service was good. The restaurant will be much nicer if they will introduce some sound absorbent surface to lower the level of noise. We will go back but only during warmer nights so we can stay outside and enjoy not only very good food but also nice conversation. DB level was so high when the restaurant was full that you could not hear the person next to you talking. It might be OK for 20 something, but for a middle age person the noise level is deafening.
The service started slow but did improve.. It is very noisy and hard to hear without  shouting.. We had 6 different entrees and everyone loved theirs. Salads were ok but not exceptional

We had reservations and arrived a little early so sat at the bar and ordered wine. The bartender was very friendly and service was great. Service continued to be great as the rest of our party arrived and we moved to a table. The catch of the day was sole, and it was wonderfully prepared. I'd also recommend the Cordon Bleu.

We tried La Fontaine for the first time a couple of days ago, and were very impressed.  We were seated immediately (we had reservations), and greeted right away. Drinks were great - unique and yummy.  We had the calamari fritti appetizer - small portion but cooked perfectly with wonderful sauces.  Beet salad was a little "meh" - lovely, but not very flavorful to my taste buds, and the beets were slightly undercooked.  The halibut special was delicious, but the braised short ribs over polenta was over-the-top SCRUMPTIOUS!  We will definitely go back.
The food was good, except for the pumpkin gnocchi (sauce) which was way too salty.

Our first visit was lunch and we wanted to try as much as we could.  the Bruschetta & the Gratin of eggplant & ricotta were wonderful as was the arugula and beet salad.  Our main courses were the Chx Scaloppini and the Sole. The whole meal was truly gourmet experience.  I want to try the
Gnoochi next time because the waitress let us try the sauce & it was heavenly!

I came for dinner and ordered the crab cakes appetizer followed by the boulibaise as a main entrée.   The appetizer consisted of two crab cakes served on a bed of arugula.  The boulibaise consisted of a large bowl with a combination of mussels, clams, scallops, prawns and salmon.  I thought the crab cakes were very good and the boulibaise was just good.   Unfortunately, the restaurant became very noisy as I was finishing my meal.

The food and service were outstanding at La Fonaine Restaurant. We started with the olive appetizer which was delicious and artfully displayed. The warm goat cheese appetizer encrusted with pistchios with crostini was very tasty. The salmon wellington was beautiful with risotto underneath it and served with veggies. Delicious. The dessert was divine - profiteroles. We loved the whole dinner. The weak point was the small wine list. Our server was very friendly and helpful. The ambience was lovely and the back-lit bar was very pretty. I would definitely go again!!
This is a nice little restaurant with tasty food and attentive service.

La Fontaine was a great choice for a birthday lunch. We ate indoors, but there are tabes out front as well.
We loved the food and service. The menu has many choices. We had baked goat cheese with honey and pistachios, followed by lovely greens with hazenuts and red and yellow beets - plenty to share. Both were super. Our entrees were shellfish over pasta in a tomato sauce, and chicken with mushrooms in a white sauce. Wonderful. We'll be back!

I ordered the salmon wellington and my wife ordered the boulibaise.  Although it was recommended by a former waitress, I thought my entre was just okay - nothing special.  However, my wife's boulibaise was much better, although not as quite as good as at some other places.  The service was very good, but the restaurant got to be quite noisy before we left.

This is the third time I've eaten at this restaurant.  While my experience hasn't always been good, in this case both the food and service were excellent.  I ordered the eggplant augratin appetizer and the steak frites entre (consisting of a good quality rib eye steak served with a mushroom sauce and very slender French fried potatoes).   In addition, the service could not have been better!

Service was excellent with no rushing and the food was excellent.  Will go again.
The only problem was trying to find a parking spot.  Five minute walk from parking spot. (on a week day, Wednesday!)
Enjoyed our brunch at La Fontaine very much. Delicious food and attentive service - perfect! Strongly recommend it to all.

The outside dinning ambience was pleasant with good food presentation. My companion said the Chicken Paillard was tasty and hot when served. My short ribs were tender, seasoned nicely but barely warm, and the meat had an "off" taste - not quite freezer burn but old. This was a business meeting so I could not afford to appear finicky by sending the ribs back - so I ate bread. Only half the outside tables were occupied and the multiple servers were polite but it took two requests, and what felt like forever, to get the bread basket replenished. There are plenty of other restaurants on Castro Street so I do not plan to return and have let my friends know that while pleasant the quality was erratic so they might enjoy another restaurant better.
Another delightful meal, well-presented and thoroughly enjoyed!

my wife and I ate dinner here and we were shown immediately to our nice table.  The servers were prompt and courteous, attentive to our every need.  The menu had many intriguing items and we found the food to be very tasty!  We will definitely be back soon!  It also looked like there were plenty of items on the menu for the kids, so we'l bring them next time!

I love this restaurant for lunch and dinner, whether it's a large dinner party, a work lunch, or a romantic dinner with my sweetie.  The restaurant is small and intimate with attentive waiters (but they don't hover!) who are content for you to have a quick meal or a two hour dining experience--whatever you desire.  Don't miss the goat cheese appetizer because it's spectacular!

I wanted to have French-Italian food for my Father's Day lunch and found La Fontaine on Castro Street.  The restaurant has been opened for about a year but there are only a couple of reviews about it.  We found the bartender/waiter extremely friendly and helpful.  He spoke with a lovely European accent and was attentive throughout our dining experience.  We enjoyed our drinks and every dish we ordered especially the fantastic dessert choices.  At the end, I was treated to a free glass of Cosmopolitan served in an artistic cocktail crystal to celebrate my Father's Day!  My wife was happy to pay the bill which was quite reasonable considering the quality of the food and the wonderful service.   I must go back for dinner soon.
Out of control children. Management did nothing to stop the noise. Ruined for everyone else.
The food was OK, but nothing special.  The staff were attentive.  The location is great and the outdoor dining nice.

We've dined at La Fontaine a few times in the past year, including New Year's Eve, and have always left satisfied. The wait staff is attentive without hovering. They provide excellent wine recommendations and the menu is diverse. Is it French or Italian? As they say, it's a fusion. They use an interesting combination of ingredients and unique sauces, pay attention to presentation, and, if you want it, a variety of pasta dishes. Portions are relatively generous. There's nothing unique about the dessert selection, but often decorated with fresh fruit and always tasty.

From the review we expected a good, if not great dinner.  Unfortunately, our entrees were below par.  The ribs were fairly dry, and not tasty; the duck didn't have much flavor either.  The profiteroles were good, though small.  For a restaurant on Castro in Mt. View to be half-full Saturday night, we are not the only ones who think it's time for a new chef or a menu review.

This restaurant is relatively new and could use improvements in service and food. My seafood boulabaisse was lukewarm and bland.  I had them reheat it in the microwave. The others in our party also thought their dishes were too bland.  The service was great with drink ordèrs but slow after that. This can become a terric dining option with some minor adjustments.
I always enjoy La Fontaine, but for some reason this time, the music was playing at too loud of a volume and it was not easy to have an enjoyable conversation.  I have not had this issue there before
When I have someone coming from out of town, I always impress them with the food and service here!
Had lunch with a friend at sidewalk tables outside restaurant. Very nice and good for conversation. Not hurried at all. Good service.

We were a party of 10 on a Sunday night, our table was ready and wait staff were also.  Service was prompt and unobtrusive.  Food was very good, except one pasta dish was a bit dry.  We brought our own wine for the main course, but did order a bottle to share before ordering.  Corkage was a reasonable $15/bottle.  We enjoyed dinner very much and will go again.

This restaurant serves the best of what France and Italy have to offer.  Definitely not your usual pasta place!
The Salmon Wellington with beurre blanc sauce was innovative and satisfying; both my date and I enjoyed
it.  We shared the house salad with Italian olives and found it just the right prelude to the dinner.

If you've been waiting for a solidly decent Italian meal in Mountain View, La Fontaine is the answer to your prayers.
Bread came first, and it was a great start.  The olive oil had a nice blend of herbs and spices, surprisingly spicy.
The cobb salad was fresh and vibrant, with sweet fresh tomatoes, crisp lettuce, and perfectly cooked bacon.
The angel hair pasta was well-cooked and well-seasoned.  I got mine with clams (instead of chicken or shrimp) and they were fresh and meaty.  The sauce light yet flavorful.  There was enough pasta for 2 meals.
The gnocchi was perfectly cooked, with sauce that was super creamy. 
Drinks were well-made and delicious.
Service was casual and delightful.
We plan on making this a regular dinner spot.

It's a happy place, with decent service and an upbeat vibe. But the food is bland. I was looking forward to enjoying the salmon Wellington, but its looks far out-shined its taste. Likewise, the bruschetta of smoked salmon and artichoke sounded great, but was merely adequate (bread, cream cheese, a sliver of lox and a sliver of artichoke: that's NOT bruschetta...it should have olive oil & rubbed garlic, not cream cheese!). Dinner for two will easily cost over $100. For just a little bit more you can avail yourself of a truly upscale restaurant.
It is nice to have a good ciOntinental restaurant in the heart of the ethnic area of Mountain View- food and service and wines excellent!

I have mix review about this place. Some dishes were average and some dishes were below average.
Appetizers were good and the bouillabaisse was ok. However my husband had the veal cutlet . This dish was bad: the sauce was wrong and the veal was thin and no taste.
Carrot and potato soup was wonderful, and seabass was cooked perfectly.

I love the Cordon Bleu which is difficult to find in the US. I like that the kitchen is so visible in the restaurant behind glass. On Saturday night, the live music was entertaining and created a nice atmosphere. Some reviewers were talking about the menu choices being traditional, I rather enjoy some real tasty classic preparations, Cordon Bleu being one of them. The service was impeccable and we will certainly come back, often :-).

This cute little French-Italian fusion restaurant is unique for its neighborhood. We sat outside on a cool evening, but when it got colder, they gladly moved us in for our main course. The calamari was very fresh and crisp and everyone was happy with their entres. I went with a group of die-hard "foodies," so there's a lot to be said for that. The short ribs are particularly good and the menu has something for everyone. Overall positive experience.
This restaurant is on the edge of a remodeled mall with lots of parking. The staff is exceptionally friendly and inviting. The menu items are tasty.
I have been to La Fontaine twice and both times the food and service were great. It is nice to have a good Mountain View for something non- Asian! We will definitely return!

Not an exciting menu, but a good range of choices. I had the chicken Cordon Bleu, my husband the veal saltimbocca. Both were delicious. Our friends had the game hen and the trout special and were very happy. We tried several appetizers as well. My favorite was the mushrooms with polenta, but all were tasty.

We had the shrimp appetizer, salmon and veal saltimbocca - TO DIE FOR. Seriously, the best Italian food I have ever had outside of Italy. Nick and Hilary gave us rockstar service, drinks were divine. The atmosphere is excellent, beautiful lighting, romantic feel, and the acoustics didn't make us feel like everyone could hear our conversation. A big plus! Have dinner here sometime, you won't regret it! In fact, I'm sure you'll be back for more!!

We weren't actually looking for a spectacular restaurant when we made our reservation. There are a lot of good restaurants on Castro St in Mountain View. Visually, La Fontaine does not distinguish itself from many others. However, the staff was warm and outstanding. The menu was great and food superlative! The décor was clean and up-scale but not spectacular, probably limited by the long/thin dimensions of its allotted space. Not bad, just not up to the outsanding food and service! We will definitely go back! Excellent value, too!
Excellent food, great service and yummy dessert!!

We were at La Fontaine on a Wednesday evening, with the end of the office-party crowd whooping it up (8 people at a table), and not many other customers. The greeter was also our waiter, and seemed to be managing the staff too. Our service was prompt and friendly, but neither the service nor the table settings was "special" in the way one appreciates for a special event. We had the goat cheese and caramelized onions (and more!) and the eggplant gratin for starters. Both delicious, the goat cheese dish outstanding. We had fish -- a red snapper special and the Salmon Wellington -- both good, but I really liked the Wellington. We chose a white wine, Pecorino Salva, by the glass, which was a wonderful accompaniment.

My friend and I really enjoyed this restaurant. It is one of the few non-Asian restaurants on Castro Street and we found the food excellent. I was especiallly happy to see a restaurant that can offer chicken that is not chicken breast--the Coq au vin was great!

This is an amazing place. If you are looking for quick service and a rushed meal then stay away, go to McDonald's. If you are looking for great food, great wine, and a relaxed atmosphere, then this is an excellent restaurant.
My wife and I both enjoyed everything about La Fontaine, I have been looking for a great dill sauce served with salmon for some time and found it here. The spinach salad was incredible. The bottle of Italian red wine was perfect with our entrees. The texture of the creme brulee had the perfect amount of creaminess that this dessert is supposed to have.
The one negative would be the tv over the bar but even that is smaller than most and not as in your face.
We will be coming back often!!

Two of us ordered the risotto of the day, Poulet Cordon Bleu (going old school for a change of pace) and a Caesar salad. Everything was well-prepared and reasonably-priced. The service was friendly and competent, as was the pacing of the courses. The room was quiet and attractive. Perhaps, most important, La Fontaine is one of the few places on Castro St. serving European cuisine, let alone French, at reasonable prices.

All in all. We had no surprises, good or bad. Just a pleasant neighborhood restaurant that we'll return to.

Note that three stars is not a bad review for me. Three is my average score for a "good" restaurant, which I believe is how the scale is supposed to work. Others seem to grade on an easier curve.
they need to add more variety, especially with pastas. Choices are dated 70's and 80's.

The service was excellent. They greeted us; immediately brought our daughter crayons, a special cup, etc. Accommodated all requests for a smaller spoon for our little one, etc. Very gracious. To me, service is AS IMPORTANT as the food, sometimes more important. We weren't blown away by the food. My husband enjoyed his meal, I had the special arugula/truffle oil salad which was very good. My pasta (capellini pomodoro) was swimming in sauce, but it tasted good. Good bread. The gelato seemed a bit stale.

Wife and I went to la Fontaine for my birthday. Being a vegetarian I was glad to see many choices for me.
I was tempted to try them all. Tried a few and liked them all. ;)
Lighting and music choices were so so. But the waitress service was very good. She was very courteous and even out dessert on the house for me (b'day).

Overall a good choice!!

I took a friend for a birthday lunch this week. It was a quiet, blustery day on Castro St and the restaurant was not as busy as usual. Service was warm, friendly and quietly celebratory -- our server whisper/ sang a happy birthday to her bearing a complimentary desert. She was thrilled, the food was delicious - light yet flavoruful, and we left feeling pampered and a indulged. What not to like?

We go here every week for dinner and the staff already remembers us. There's a reason for why go here so regularly: the experience is consistently very good, and the prices are moderate. Some things to try:
* The grilled octopus (appetizer) is one of the best things I ever ate, and it is *that* good every time. Seriously, buy it.
* Carmenet reserve chardonnay is my favourite wine so far (I'm by no means a wine snob, but I really like this one - it's similar to the chardonnay from Willam Hill and from Artesa wineries in Napa).
* The best dessert is Profiteroles - pastry with warm chocolate on the outside and cold ice-cream on the inside. They're delicious.

What a gem of a restaurant. Love the food, staff and owners.
The goat cheese appetizer is off the charts.
Looking forward to getting back soon.

This appears to be a relatively new restaurant on Castro St. in downtown Mtn View. We tried it not knowing what to expect and were pleasantly surprised! Welcoming staff, attentive service and good food. My date had the Salmon Wellington and I the Spaghetti and Meatballs. We shared the La Fontaine arugula salad in advance and found it one of the best we had ever been presented: not too sweet dressing with pomegranate seeds.

My husband and I enjoyed our anniversary dinner here on Saturday night and could not be happier with our experience. The atmosphere was enjoyable - romantic, charming, and peaceful. The service was very professional, friendly, and prompt. The food was very tasty, well prepared, and served piping hot. It's nice to experience French food without breaking the bank too. The owner was gracious enough to offer a Profiterole dessert on the house for our anniversary celebration. We will be coming back again to this ideal location on Castro Avenue in Mountain View.

I was in the area on Friday night and made reservations for dinner at 8:00. I am unfamiliar with Castro Street area, so I went in a bit blind. I liked what I saw on the menu and made my choice. I was a bit underwhelmed. The service was fine, attentive and friendly, the food was just so so. My companion ordered the chicken penne which was clearly the better choice, I ordered the chicken saltimbocca and was rather disappointed. It consisted of a pounded chicken breast, topped with a few sage leaves and a slice of what I believe should have been prosciutto, but it was round and then covered in a brown gravy. It was accompanied by a very small quantity of mixed vegetables and mashed potatoes that just did not taste good.

We have been trying all the restaurants that interest us along Castro St. in Mountain View, and La Fontaine was on that list. We are glad we tried it and we definitely will go back. What we found amazing was that there really was a dish for everyone (Salmon Wellington for me, spaghetti and meatballs for my husband, Coq au Vin for one friend and Seafood Linguine for another; I was very happy that the Wellington pastry was so light and thin and did not overwhelm the salmon). The other thing we liked was that there wasn't too much food on each plate; we find many restaurants slop lots of food on a single plate and that isn't appetizing to see. Each of the four of us was very happy with the plating of our meal and with the taste.

Food was great but they have a live singer on Friday night so it was hard to have an actual conversation at dinner. Would plan to go at a different time next time so that the singer isn't there. He's not bad but just not what I wanted when out to dinner.

First time here.  Service was good and attentive.  Food was tasty.  Soup dumplings on point.  Pot stickers very good.  Congee was good needed a little more flavor so the white pepper they brought was a good balance.  Meat skewers a bit chewy/fatty.   But will be coming back to try the shabu shabu which looked good.

The hostess/waitress explained our options carefully and made useful recommendations. Food arrived hot and reasonably fast, service was friendly and efficient. We greatly enjoyed the scallion pancakes that came folded over with a choice of savory stuffing -- we had beef, shrimp, spicy beef. Had never seen anything like it before, except perhaps a taco. The Xiao Long Bao, shanghai soup dumplings, were excellent. All in all, a varied menu, some originals, great execution and service.

We are so happy this place is close to us. Our last 2 visits the food was outstanding compared to other skewer places. They have a wide variety of food and amazingly each item we ordered was tasty. We loved the minced beef porridge, the chicken thigh (soooo hard to find tender & juicy ones) and chicken skin skewers, har gaw (shrimp perfectly cooked and seasoned which is also rare), and I can't remember the other items we ordered but I know it was all enjoyable. The service was personable and efficient. We were late to our reservation and they seated us right away and we needed to attend a show nearby and made it on time because of their excellent service. We were surprised how reasonable the bill was because we find the food to be higher quality and cooked just right. We'll keep choosing this place over other skewer/dumpling places in the area.
The beef tongue skewers are INCREDIBLE. We ordered more mid meal. The service was also lovely and you get to try a lot of different foods for a price that’s SO reasonable!

Food was delicious, and service is great. It was not a typical grill place, where you cook your own meat, which for some reason was what I expected, but otherwise it was perfectly seasoned and had a great selection.
Great local dumpling restaurant.  Cannot miss on the menu but our favorites are chicken thigh with wasabi, pan fried dumpling and scallion pancakes.  Fantastic vibe, friendly, kind staff.

We really enjoying eating at this Redwood City downtown restaurant.  We find the food to be really good and reasonably priced.  The service is outstanding, they are very attentive but not overly intrusive.   We eat here at least once a month.  If you haven't tired, it you should really go.
Work lunch. Great food and super service. Thank you!

This was my second time at Brochette, and just as good as the first time.  My son especially enjoyed the fish congee.  It had big chucks of white fish that were nice and tender.  The bulgogi filled grilled rice ball was also very good. And by of course, the skewers were delicious.  We plan to visit often.
Great food! Enjoyed the atmosphere as well. Dumplings are phenomenal and are a work of art. Highly recommended.

Parking a little tough. Very nice looking place on the inside.   Not many customers at noon on a Thursday so I’m wonton they are not catching the downtown lunch crowd but the delivery business was hopping.  Super friendly and courteous waitress.  Dumplings were excellent: plentiful juicy and yummy interior.   Two bites large. The takoyaki was nice but a little too rich.  Overall, I would return.
Seems like mostly frozen food. The fried foods was overcooked and seems like oil was old and used beyond its prime. Beer was cold though,
Great place! We had a blast and the staff was super nice
Delicious!  Loved everything, had spicy dumplings, pan fried soup dumplings, pork ramen and wagyu beef tataki.  Can’t wait to go back!
Excellent food, service, vibe. Great for hanging out with friends or a date night

Overall good experience. Some of the food was excellent, Dumplings and umami, pork belly etc.
potstickers and okra I would not recommend.

Great experience overall. Dimsum and skewers were all executed perfectly. Cannot recommend this place enough. Everything we ate and drank was exactly what i was hoping for when i ordered. the manager Kaniel made great recommendations and was clearly passionate about the food and committed to making our experience great. We left full and had plenty of drinks. the bill was lower than we expected for the quality of the food and drinks. I can't wait to go back

We really love going to this Redwood City downtown location.  The food never disappoints and the service is really great.  Our favorite server (Kaniel) is always welcoming and provides exceptional service.  If you haven't gone here yet, you really need to check it out!
Wonderful assortment of familiar and novel pot stickers, sushi, skewers, and more.  We have yet to order anything at this restaurant that we did not like.
Great local dumpling house. Highly recommend for great food and service.
Great for our 8 person work team happy hour. Took great care of everyone. Very kind.
Excellent vibe and service. Delicious food. Highly recommend
We really love this place - great service and great food - our favorite server Kaniel is OUTSTANDING!
Very good but no bar, no fancy alcohol free drinks, no fancy teas. Very casual. The congee is worth going back for.
This place is fabulous. I've returned many times, and it's always been great.

We had such a lovely time everyone was so nice and the food was very unusual and beautifully done. Everyone was very gracious. It’s a cute, relatively small place with an open kitchen and lovely options. I really liked how you could review the menu and just check off what you like and kind of do a tapas style. The pricing is reasonable and it’s easy to park.

The food that my wife and I had at the Brochette and Dumpling Grill was excellent!  The wait staff was very attentive.  We can't wait to go back to go back and try some more items off of their menu.  Lots to choose from.👍👍

We have eaten at this location several times and continues to be a great place!  Everything that we had has been yummy.  The wings have great sauce, the siu mai is amazing, chicken kaarage, chicken thigh with yuzu.  The service is so good and the location is welcoming and pleasant.  If you haven't tried this place, you really should -so glad they are in Redwood City!

This is a great addition to downtown Redwood City.  The food was authentic and tasty.  We were served promptly. The price was reasonable for the quality. The restaurant had a comfortable atmosphere.  We were there on a Friday night and most of the tables were occupied, so that's a good sign of popularity.
What a treat to try this spot on Main Street in Redwood City on Christmas night! Our food arrived quickly to our table and was piping hot and delicious!
This place has become one of our favorite places to have dinner in Redwood City.  Food is great, service is exceptional!
They were out of a few items and the food was not very good.
What’s not to like!  Asian “tappas” forever. Some thing for everyone on this menu. The sake service is really special order a bottle of cold sake, and see what Amber does with it!

Really enjoy the restaurant, food is terrific.

Last night was loud with children not being managed well.

We've been twice and ordered different things each time.  Food is cooked perfectly and good selection.   Love the happy hour with reduced price appetizers and wine. 
Inside of restaurant is nicely appointed, clean and calming.    Service is very attentive.   We'll be back!

Great food from a diverse menu.  Amazing combination of flavors and formats for delicious appetizers and mains.  The service was a bit slow / erratic but friendly throughout.  All the tables were full and there were only two servers so they may have been short-handed.  Despite any service issues, no was heading for the door unsatisfied.  Definitely recommend Brochette and Dumpling!

Great experience! The dumplings here are awesome. We’re so happy to have a good dumpling place in Redwood City. I recommend the soup dumplings and chicken/mushroom. My daughter loved the edamame, miso soup and side of tofu.

Nicely appointed restaurant, service was very good, food was excellent!  Loved the Happy Hour offerings.   Napa cabbage & pork dumplings,  Har Gow,  Wagyu, pork belly skewers had a nice smoky flavor.   Pork and shrimp pot stickers and wonton in chili oil.    All very good - not one thing we didn't like.   The topper was the Black sesame seed cheesecake!
Will be coming here again! Great food, nice ambience and service.
Terrific place.  Food was great.  Staff was friendly & courteous. Wish the food came a bit quicker but the wait wasn’t too badz

name: Steins Beer Garden
description: Steins Beer Garden is a modern American take on the classic German biergarten!With spacious indoors and dog-friendly patio seating, we proudly feature 31 taps of craft beer, exhilarating craft cocktails, and an excellent variety of American Gourmet Comfort Food from Executive Chef Eduardo Andrade.Through our Made-From-Scratch house dishes and deep appreciation for the highest quality of ingredients, we always strive to bring forth an exceptional communal dining experience.See you at the beer garden!
hours:
Lunch and Dinner
Mon–Thu 12:00 pm–9:00 pm
Fri 12:00 pm–10:00 pm
Sat 10:00 am–10:00 pm
Sun 10:00 am–9:00 pm

reviews.text: Always good food and good service.  First time for brunch today and it was very good.  Very tasty and well presented.
They were very accommodating for my allergies.

I’ve been going here since it opened and not once have I been disappointed.  I heard it was closing so I went with my family one last time.  Then we heard it was being bought out and it will continue to operate.  This is great news and looking forward to enjoying Steins for longer.  One request, please bring the lasagna back.  This was really good and wondered why it was removed from the menu.
food and drink, atmosphere were amazing and want to visit there again
Goodbye Steins! You will be missed. Thanks for all the memories.
We're going to miss this place. It's always been a great, dog-friendly place for brunch, drinks, or dinner.
Worst service!! So slow, didn’t come to check on us throughout the meal, etc.
Nice selection of beer.  Good food. Friendly people.  Plenty of parking on a busy holiday.
Love the varied beer menu and the hamburger was delicious!
Amazing experience at this place! What a beautifully located by the pier. They have excellent schnitzel! The cocktails are a die for.

It was my first time eating at Stein's Beer Garden, and definitely won't be my last.  Portion sizes are very generous and the flavors pop.  Their fish tacos were absolutely delicious.  My husband had the chicken tenders which I thought were very good.  They were tender and fresh, not overly seasoned.  I could tell they were hand battered and not received frozen and pre-manufactured like those served at most eateries.  

Service was also impeccable.  Daniel was our server and showed us just the right amount of attention -- neither too much, nor too little -- was friendly and had a great personality.  Thank you, Daniel, for the great service.
Great food, service was  perfect, reserving for another Sunday  already .
Delicious food and I loved sitting outdoors!  The staff was terrific!  Will go back soon!!!
Good drinks and atmosphere. Not impressed with the food.
The outdoor patio is lovely. Service was great. Food was just okay.

We visited on a cool night, so the patio (which would have been my first choice) was not attractive that time. Inside, the ambiance is good - but the noise level is tough; even the server mentioned it (couldn't hear us ordering).

The menu is diverse and interesting and the prices not unreasonable.

The service was very accommodating (allowing one of my guests to make multiple substitutions. But the service was slow. And when my guest asked for bread, we initially got a yes. But then no follow-up. Then we asked a busser. He got our server back (at least 15 minutes after the initial request). Then the server stopped by and said the bread would come in another 3 minutes. Nope! It was at least another 10 minutes. And the server didn't warn us of the charge.
My guest who asked for the bread is the slowest eater in our group, so the delay in serving the bread (a simple request!) really destabilized our timing.
Had been looking forward to dining here for quite some time but was very disappointed.! We should’ve just gone to In n Out, where the food would have tasted better and been much cheaper!
The food was really good.  The waitress had to be asked for the dessert menu and my ice tea and water were never refilled or topped off.

The service was poor. We sat outside at an empty table for at least 15 minutes, before asking to move inside. Then we managed to get drinks, but went to the bar to get our own water. After the food finally arrived, we had to ask again for silverware and napkins. Not a great dining experience for what was supposed to be a Father’s Day celebration. Will not return anytime soon.

Our server was fine but he had NO help. This lead to our drinks sitting at the bar waiting to be brought to us for 25 minutes. Not only did this happen once, but twice! The dining room was 1/2 full, the bar was empty, and we watched as staff walked by our beers just sitting there getting warm. Even the bartenders were just standing around most of the time. When I brought this issue to someone’s attention, they said they’d let the manager know, but no manager ever came by. I

The food was good but not good enough for us to ever come back here with so many other options around.

name: Khazana by Chef Sanjeev Kapoor
description: Sanjeev Kapoor is one of the most influential chefs in Indian cuisine in the 21st century. He has been awarded the title of ‘Best Chef of India’ by the government and has received the Padma Shri, India’s highest civilian award, for his culinary contributions and for elevating India's presence on the global culinary stage.
hours:
Mon–Thu, Sun 5:00 pm–9:00 pm
Wed–Fri 11:30 am–2:00 pm
Fri, Sat 5:00 pm–10:00 pm
Sat, Sun 11:00 am–3:00 pm

reviews.text: An absolute tour de force! We enjoyed four different appetizers, two main courses and one dessert plus three drinks. The creativity and quality of the food was amazing! Looking forward to our next visit!

The food and ambience were outstanding - everything was very tasty and they were very kind to our party of 8 (two families with a bunch of kids) - the presentation is also top notch and the table service is really good - many staff, all well spoken, attentive and careful

The only thing I'll point out is that when families with kids ask for something to be made less spicy - please have better answers than: "oh the spice is already there", "we can't make much change", etc - instead do better and see how you can provide an alternative or a less spicy variant - this is a fancy restaurant - we expect the chefs/kitchen to be flexible - we're not asking for custom made to order off menu items - we're just asking for simple moderation/modifications to existing menu items that honestly other restaurants have zero issue with
Great food and service. The food had creative touch and did not sacrifice the taste. Glad that it was not too much fusion!

The server at our table was very very nice. She was friendly and did a good job explaining everything.

Food was also good quality and tasty. I would have preferred more flavorful, but not more garlicky. Actually, that is what I liked that the vegetarian food was not overly garlicky.

The food was fine. I had the pani poori was different tasting, than regular pani poori. I did like the presentation. Overpriced for Indian food, but known given it was Sanjeev Kapoor’s restaurant.

I was just fascinated that the waiter did not check on me to order food, after eating my appetizer. I waited about 25-30 minutes, and just gave up and handed them my credit card to close out the bill.

Oh well.

We had higher expectations from Khazana. The food was average, as was the service. From a value for money perspective, it wasn’t great, because there was nothing in the experience that was outstanding or worth a special mention.

Had dinner at Khazana last week. We have been wanting to go there since it opened because we have been to the Yellow Chilli in Santa Clara a few times and loved it.

The service was top notch. The staff paid attention to us without being intrusive.

We ordered vegetarian food and everything was just very delicious. We ordered Chana Jor Garam and Ricotta gulati kebabs for starters and they were both awesome. For the main course, we had sham savera kofta (actually invented by Chef Sanjeev Kapoor) and baked cauliflower mussalam with garlic naan and lacha paratha. Dessert was carrot pudding tart. It was mouth watering.

Will definitely come back soon.
Excellent food. Service tonight was very erratic and slow. Lots of waiting for my drink and also for the food.

Excellent food and good recommendations by the server. Service was a little slow considering the place was not crowded but we really appreciated that chef was able to make a Paneer dish for our son without nuts. The ambiance was quiet and chill and the dark lighting made the experience very private. Wonderful dinner and will certainly be back to try the other things on the menu.
food was tasty, portions very small - overpriced.  spinach cheese dish better
Good food. Extremely slow service. Our drinks arrived after appetizers.

The service was mediocre. The food was good. When they cleared the first course my fork was taken away. When the next course arrived I asked for a fork and no one came back with one. I waited and finally managed to finish my meal without a fork as it was naan.
When the bill arrived the options for tip were only 18, 20 and 22 or 25 % or no tip.
There was no option for custom tip. When I asked the hostess she said the Square company wouldn’t give them that option.

If the restaurant hopes to be tipped 18-25%, their service has to match that.
The Food quality was good but was a bit on the pricier side. We tried the paneer tikla, prawns, sham-savera and home style chicken curry with butter and garlic naan. All items were tasty.

Too expensive. Had chicken pepper, Amritsar fish, pepper mushroom and steamed rice. It was $115. Had no drinks. Also, options for tipping was no tip, 18%, 25% etc. A choice of custom tip wasn’t there. Restaurants shouldn’t force customers to pay. I usually pay over 18% tips but it shouldn’t be mandated.

Food was awesome, had small plates and large plates. Everything was unique, tasty and enjoyable. Matthew our server was helpful. The Manager checked in with us and was kind to substitute a drink for one of the table guest. Overall was a good evening. Big shout out to the entire team at Khazana
Not a great experience that I hoped. Food is ordinary for the price, servers not interested in quality customer service. Overall disappointing experience

Vishal and Mathew make this restaurant an exceptional memorable experience!
Will return again soon!
Thank you for giving us a great experience

Good things and bad things. Ambience is great. Food is very beautifully presented. Service is very decent. Food taste is so so.. medium, quality, Indian and very spicy. Given the great choices for Indian in the Bay area, would avoid at these prices.

Tasty take on Indian food with innovation. Timely and friendly service. Good lighting- better than most places!
We will be back!

Good place, tasty food, good service.
Only neg I felt that place was a bit cold and bathrooms were not clean.

We had an amazing dinner here. We enjoyed every thing we ordered which came without much delay. The vibes are modern but not pretentious and the food is real indian without being trying to be innovative and crazy.
Great food and best service. This was our second time eating there.
The food was hideous. We are vegetarians so may be it was just us but the food was bad
Great place for a special occasion. We were there for our 30th wedding anniversary. A good choice of dishes and drinks. Service was prompt.
Initially we were assigned to seat near front lobby and we were not comfortable but we requested the staff to make us sit in the back; decently good. Ambiance was good.

This was our first time at Khazana. We have been to other modern Indian cuisine in Palo Alto and are a big fan. The food at Khazana beat our expectations. I would highly recommend the assorted papad to start along with some small plates. We tried the Verki chicken and Lamb chops. Both were perfectly cooked and spiced. Spiced for flavor not heat. Then we tried the signature dish Shaam Savera just cause this was the dish that made this chef famous. Along with Garlic Naan (best i have ever had), it was a great experience. To finish we had the Gulab Jamun and yet again this was the best version of this dessert i have ever had. The service was great, ambience is good though the internal decor could be better. The food is amazing and definitely worth the price. Complements to the chef for recreating such traditional flavors with a modern touch.

I was really hoping to love this place, but the food fell way too short! The service was really good, the place is pretty and feels upscale yet not uptight, but all that got overshadowed by the mediocre food. We had the edamame pani puris, jackfruit tacos and veggie biryani and all three were very very basic. They were presented very nicely but the flavors were bland. I wasn’t expecting authentic Indian flavors because it is a fusion but nothing really hit the mark. I hope they improve the food. I will likely go back one more time and try something else to give them another chance but won’t be top of my list, sadly. :(
Nice ambiance, decent food, good service. Pani poori, Khichadi, Shrimps, Daal, Breads were enjoyable. Would be trying Chicken tariwala next time we visit this place.

Very bad experience!! The food was not that great. Cost was very high. The restaurant was very very very noisy. The chairs were extremely uncomfortable. The temperature setting was not good. The service was average. The waiters were very nice , but service was mediocre.

Loved the food… everything we tried was delicious .. great service … employees were polite and friendly. 

The only thing we found disappointing was “ kitchen open item charge $5 per person ( cake fees ) as they had to serve the cake we took to celebrate the birthday of a family member.
Excellent flavors and great service. Definitely be dining there again

Very small quantities for the price you pay. Same sauce and chutneys for all appetizers. Very limited options to chose from.

Not worth the money you end up paying for the quantities you get.
Unnecessarily pretentious. Average tasting food, average service. Great location though

We went with a little higher expectations and were disappointed. The menue was short as expected. The food was of average quality. The staff was less attentive than expected. There was not much to choose from for desert. Overall the experience was underwhelming. I think the restaurant can de better.
Wow awesome went for my anniversary dinner loved it they also treated us with a cheescake surprise

some dishes did not make sense. burrata saag did not work. amritsari fish was mostly onion tadka. biryani was average. sadly tandoori roti was burnt.  raita was made of greek yoghurt - too thick. jackfruit taco was good.
Food was average and overpriced for what it was. DIfficult to get waiter's attention.
If someone makes a reservation in advance, please ensure that the table is ready at the agreed upon time.

I had made dinner reservation for last Friday at Palo Alto Khazana indicating that the occasion was my birthday. When we dined, neither was this acknowledged with wishes not was I offered a complimentary treat that is typically done in other restaurants. For a high-end and pricey restaurant I would have expected this basic courtesy. It was my special day and I had many other options to celebrated but I chose them.  When I brought this up with the lady at the reception after dinner and while leaving, she seemed apologetic and offered to make amends and do better next time. The manager though didn't demonstrate any remorse. She had a 'yes-it-happened-but-can-we-move-on attitude offering a discount next time. When I said I may not be back, she just sighed and left.

The service and hospitality lacked warmth. Food was okay but not matching the price. Definitely it was many levels lower than their other Bay Area one, Santa Clara Yellow Chilli.

I was reviewing the reviews of last week and observed ratings had gone down drastically with many negative feedback. So there's something to be analyzed and attended by the management.

I'm a big fan of Chef Kapoor's cheerful shows and delectable recipes and this experience was disappointing and left a sour taste.
Excellent Indian food.  All the dishes we ordered were lovely both in taste and to look at.  Closer to authentic Indian food than other restaurants in the neighborhood.

We were really enjoyed the decor and ambience of Khazana.   The food was good for the most part, some items better than others, however, the main items were good.  It lacked a bit of depth or flavors and didn't feel unique or special, as I would expect at that price point.   There was plenty of waitstaff, however, very little interaction with us.   A few dishes needed some explanation, as we didn't know what they were and there was no offering or concern for us other than taking an order and delivering.   Not a great overall experience with regard to overall feel.   This is a restaurant that needs someone to asking if there are questions about the menu, etc.   Otherwise, lovely atmosphere and good food.
Standard Indian food that was cooked well, but lacked the special twist I would expect from a chef of this caliber.

Khazana by Sanjeev Kapoor comes with a lot of expectations. Unfortunately, my recent visit to the restaurant left me with mixed feelings.

The staff were polite and prompt.The food was very basic, lacked the flavors. Service was not bad.

For the premium price point, the food did not justify the cost. While the portions were okay, the flavors and presentation didn’t leave a lasting impression.

Restaurant seems to rely heavily on its brand name rather than delivering the exceptional culinary experience one would expect. It’s not a bad choice if you’re nearby and craving Indian food, but it doesn’t live up to the hype or price tag.

Would I return? Probably not, unless there is significant revamp in menu or execution.
It was a great experience. The food and ambiance were awesome.

We were delighted with our dining experience at Khazana.  We are avoiding carbs so ordered dishes that focused on meat and vegetables:  Peanut slaw (delicious, crunchy and fresh!), chickpea fritters (4 per order - delicious with great chutney sauce); Eggplant bharga?  Not sure the name but the preparation and sauce were incredible and not bitter or too smokey) and the fish tikka masala - absolutely fabulous. .

Only gave 3 stars for service because no one waited on us for about 10 minutes after arriving. But once they attended us the service was excellent. Appreciate that we could sample the wines available by the glass to decide.  Hope they will consider adding Belgian style triples and golden ales (Like Pranqster) to their extensive beer menu which go great with Indian food. Sadly the beer menu was focused on hoppy, bitter IPAs and lagers.  The cocktail flavors were exotic and fun (loved the Saffron Negroni). Will definitely come back to try more of the menu.

Review for Khazana

I had high hopes for Khazana, but my experience was disappointing. The food was far from what I expected—it lacked flavor and freshness. Surprisingly, even the waiter seemed to acknowledge the shortcomings. At one point, he casually suggested I might enjoy dining at another restaurant instead (E***n in Palo Alto) 😉While the ambiance was decent, it couldn’t make up for the poor service and subpar cuisine. I don’t plan on returning, and I can’t recommend it to others either.
Papaddum was moist and they just refried it even after asking them to replace. Food is average for the price and options are very few to choose from. Menu was confusing for main course.

Really great experience! I didn’t pay for the food, so I’m not sure about the value. Our server was great, but she forgot a few things which is a little annoying. But overall, I really like her she made our experience better. ￼￼

I left my scarf there in the seat of the restaurant!
Wonderful service!
Our friends enjoyed!
Loved the food and the ambience. Super unique twist to Indian dishes

We ordered Bedgi chicken which was delicious. Veg Galouti kebab was also soft, could have been little more flavorful. Loved the garlic naan and the mango butter chicken. Was disappointed by Mishti Doi. This dish lacked flavor and texture. It was not curd like but rather chenna like. No jaggery,sugar etc made it very plain and bland. I have had misti doi in multiple places and this did not meet my expectations at all.

We booked this place to celebrate our anniversary dinner. Upon arrival, my wife picked a table for us to seat and the waiter mentioned he was going to set the table up and asked us to wait near the lobby. He then went busy on a phone call. Another couple entered and sat at the table my wife picked up while we were still waiting. The waiter finished the phone call and when we mentioned what just happened he had no solutions to offer. We had a very bitter experience and had to walk off. The experience felt absolutely disrespectful.
Well crafted and cooked dishes. Good portion size - not too small and not too big. Creative cocktails and a decent wine list.
Nice Ambiance and great service. Food was disappointing.
Great food but service was very poor.   Drinks did not come until halfway thru the meal although it was ordered right at the beginning.   The overall service level needs to improve.
Excellent food. Probably the best I have tasted in the Bay Area.
Matthew hosted us really well! 5 stars to him! Authentic food with a great vibe. Rooh and Etta has some serious competition!

Was excited to try out a new place, but apprehensive about how it might stack up to similar options in the area. Fortunately, it overperformed—will certainly be back for more. Delicious food, particularly the Mango Butter Chicken. The presentation on the Puri is also innovate and cool. Recommend for sure!

Overall very mediocre food for the price. A lot of hype, but unfortunately failed to deliver. The starter chicken had no spices. Just a like warm chicken piece. Overall the food can be had at other places for half the price. Won’t be going there again.
Overall a great experience and great food. Everyhting was perfect!!!
We loved some new dishes like papaya salad and the sea bass.
Fusion Indian cuisine. We had the Panipuri, Jackfruit Taco and Chicken with silver leaf. All were delicious, well presented. Service was excellent. We were there for lunch.
The food was delicious, the drinks were amazing and the service was very nice.

All in all we were pleasantly surprised. The food was between 3 and 4 stars - a few things (like the mango butter chicken and small plate tiger prawns) were excellent, others were fine but nothing special. The service was excellent, our waiter was attentive and explained everything well. They haven't done much to the restaurant since Joya was in the location, but it was always a nice space so that's fine. Prices were high (to be expected on University Ave in Palo Alto) but not outrageous.

I liked the ambiance a view of University Avenue, and the service was attentive, but the food was too spicy for a non-Indian.  I thought the spice covered up the real flavor of the food, or the spices were just off.  At any rate, I don't have a real desire to return.
Excellent authentic Indian cuisine with great service!
Below par.  Food was terrible .  I ordered Amritsari Fish and lamb.   Naan was cold.  Service was slow and poor.

Overall, the food was tasty, though it was a bit difficult to know how much to order. In the end we had three small plates (appetizers), two large plates (entrees), a daal, two naan, and two rice (sides) between four adults. We could have had an additional large plate.

The service was friendly but on the chaotic side. We ordered drinks (two servers tried to take our drinks order) which took quite a while to come; then we had to summon a server over to take the food order. One of the small plates came out quickly, the others didn’t appear till plate one was finished; then our large plates arrived while we were still on the small plates. We felt mobbed: people were trying to take the small plates away, others were delivering the large ones, and at least one (maybe two?) other servers were trying to extract our small eating plates and swap in large ones while at least one of us still had food on her plate! Teething troubles, I’m guessing.

The space used to be Joya, which was our favorite restaurant in Palo Alto. It doesn’t look very different now. The drapes have been removed which has increased the noise level.
Food was decent but service was very slow. Even drinks order took 20-25mins. The chickpeas patties were my fav and the vegetarian Biryani too

We arrived for our reservation and were asked to wait 5 minutes to be seated. That’s fine. I asked for indoor seating and they placed us on the corner of the threshold between the restaurant and open air sidewalk window. Not the end of the world. We waited 20 minutes to have our drink order taken. Getting frustrating. Our appetizer and drinks came out in a reasonable amount of time, but then we waited almost an hour for our entrees.

We’re a pretty patient crowd when it comes to restaurant-going, but I worry something is wrong at this restaurant if Thursday night treated us this poorly. The owner did comp our cocktails—and seemed genuinely apologetic for the delay about 45 minutes in—but I still feel compelled to write about the experience because it seemed maybe one member of the whole staff was looking after us. To wit: Our water cups were never refilled a single time.

Hopefully these comments and experiences are taken under advisement by Khazana and major improvements are made.
We enjoyed the drinks, the appetizers and the service, especially the excellent service at the bar. It was noisy and the main courses were not as good as the appetizers.

For Palo Alto standards- disappointing service experience. Server messed up order, waited for food for over 40 mins. When asked on order status, almost next moment dumped all cold food at the table. Food taste was ok. Will not be visiting again!

The food presentation and taste were top notch at Khazana. However, rhetorical service speed could’ve been better. I felt it was a little sluggish. The staff was very polite, friendly and courteous. I feel they need more staff to manage during peak hours.

2nd time visiting within 5 days. Enjoyed the food. The first week of opening, service was overwhelming,2nd week was good but not great. Had to signal many times for some one to notice that we wanted to order more bread. Overall very good and good food and cocktails. Will return again
Excellent food, service was a bit slow. Overall great experience

Great new restaurant..Loved the food!! Our server was really good with recommendations based on everyone’s preferences and dietary restrictions!! Great ambience as well. Not cheap, but well worth the $$$
Staff still learning but food was was good and location is nice

Khazana was a decent experience for us. We had ordered Pani Puri, Paneer Tikka and Gulab Jamun. The dishes left a lot to desire. Pani Puri was nice. However, the other dishes didn't taste good. We had higher expectations for sure.

The service was impeccable, though. The servers were super attentive and available at all times.

name: Benihana - San Mateo, CA
description: At Benihana San Mateo, California, our food is not only cooked it’s choreographed. You’ll find a dining experience unlike any other! Our guests are seated at a communal hibachi grill tables in groups, where your personal chef will perform the ancient art of Teppanyaki. Our chefs will have you craving for more as they slice and dice your meal before your eyes. Highly skilled and well-trained, your personal chef will entertain you as they cook such favorites as steak, chicken, seafood, and fresh vegetables in traditional Japanese style. You can enjoy sushi and sashimi prepared by a talented sushi chef and indulge in our famous, award-winning signature hot sake or a specialty cocktail.
hours:
Mon–Thu, Sun 11:00 am–10:00 pm
Fri, Sat 11:00 am–11:00 pm

reviews.text: Same Benihana as others. Service was good and good was the same.  Great place for families to celebrate special occasions.

This is the 50th anniversary of the first time we went to Benihana!
Still not tired of the show as you eat your dinner.
Of course, we have a new generation of artist, just playing their skills. Gone all of the old Japanese wizards and replaced by a younger generation. our chef is two months into his journey and still has all his fingers. Maybe we will see him in another few years and see how he’s improved his skills. ￼
Food is still the same taste, and of course the prices have kept pace with the times.

We had the traditional 5 course menu, filet mignon and Yakima with chicken.  We understand that it just recently opened but there were not enough servers.  Ours went on lunch during our lunch and no one took his place.  The chef did his bit what they're trained to do, like clinking the spatulas  and the standard onion volcano.  The filet mignon was dry and overcooked same with eh NY steak at the seat next to me.  We told the manager and he told the chef to go ahead and make us a new order and make sure that it is medium well.  We appreciate the attention to our request and to make our experience a better one.

My husband and I had a nice lunch at this new Benihana restaurant. We had eaten at several other ones and were very excited when they opened this new one. I was extremely happy to not have to wait the typical 45 minutes we usually have to wait even with a reservation. We had an early reservation (11:30) though. However when we left (12:50) there were swarms of people waiting.

Dixon was our chef and he did good. He opened with the standard fork and spatula toss and dropped them a few times (as well as the shrimp tail toss) however he was trying his best and was pleasant. He cooked our food the way we asked and that was more important.  Azad was our server and he was excellent. He was very polite and attentive to our every need.

I especially enjoyed Roger who stopped by to see how our experience was. It was a nice touch and showed the management cared.

The average main dinner entree is $40. I’d be fine with it if the food was high quality and delicious, but it wasn’t. Majority of the price must be for the ambiance and experience, which is high energy. I wish Benihana the best but the food is definitely overpriced. If you’re looking to treat your family to a once in a while special dinner, there’s definitely better value somewhere else.
The staff needs more training.  Maybe wait a few months before trying it out.
