Nothing serious but worth noting.  I doubt we'll return or recommend.  Disappointed for sure.

Have enjoyed dining at Camper several times in the past. I made this reservation for my mother-in-law's birthday, and let the staff know in our reservation notes.

Unfortunately we were seated in the back room of the restaurant, which has none of the ambiance we've enjoyed in the past at the restaurant. I had confirmed with the staff to put a candle in one of our desserts so we could sing happy birthday- then, they forgot to do it.

Overall, a lackluster dinner, and I wouldn't return for a special occasion in the future given many other great dining options in the area.
Rock star chef, love the fact that they have several veggie-forward entrees.

Absolutely love camper! Such a fantastic local gem. Always happy to see some of the special seasonal changes to their menu. We typically go for dinner, they have a wonderful outdoor patio area that is not overly noisy, just the right amount of ambiance. Food is always delicious no matter what you get, 10/10 would recommend.
Great food and drinks. Host was kind enough to comp us free dessert because our table was not ready in time for our reservation. Would go back again soon.
We were there for brunch.  Very limited menu. Quinoa bowl was bland.  Avocado toast was good.  Overall underwhelming. Been here for dinner before and that was better.
Food was good but a bit pricy for the portion sizes. Pasta was delicious.
Perfecto!!!

Modern space which is nice to grab a drink (pretty bar), but the dining area was quite loud.  Food was under-seasoned, presentation was fair, and our table commented that the server did not seem to enjoy his role.  There is a lot of competition in the area and they may need to slightly improve in some areas to make it a place to want to return to.  It has the bones...just some tweaks.  We sadly will not be back.
Really cool atmosphere, the food is amazing and very creative. This kind of place is really rare in the Bay Area. So happy it landed in my neighborhood ;-)
Cute find in downtown Menlo Park.  They have a large pasta selection and some interesting cocktails.

I’ve had good meals here in the past, which makes this meal particularly disappointing. I ordered the pasta with crab because it’s in season. I’m not exaggerating when I say there might have been one half ounce of crab. I couldn’t even see it at first. Pasta portion itself was small as well. $56 for one glass of wine and a puny portion of pasta.
great new place in Menlo park . the food was delicious . only think our fried chicken sandwich was very dry . but we will definitely  come back to try dinner …
Noisy, terrible service, food came out randomly, moderately ok food, overpriced for what we had

The noise level in this restaurant is just oppressive. You have a very hard time having a conversation at our table, and that forces everyone to raise their voice, and it a viscous circle. The noise level really killed the meal for our group. And a $300 bill for 4 people should afford you an enjoyable experience. Wines by the glass weren’t great,
They’ve improved so much! I’m thrilled.
Great place for a good dinner with an old friend.

Camper was amazing. Be prepared for a really noisy ambiance that makes conversation a bit rough. Food and service excellent. We'll be going back for brunch and sitting outside next time to avoid the noise.

Love the location
The food is delicious 
The staff is quite attentive 
Would like more peacefulness-a few soft murals to muffle the noise in order to have converse 
Overall, delighted it is in our neighborhood
Wonderful service and fantastic food from beginning to end.

I went to Camper two times a few months apart giving them the benefit of the doubt. I was disappointed. Started with the cheese plate but due to an error on the menu it is meat OR cheese. So we got a plate of salami. Cod was dry and badly seasoned. Burger was pretty good but fries were very overcooked. Inedible. Chocolate chip cookies were undercooked and took 20 minutes to get them.
great craft cocktails, and interesting and seasonal ingredients.

Hard to believe that a restaurant can continue to get better and better, but each time I visit (I've been at least 8 times) by expectations are exceeded. Always something something surprising and delightful.  Unique flavors. Fresh.  Wonderful staff.  How lucky we are to have within walking distance of our home.  Long live Camper!

I love this place. The bar is great, the burger is one of the best I’ve ever had, and the pastas are creative and fabulous. The staff makes an effort to get to know you and greet you by name. I plan to be a regular

Overall it was a great find especially since we are Vegetarians.  The menu is quite interesting and varied. Definitely a place for foodies regardless of your food  interest. Will definitely return.  The service is superb and the waiter was very helpful in explaining the various menu selections.

This neighborhood spot is my favorite place.  I eat here often but Chef Greg is constantly adding new things to the menu so it's always a unique experience.  The staff is knowledgable and kind and the drinks are delicious!

First visit for NYE dinner... AMAZING from beginning to end!! Our server Sonya was spectacular! Attentive and funny, she was knowledgeable about the menu and had great suggestions.. from appetizers to desserts we were not disappointed! Will definitely be back!

Service with Robert was excellent on Christmas Eve. He paired wine and suggested appetizers that went well together. Enjoyed the burrata with the Shishito peppers. It was the perfect balance. If you can’t take spicy, remove the seeds from the peppers. For the main entree we had a squash pasta that was really tasty (so good that I ate it all before taking a pic)  and a fried rice beef dish. The ingredients they use for everything tastes fresh & uniquely different. (Example: Hot Cider = two thumbs up) 
Dessert: molten lava cake. They used to have a s’mores dessert that was really good but they sadly removed it from the menu.

Great
Nice wine comments
Good solid menu with really good food

Service was a little slow and we had to ask to order appetizers.  Main courses were disappointingly bland except for the burgers and fries.  Menu looked good but unfortunately didn't deliver on taste.
Wonderful experience.  Highly recommended!

I don't review restaurants often and these days most people just leave reviews when something is bad. In this case I had to give the great folks over at Camper a huge THANK YOU! I had dinner at Camper this week and it was one of the best meals I've had in a long time. The menu is so diverse, there is something on there for any eater. The burrata, short rib fried rice, cheeseburger and caramelized custard toast were standouts for me. We had many cocktails that were all delicious and a bottle of wine from their extensive wine list that was perfect for the meal. The service was impeccable and the overall meal was one that I can't wait to come back for. Thanks Camper!
Delicious food and friendly atmosphere. Mussels are the best!!
The food was unexciting and the menu very limited.  I was unimpressed with the portions for the money. VERY noisy and challenging to hear the person seated right next to me at times.
Wonderful food and generous portions in a trendy setting.

I really wanted to love this restaurant.  It has a promising menu in a great location with prices that seem justified for the locale.  However, the food just didn't quite hit.   The appetizers were good but not exceptional (Shishito peppers, ahi).  We had the beef dish and halibut entrees.  Again, they were fine, just not great.  The fish was cooked well, but was bland, begging for some acid and salt.  The beef was beautifully cooked, but the jus along with it had an almost burnt taste to it.  The drinks and service were great and they never remotely rushed us out as the last guests there.  There is a great opportunity to elevate this good restaurant into a great one.

Food was generally excellent except for one main course which was a bit bland, seemed to lack just salt and pepper.  All other dishes were excellent. Fantastic desserts. Great waiter and staff. Highly recommended.

Thrilled to find Camper as unique and tasty as friends suggested. The menu is filled with original dishes and the bar and cocktail menu look very exciting! (We were there for early lunch, no drinks this time.) We gobbled up  4 different entrees and two appetizers—loved the deviled eggs and beat salad especially. All great in a delightful, simple but elegant, camper decor. Thanks Liz and Logan, so wish we lived nearby, we’d be regulars!

We had a perfectly delicious meal at Camper last night but what I really want to praise this restaurant for is their service.

Sonja was our server and not only did she answer our questions about what to order with clear honestly (and not trying to up-sell to pad her tip),  but she went above and beyond for us when it was clear we were having a less-than-stellar night (for reasons having nothing to do with Camper).

Her attentiveness and kindness was deeply felt by both my and my husband and even if we had no reason to go back for the food (which we do and will), we'd go back to see Sonja again.
Pasta wasn’t as al Dente as we’d like and the fish was a little fishy
Fabulous food and service.  Noisy but ambience otherwise great.

This was my second visit to Camper after an underwhelming first visit. This visit was better but there were still some opportunities for improvement, in my opinion. 

Our server was lovely. However, he didn't know the difference between vegan and vegetarian. The menu identifies vegan, gluten free, and dishes that contain nuts. They DON'T identify their vegetarian dishes, for some reason. I guess that wouldn't be a problem IF the servers knew what 'vegetarian' meant. I first asked if the dish: Green Curry Risotto, Coconut Milk, Red Veined Swiss Chard, Vadouvan, Paneer, Crispy Leeks was vegetarian. It appeared to be but I thought I'd ask to be sure since it wasn't stated as vegetarian. The server replied that it was not because it contained paneer, which could be removed. I explained to him that paneer is cheese and qualifies as vegetarian. He looked puzzled. So I then asked if the dish: Rosemary Herb Dumplings, Pt. Reyes Bsy Blue, Toasted Walnuts, Brown Butter, Bosc Pears was vegetarian. Our server said he didn't know and would need to check with the kitchen. He returned and informed us that it was NOT vegetarian because it contained Pt. Reyes Bay Blue Cheese and Brown Butter. I almost got up and left at that point. I truly couldn't believe what I was hearing. They are charging 20+ dollars for these dishes and neither the menu or the server could tell me if a dish is vegetarian or not. I understand that English may not be the first language for some folks, which is great! We need more diversity. But this cannot be the excuse, especially if we're talking about a server in a restaurant that can be trained to understand the difference. Also, dishes were not explained to us as they were delivered. A young woman delivered the chicken dish to our table and simply said, "Here's your chicken" and walked away. Open Table isn't allowing enough room to go into the food, which was okay. The stand-outs were the drinks and the burrata, squash, persimmon salad. Excellent.

Ok who serves 4 tiny tortelli for that price? Ridiculous and embarrassing. No idea that it would be that small and too late to order anything g else. I have never in my entire life complained about portion size. Salad was nothing special. Hard to eat actually.
Cool and hip ambiance for Menlo Park. Food and drink were pricy. Food wasn't bad, but I would have expected food considering the prices. Drinks were expensive and heavily iced.

Nice menu and great seats outside between the sidewalk and the street. Food was good, not great. Certainly not memorable. In my opinion, a bit overpriced, but a welcome addition to the dining options in MP.
Chef Greg is the best! Everything was delicious and the service impeccable!
Good food in a very loud environment. Just be careful when you pay and make sure they don't overcharge you or make you pay for something they said is for free for a special occasion.

This is our favorite local restaurant.  Prices are reasonable, food is very good and the service and Managers are excellent.  We feel at home and welcomed every time we dine here.  The wine and bourbon selections are great and the mixed drinks are very creative.  Currently, the Sangria w/mission figs is a real treat!  My only minor complaint is that I believe there should be more salt to season their creative food!
Amazing everything. HIGHLY recommend :)
Everything was great. I was additionally impressed when one of the wait staff came over and asked how ever thing was. It turns out it was the owner.

Camper has a warm, relaxed, but sophisticated vibe. Great cocktails, fabulous farm-to-table food. Amazing desserts. Staff is knowledgeable and  attentive without being overbearing. We tried fish, pasta, duck, cornbread appetizer. All were delicious. Chocolate molten cake is a chocolate lovers dream.
My sister and I enjoyed an amazing lunch at Camper.  Very creative and delicious entrees.  Staff was attentive and able to modify my lunch to accommodate a dietary issue.  GREAT PLACE!
Great healthy yet filling salad quinoa, squash, eggs A++++
Sophisticated, inspired, well executed, and unpretentious.

Our server was rather busy so he didn’t give us enough attention like when my meal came out rather lukewarm while my companions was steaming hot, he was no where to be found.  My friends meal was supposed to be sans mushrooms but they were all over.  Our server noticed after he came to clear her dish.  The bowl of a million not so great olives should be removed from the menu.  No one could eat this many and frankly they weren’t very tasty.  We were both happy with how our meals tasted but I don’t think our meals, drinks, etc were worth $185.
The restaurant was very cold and dark.  Service was a bit slow.  Food is overpriced for the portions.  I want to like this place, but am disappointed the times I have gone.
Bland food and poor service, plus expensive. Won’t go back.

The place was hopping on a Saturday night, and the service was a little ragged but cheerful. The creative menu slightly exceeds the execution, but you will each well enough. Not as good as Protégé or Bird Dog, but not as expensive, either.

This is our third time to Camper and I have really enjoyed it. My chickpea vegan meal was outstanding! My husband said his burger was fine and our friend said her chicken was only okay. This is why the 4 star rather than 5. The peppers and cornbread appetizers we ordered were excellent as well as our salads. Wine list is very good and we had a very friendly and attentive waiter.

Energetic is a clever word to use to describe a noise level that impedes conversation.  Give me a break.
The food was not outstanding.  The risotto was undercooked and the sauce drizzled on it was not described on the menu, as I remember and contained a hint of heat, which I did not want.  The arugula salad was so meh.  Any number of enhancements would have been welcome, such as toasted pine nuts, herbs, other greens or vegetables.  Just endless  bites of a bitter green that needs excitement and softening.  The cornbread was fine, but nothing to write home about.  The cost of l25 for a  steak is ludcrous: I can get it at the local market and the farmer's market for one fifth of that and cook it to
perfection.  Camper is approaching the mindset of Silicon Valley:  lets make as much money as we can
without the substance, and make hype the path to those goals.

The staff was great, the ambiance very nice. Generally all three of us found the food to be just OK. It was not super flavorful or interesting and the steak helping was pretty small. Maybe thats the foodie way but not mine.

"I guess some people just like bland food?" my wife said, trying to explain the crowds and the 4-star Yelp rating for Camper. Everything about this place was pretty uninteresting, and it didn't live up to our expectations. 

We got the cornbread, chorizo rigatoni, and flat iron steak, and two drinks. It ranged from "meh" to "not good." It was certainly not worth the price. 

The bread was bland and uninteresting. It came with butter that was sweetened and peppered, but accidentally had some whole peppercorns that made my wife gag. 

I didn't like the rigatoni, but my wife did. We agreed that it tasted similar to simple pasta with meat sauce you could make at home. 

The flat iron steak was alright, but not particularly appealing, and it came out cool instead of hot. My favorite part of the meal was the tomato and pesto sauces which came with the steak and tasted good on the potatoes. 

I had the old fashioned, which seemed safe, but it was sour and had a lemon peel. It was much closer to a whiskey sour than an old fashioned, which is usually sweet and has an orange peel. I like creative cocktails, but this one didn't taste great and seemed like a big miss. 

I think the service was alright aside from bringing the steak cold. The ambiance was fine, but nothing special. 

I just can't imagine coming back to this place, especially at these prices. You could get an amazing meal in a one-of-a-kind atmosphere at Bird Dog or Taverna for the same cost.
It's a place to go eat, and the food is pretty good, management and staff are great, but it's not a "wow gotta get back here soon" kinda place...

I was in Menlo for a short visit and choose to have lunch at Camper based on a Michelin 2019 recommendation.  The restaurant did not disappoint.  In fact it was so good we returned for  dinner.
While everything was tasty and beautifully plated I have to give a shout out to the Chickpea Panisse with Tunisian Spiced Carrots, the Garlic Chive dumplings, the Tomato Carpaccio ricotta salad and the Halibut Crudo. I could continue raving about the food but feel remiss if I don't mention the atmosphere and staff. Everyone working at Camper were friendly and professional. The design is casual and there is a feeling of warmth and calm to the place. A wonderful culinary experience.

Was really an awful food experience. Menu looks interesting but everything is truly poorly prepared, tasteless and very disappointing particularly given the prices. Spent 100 per person. We went for the server recommendations.

Tomato salad with chorizo was truly mush. Chorizo bits seemed like burned croutons. No flavor whatsoever.  Shishito peppers were undercooked do not uniformly crispy. Tasted like eating semi cooked peppers- tough.

Their dill gnocchi - tasted like over cooked tatertots.  In fact we asked the sever if it really was gnocchi. Dry - tasteless.

The potatoes crusted cod tasted old and fishy. Was dry with again no flavor.

I’ve had better frozen dinners than this meal. Was a birthday dinner for a friend and was so sorry it was SUCH a cruddy food experience.

Seriously question if there is a chef in the kitchen.  

Advice - avoid at all costs.
Food was excellent, service was outstanding and I highly recommend
Too noisy in the restaurant- couldn’t hear well at all!!
Amazing!!! Best place on the peninsula!!
Vibrant environment with a nice bar and well-made drinks. We love their pastas.

I would definitely go back at least once- and suspect have a better experience, but we made a reservation at 8:00 and weren't sat til just about 9:00 which was shocking. We were happy to sit at the bar, but usually if you keep somebody waiting for an hour you'd at least comp them a drink or something... there was only the most superficial of apologies from the hostess for the wait which was frustrating. That said, we'd give it another shot because everything else was great!
Took my husband here for his birthday.  Food and service were wonderful; couldn’t have been better!  My only complaint is that the noise level was so high we had a difficult time hearing each other.
Awesome food (burgers are out of this world, as are the drinks and desserts). Server was knowledgeable, patient and friendly. We were a group of 9 and thoroughly enjoyed ourselves.
Loved it!  The food was great, the service was outstanding, and the desserts were devine!
I had mussels outside and I felt like I was on vacation. Thank you Camper!
The food was great but both of our entrees didn't actually have what the menu said was in it.

The menu at Camper has mostly off-the-wall offerings all at extremely high prices.  The only entree my wife & I found interesting was a cheeseburger & fries for $20.  The fries were very tasty, and I enjoyed my burger but my wife thought it had a gamy taste.  
     Service was adequate and the ambience was average, but I doubt I will return to Camper.  Two burgers and one ice tea should not cost $55 with gratuity.
Hands down the best restaurant in Menlo Park.
Go at Happy Hour or lunch for better value. A bit pricey for Menlo Park.

A delicious, creative night out.  This restaurant has truly "upped" the dining scene in Menlo Park.  Fabulous cocktails, every bite of food special, fun to share.  Casual but sophisticated and smart environment.

I had heard many good things about this restaurant and was looking forward to trying it.  The setting is lovely and it had reliable service.  The menu seemed to be a stretch for something unusual - one dish seemed like a candidate but I was not familiar with 2 of the ingredients and had to ask the waiter said he was not familiar with two of the items noted.  I ended up with the fried chicken which the waiter recommended.  The batter did not seem seasoned at all and I did not find it to be particularly appetizing.  The overall dining experience was nothing more than acceptable.  Having heard such great things about the restaurant, I was disappointed.

Very enjoyable eating outdoors.  Service was very nice also, and food was good.  We were pleasantly surprised with the small “balls” of the impossible chicken.  The hamburger was fine but not memorable.  Our friends were very happy with their entrees. We gave 4 stars instead of 5, because while everything was good, the food was not as memorable as some meals, and we reward memorable meals with a 5.

The restaurant has a nice atmosphere albeit somewhat loud on a Saturday night.  Cocktails were well made and tasty. We ordered 4 plates to share. The Duck liver pate had good flavor and taste served with apricot jam and two brioche pieces of toast.  The field greens with stone fruit had only 2 small slices of fruit. The hamachi crudo had 8 small pieces of fresh tasting fish with dotes of avocado and several cucamelon pieces which were unique and tasty. Overall nice presentation but small for $17.  We then had a corn agnolotti that was by far the best tasting dish of the evening.  Unfortunately, after 4 dishes we were still hungry and ordered a second pasta dish, rigatoni with house made bolognase that was fair.  Good food that unfortunately is overpriced for the portion size.
The food was very good. The noise level was way too high! Could hardly talk!

Disapointing. The food was average (all on the menu it all looked promising), the service showed up when to take an order and deliver a bill. This was especially dissapointing as we needed a few things during the meal. The ambiant noise level is quite high, making it hard to hear yourself, much less your dining compainion. Would not go back. It might be quiter eating outside.
While the food was very good, the wait staff needs improvement.
Team dinner from work
The food was good and the service was ok - it feels a little expensive for something that is a nice experience but not more than that.
Some great pasta on the menu and good basic dishes.  Salads were huge. Service getting wind was a little slow, but friendly and accommodating

The place is what downtown Menlo Park was begging for. Fresh food. Creative and interesting combinations. Lots of seasonality built into the menu. Great flavors. Something for everyone.  Reasonably priced (great value).  

Staff is warm and friendly - nothing pretentious. Efficient. It's a lot like its town. Well done. Understated.
I really love this place, especially the pastas.
Go for lunch for a quieter atmosphere. Outside seating is elegant.

Gorgeous space, delicious food and cocktails.  They have wonderful outdoor seating for al fresco dining as well (it was  full already so we couldn't partake, unfortunately).  It can get a bit loud inside, but overall, we really enjoyed the ambiance and our meal.  

Will definitely go back!
Wonderful imaginative food, absolutely loved it
The first few times we had dinner there, the food was wonderful. The last 2 times not so. I ordered the trout. It was really dry. The creativity has gone down along with the quality

I'm kinda on the fence about this place, it's still a bit uneven.  The French Omelette that I had was OK, but nothing memorable.  Friend's hamburger was outstanding she said.  When I've been here before it's been OK but again nothing to rush back for.  Others have said great things though so will keep trying.
We sat outside and it was absolutely lovely and much more quiet than inside!
We enjoyed all the food items. Everything was delicious and beautifully prepared. The shishiti peppers, the steak, the trout, and the olives were all phenomenal.

We had dinner at Camper. We ordered appetizers and a pasta. The string fries were DELICIOUS! The clam dip was greasy and not very flavorful. The hummus was good but not earthshaking. The bolognese was also greasy and rather flavorless. My husband enjoyed his "old fashioned" drink and I liked my lime gimlet! The ambiance was nice and the place has a great little area outdoors on the street as well. Overall, the food would keep me from coming back. Too bad as the menu looked good and we had high hopes.

Amazing meal. 
From the moment I walked in I knew I liked this place. It is has warm beautiful light and welcoming service. The hostess welcomed us with a warm smile. The food is farm to table and everything we tried was delicious. Burrata is a must have.  The pastas are made in house and out of this world. All the favors are great. All in all I would highly recommend this place and plan to come back quite a lot.
Excellent burger but the salad was so bitter! I could not take a second bite. Waiter was very nice and attentive. Thank
The food was excellent and the services was quite good.   The cocktails were creative and quite good!  I'll go back again.
The menu had a wonderful vegetarian dish.  We ate outside, nice to have that option.

Our first time here.  Very good food.  Bring a sweater, the AC was really cold.  Service could have been better.  Waited a little long to order.  Appetizer arrived but salad never did.  Again, food was very good so will try again.
Met the chef. Engaging talented person. Everything was fabulous. I particularly liked his weaving of subtle smoke flavors. We over ordered but loved everything. Looking forward to returning

On a hot evening, we chose to sit outside and there was still a fair amount of car traffic at 6pm.  The food lived up to its past, I'm a repeat customer.  The hamburger is a perfect, quick, dinner to split and they do it so nicely.
Every course was delicious, creative, and beautifully assembled.
Need a few more places like this in Menlo Park! Brings in great food, cocktails, ambiance and superb service!
Food  (rock cod and rigatoni) were excellent.  Would give 4 & 1/2 stars if I could.  Wine was too pricey in my humble opinion.

We were prepared for something really special; the website looked modern, the menu looked eclectic, and with plenty of varied options.

However, the food did not live up to the promises of the menu and environment. Ultimately we were disappointed.

Well decorated , nice ambience, strong waitstaff but  disappointing food. Burrata appetizer came on very burned toast and was a mix of too many flavors. On the other hand, rigatoni entree came with watery pasta and a very bland tomato sauce. The corn agnolotti entree was delicious but very sparse. A disappointing experience overall.

Highly recommended.  Upscale, but casual - pricing is very reasonable.  Food was really excellent - one of the best pastas I've ever had!  Great top shelf bar with innovative cocktails.  Desserts are not to be missed.  Service was fantastic!
Extremely loud! We could not carry on a conversation.
Nice place with really unusual menu. We all enjoyed the different things we order, and the service was very good.
I was there with a friend for lunch. We were quite happy with the service and the foods we had were delicious.
Went for our wedding anniversary - staff was great. Shoestring French fries were really good, hamburger was good. Pudding was awesome and comped for anniversary. Will return regularly.
Incredible quality. Imaginative combinations (but NOT weird). So fresh. The menu is highly seasonable. Totally unpretentious...but amazing. Priced perfectly.

The Bahn Mi sandwich would have been excellent except there was very little porchetta in it.  The melon soup was good although I’m not super wild about coconut and there was a coconut taste from the coconut milk used.
Phenomenal
Food was just not great, both dishes. Salad was overdressed and pieces of lettuce way too big. The quinoa was soupy

Food was quite good, but service was spotty at best. We had to wait sometime before ordering and then bread was brought out as an after thought just before the main course. Dessert menus arrived before we were done with the main course.

This was my first visit to Camper, even though I live just 10 minutes away.  It's a nice combo of  neighborhood informality, an interesting menu, an above-avg wine list, and a moderate-noise atmosphere.  Excellent and knowledgeable service.  Dishes extremely variable in the end.  I will go back, at lest once more, to see if I can zero in on really successful dishes.  Wine list is much stronger for reds than for whites, but corkage is also reasonable, so taking your own bottle is a fair proposition.
Very enjoyable. Great food, excellent service. Will definitely go again!
Second time there and my Nashville hot chicken had no “hot”.  Breading was super heavy, greasy,  and under seasoned .  I think there are great ideas in the menu but lacks execution. .
Fantastic place, food was excellent and the service every bit as good

There was a small mess-up with the preparation of one of our dishes - related to cooking hardware, not the chef. This was fixed quickly and a complimentary dessert was provided. Food is excellent and fairly innovative. Service very attentive. Noise was a problem - we are an older couple who try to talk instead of text (which we do in the right setting). Noise was the low point. Portions very large, so the price, though high, might be reasonable.
Excellent staff and food... the best....
The charcuterie board was fantastic! We enjoyed a few appetizers and pasta. The place wasn't too packed or loud for an early Saturday evening.
I thought the food was bland and not worth the money. The bucatini was FOUL.
Seasonal, fresh, and yummy menu. Lots of love put into the ingredients, space, menu and meals. Fun bar as well. Check them out.

We met friends for dinner on our recommendation (after we had lunched here). We started with the olives (which weren't quite as good as they had been for lunch), the Spanish White anchovies which were considered very good by the person who ordered them) and a double order of the meats and cheeses which was a single large hard cheese and one type of charcuterie which disappointed our friends, still very good. Two of us had the grilled squid and pasta with fresh basil pesto. Our friend thought the squid portion was a bit sparse. My wife had the Portola Valley Sweet Corn Agolotti which she liked a lot. Our other guest had the hamburger which she enjoyed very much. Dessert was just sorbets and gelato, the pistachio was declared the winner. We shared a bottle of Neyer Chardonnay and a French rose from Provence, both were excellent with the dinner. The service was very good as it had been at lunch, used items disappear with very little intrusion. Things are very fresh tasting and when dealing with fresh, they can vary from visit to visit. My wife and I were happy, our friends a little less so.
The food was excellent, thoughtfully sourced and a nice menu mix. Welcome addition to Menlo Park we wish them the best of luck!

We had a most enjoyable dinner for a birthday celebration. The owner came by and was most gracious. It wasn’t cheap but it’s the best restaurant we’ve been to in this location. So we’ll be back next time we need a special place. The dishes were creative with just the right size portions. The food was plated beautifully. I really enjoyed my steak.
Food was bland and overpriced
I had a juicy, perfectly cooked burger with the best fries!
A great addition to Menlo Park.  Food and service were top notch!  I hight recommend it!
Excellent service, food was very tasty. My guest loved the quinoa salad. My pasta tasted great but the pasta was a bit overcooked and mushy.
Burger was just okay! Service, felt rushed. Get them in and out. Server never returned to pepper my salad.
Had great expectations but found that it was overpriced for very boring menu --- unexciting and very disappointing dining experience
Menu and food preparation was amazing.  We had gone once 6 months ago and thought it was just 'OK' but this time it was one of the best meals we have had on the peninsula.
Such tasty and fresh food.  Every little ingredient is unique and wonderful and adds to the overall flavor profile of the dish.

It was our first time and the decor was so nice that I had high expectations. We decided to sit outside because inside felt pretty stuffy and the food was just okay. I'm pretty sure the waffle came with margarine instead of real butter and the pasta didn't taste homemade, even though the server said it was. Nothing was bad, but nothing blew me away either.

Outside brunch was delicious!  The açaí bowl is incredible. Fruity. Healthy. Hemp seeds. With a Sightglass Coffee,
Sunshine and friends, I dare you to find a better brunch in Menlo Park.

Service was slow on Saturday afternoon - probably short of staff.  I have eaten at the restaurant almost every month for the last few months, the food is generally very good and staff were attentive and helpful on previous visits.
The appetizers came fairly quickly, but it was more than 40 min before the main courses came. The place was packed (which is ok) but the kitchen couldn't keep up.
Great spot for lunch. Dessert options were limited though.
Everyone was very nice only the waiter didn't fill up my water glass often enough.  Not a big deal but hey, you want a review.
Excellent food, service and friendliness. A bit noisy fir conversation. We felt like we Needed to shout to be heard

We had been wanted to go to Camper for a long time, so we were looking forwarding to seeing what they were all about.  Our experience was mixed, but we are looking forward to giving it another try.  Some dishes were good (corn bread, burrata and asparagus, cheeseburger, and Gnudi).  Others were meh (green salad, shishito peppers, bucatini with spicy sausage).  Service was very good and wine list had nice options.  We sat down at 8:15pm, so we closed the place out on a Saturday night, so this is a regular Menlo Park local restaurant.  We will try other things when we go next time and get a more full picture of what they are really good at executing.

Great New Addition to Menlo Park Scene
Upscale restaurant with unique selection of farm-to-table dishes.  We had interesting appetizer dish of pickled beans, strawberries and other things.  Main chicken dish was outstanding.  Fish offering was also fabulous.  Not inexpensive, but in par with other nice restaurants in the area.  Highly recommended.

We had wanted to drop by Camper since its opening and we went with some friends for lunch. It was a nice day, so we opted for the outdoor seating. Our waiter Ron was very polite and help in choosing our selections. We started with the olives, which were an amazing assortment of different olives in oil with spices sprinkled on top – sooo good. We tried the chilled asparagus soup, the quinoa bowl, the pork belly sandwich and the chicken Milanese sandwich (they come with fries or with a side salad). I had the fish stew, which had at least six types of fish and shellfish in a light tomato broth – delicious. The desserts (ice cream and sorbets for us) are made in house and are excellent: the hazelnut chocolate was voted best, but the pistachio and wine reduction sorbet were close contenders. We resolved to come back for dinner to try some of the other items not on the lunch menu. Very fresh ingredients with cuisine influenced by several food cultures make this spot worth a try.
Perfect lunch spot to catch up with a wonderful friend.
So delicious! My favorite was the bass and the garlic aioli sauce that came with the French fries!!! How can you go wrong? I literally licked my plate.
Food was good, received incorrect food 3x.
We sat outside and had the freshest salads!  It was a spring day both outside and on our plates. Thank you Camper for an outstanding lunch.
Not sure why they can't get the burger temp right but we have tried endless times... Overall great for the area but should be much better...

Been going here since it first opened. A big city class restaurant in Menlo.  Fantastic food that is both nostalgic in the taste buds while working with new combinations and fresh ingredients. Highly recommended. Oh, and love the staff.
Fine experience, little pricey, interior a little blah cold surfaces- loved the natural light!
I was pleasantly surprised. I wasn’t expecting much giving all the input I’ve been getting. I thought the menu had enough choices and the food was creative and tasty
Good food, interesting flavors, good cocktails and good location.
Everything was ALMOST good, attention to the last detail was evident in most dishes.  The hostess was on her cell phone at the doorway the entire time.  Expected more
Bad service, bad food.

Nice menu items that are generally well prepared and good cocktails. We tried one outstanding pasta with one of the most unique and complex flavours I’ve tasted in a while. The restaurant has an almost-cool atmosphere - definitely one of the better in Palo Alto/Menlo park but the lighting in the bar is too bright and the tv lowers the bar.

Ambience is great; food is horrible; waiters look like they want to be somewhere else. 
Mixed cheese/charcuterie: Safeway quality
Gnudi with ricotta: so much salt couldn’t finish
Burger: again too salty
Angus beef: ok
Panna cotta: messy

I love this place.  I especially love the people who work here.  They are very thoughtful and friendly, thereby adding to the already great atmosphere and food.  There's a little something for everyone on the menu.
Delicious food- we enjoyed eating on the patio

A friend recommended this restaurant, so I went there for dinner. I read the reviews. Hard to believe I was at the same restaurant. I ordered the “deviled eggs”. (Maybe I didn’t read the menu/description of the dish) I was expecting regular deviled egg, but instead got 2 cold soft boiled  eggs sitting is a sauce and sprinkled with some kind of seasoning. They just didn’t Taste right. We ordered 2 pasta dishes. I ordered the pasta kale pesto dish with pinenuts.  The noodle were over cooked and sauce lacked flavor. This wasn’t a cheap meal either. I will not be returning.  On the plus side, the service is good. :)
Great menu.  Great food.  Friendly staff.  Bamboo straws (environmentally friendly).  Decently priced meals in a generally expensive area.
Noise level unbearable. Food was not to our liking. The pino Grigio was horrid.

Cool atmosphere, but found it nearly impossible to have a conversation due to the noise level. May be best for couples and very small groups, but I won't bring clients again. (Sorry, and no offense intended.)
The service was attentive without being annoying.   The food was delicious, well seasoned and perfect.  All in all a great dining experience.

We were excited to visit Camper, a bustling American Farm-to-Table bistro.  Our pastas and salads were excellent.  Unfortunately they were out of the lamb, which is what we chose first.  The dessert was a killer chocolate bombe, which topped off meal beautifully.  A tad noisy, but except for the hard, glassy surfaces, the ambiance was cozy and the food took center stage.  We would return with pleasure.
My first time there.  Great atmosphere and food.  Fairly low noise level. Great drinks.

The food was hit and miss, one meal good, the other two not so good. The server forgot one item we ordered. They have a 5% surcharge for Healthy California. This is a deal breaker for us. We are all for health care and paying employees, but not with a surcharge. Tell your customers upfront what you are going to charge them instead of surprising them at the end with the bill. Besides, how do we really know the surcharge goes to what the owner says it will. Transparency Camper!

We had tried this restaurant out only 2 weeks earlier and were impressed with the selection on pasta dishes.  Took a friend back with us and was disappointed to see only 4 options for pasta.  I know the menu is set around seasonal items but pasta is not effected by seasons.  What happened?

At brunch, this is a place where you can enjoy the food AND the company - the noise level and ambiance
are great for a meaningful catch-up, and the service was superb.

We were so excited about the new addition to a pretty stale restaurant scene but were incredibly underwhelmed by chewy two strips of iron steak. The Harissa was the best part of that dish.  The lamb was okay but the side of cabbage was boring and I didn't touch it.  The burrata was ambitious but didn't feel cohesive.  The corn bread tasted like something I would get at the Santa Monica pier, stale and flavorless. The drinks were good but not enough to return.  So bummed.

We were looking forward to trying Camper but our experience was only somewhat satisfactory.  The staff was pleasant  . The food however was mediocre.  Our salad was good and plentiful...we shared it but I had the chicken and it was unremarkable. My husband had one of the pastas and the sauce lacked originality. For the amount of money, it was not worth it.
Delicious food, knowledgable servers, and really yummy cocktails with a focus on fresh local ingredients.

I have had dinner at Camper several times and it is always fabulous.  Had lunch there yesterday for the first time and it proved to be every bit as good as their dinner service.
Camper is truly a treasure.

The lady at the front desk didn't smile or greet us when we arrived.  The service didn't improve when we got to our table and waited over 20minutes for a waitress to come.  The food was average at best - starting with the chicken liver pate and brioche - the brioche was so dry and over toasted it was impossible to cut, the salad was equally unimpressive.  The main courses lacked anything to distinguish them.  Coupled with the poor service it was not a night to remember and we will not be going back.

Surprisingly disappointing: food was ambitious but not delicious, service was fine but not especially good; noise level became distracting as the night wore on. It’s not the “go-to” spot I was hoping for.
Food was good service was lacking! Need to go back and try more things on the menu to give a proper review.

Excellent all around as always. Great food and atmosphere. The cauliflower soup was to die for - creamy and delicious. 
Love having Camper in Menlo Park.
The restaurant was freezing - had to wear my coat during lunch.  The food sounded interesting but didn't deliver on taste.
Sat in the backroom it has very little ambience. Looks like it’s used for large events. Service was slow, food was good. Took forever to get our drinks.
Our only disappointment is that the menu posted online was different than the restaurant menu.  Still was fantastic!
I want to love this restaurant but just can’t seem to. Food just ok.
Nice atmosphere. Dim lighting, casual, a little loud, but still a good atmosphere. Excellent food and wine.
The food here is very good. Bread is not included with the meal. But the noise level is too high to have a conversation.
Overall a great spot. Burger was quite tasty, pasta always great. Some inconsistencies between advertised menu and actual menu, but other than that it’s. Great spot

Food was average in taste, menu selections were good, however the price for the overall meal was not worth it. $82 for a small appitizer, 2 pasta dishes and a couple of drinks. Much better places to dine out there

3 of our entrees were very good, 2 were very bad. They forgot the candle in the dessert for our birthday party, but then I guess realized it later and wished us happy birthday! ? Wtf?! I come to a nice restaurant on a birthday to get a candle not to have the waitress SAY “happy birthday”. Overall. Poor.

Camper is spot on using seasonal local organic produce and local purveyors. We liked the Palak Panisse, buckwheat pasta and vegetarian asparagus entree. Chef Greg Kuzia-Carmel had worked at Cotogna, an SF favorite. Nice wine list and specialty cocktails. Service was good, but it would have been helpful if the server had recommended sharing some of the dishes as the portions can be large.  It can get very loud at peak times. Camper is good, but needs to edit and refine the menu and work on server training to be great.

Not only did our server seem like a novice but our first appetizer came out before our glass of wine arrived. The restaurant wasn’t packed so there’s no reason 2glasses I’d wine couldn’t be delivered to the table. My friend and I are both foodies and there wasn’t one dish out of 3 that we liked. The barrata has pickled veggies and the pickling flavor was too potent. The pasta dish was too al dante and should have been cooked 30-60 seconds more. The flavor of the pasta was mild and uninteresting, though the description sounded good. The cod was plane and VERY fishy. I love fish and could not even finish the small portion I had on my plate.  I have tried every new restaurant that opens up on the peninsula and think Campers is the worst. It is also over priced and pretentious to think they can charge $140 for a 2 person rib eye in Menlo Park. I didn’t try the rib eye but if I wanted one for that price I’d go to a steak house not Campers. I will not return nor will my friend.

I made our reservations well over a month ago and tagged my event as a special occasion.  
We arrived to Camper on time, yet they stuck us at the table near the restrooms, I had the green exit sign and the lights to the bathroom glowing in my face during our meal. 
For such a nice dinner, the lighting really soured my experience. The exit sign and bright bathroom atrium area is no place for a table - and no place to seat a party that made reservations well in advance.

Chicken mediocre - a few beans at bottom of vegetables best thing all evening.  Rigatoni bolognese was mediocre as well.  Corn bread was just weird - tasted deep fried(?).  Some nice local bread would have been nice.  Disappointing after reading good reviews.
Great food and service. Professional and friendly. A neighborhood favorite.

French fries and Brussels sprouts were excellent. The cornbread was cold and dreadful. The pork was very good, the fish only so-so. That chocolate dessert was superb. The staff was fair. They tried, but forgot one order, and brought our check together with the dessert, checking back to see if I was ready to pay it yet. In short, the kitchen is promising; the front staff needs lots of work.

We went to Camper after hearing good things about it.  Indeed, the food is very good, in some cases quite unusual, and priced comparably with other similar restaurants.  Service was fine.  The problem was noise.  It was so loud that it was nearly impossible to hear my partner.  This is not a minor issue, it is a serious one, it was unpleasant.  I realize that this is what produces vibe, but everyone was screaming - which of course goes with drinking more (probably a better profit margin) and so it's more like a bar scene where this may be OK, but not a mid-high-end restaurant.  This is not a restaurant to go to if you have any intention of having a conversation (maybe this is why so many people were just looking at their cell phone).  Unfortunately we won't go back, since I think the food is very good, and I can not recommend this restaurant to others.
Terrible service.
Food was great, one of the best in the area.  Definitely worth a visit.
We had a nice dinner for 6 last week and everyone seemed to enjoy the evening, the venue and the food
Another great meal, love the ever changing menu, friendly and attentive staff and never seems too noisy.

Was really excited to try this new spot and New American food is my favorite, but food was average and service was below average.  The server fumbled his way through the menu, cocktails were inconsistent, and all the dishes were bland except for the pasta we had.

Crudo = amazing.  Burrata = spectacular.  Terrific burger.  Brussel Sprouts done to perfection.
Earlier reviews mention loudness being an issue.  It was in the earlier days, but no more.  Great local spot.  Greg (chef) and Logan have it all dialed in.
A nice addition to downtown Menlo Park. It is a great place for food. It does get loud. The season all menu changes so you can try different things. The food is great with large portions.

The Staff and food were mediocre at best. I had the risotto and it was lukewarm and the shrimp was chewy. My friend had a very disappointing pasta dish. It was cold, over cooked and flavorless. She took two bites and refused to eat the rest.  The staff lacked personality and enthusiasm. We will definitely not be returning.
Very loud and hard to have a conversation

We had extremely poor service. The hostess finally took our order. No one checked up. We never knew who or if there was a waiter, and we in the end had to go to the mattress d’ to ask for our check. We weren’t sure who, if anyone, the tip would be for. It was a strange experience. One friend asked if my lunch partner and I were involve. It seemed so!

Took a dear friend here for a nice dinner. Had to wait for our table, even with reservation, but had a good drink at the bar. The food was delicious, well served, good moderate portion size, creative recipes. The dessert list was lacking for both of us, but other than that, we loved it.
Great good, great service, would love to come back!

Camper was FANTASTIC!  The service, the food, the ambiance!!!!  We loved the deviled eggs, the vegan house made pasta, the tuna crudo and the wine selection is awesome!  Definitely will be going back soon!
Service was awful, food was average at best, drinks were okay

I had the Chickpea Panisse and it was delicious.  The stinging broccoli, nettle pesto with walnuts was bright green and so brightly flavored.  The burrata had turnips and a smoked ham and the flavors were balanced and smooth.  My friend had the burger and loved it, and the fries!

Can't think of anything to rave about at Camper, although the hostess was friendly.  The service was good, not great; timing was a bit off and they brought our coffee without spoons and with a tiny cup of milk.  They did respond quickly, however, and brought spoons and a more appropriate container of milk.  Food was unexceptional - my omelet had too much of a too-rich sauce made with ricotta and herbs.  My friend had the fish and chips, which was good but not exceptional.  We got there at noon and they were out of the soup of the day already.  Decor is minimal, to say the least, but that is in keeping with their theme I suppose.  Prices were more reasonable than expected, though.  Perhaps we should have tried something else.
The food was excellent. The service was ok (food arrived before our wine, we nedd
Great food! Very nice place. Portions are a bit small.

I was really looking forward to going to Camper after my daughter went with her father.  She loved the rigatoni and kept asking to go back.  Unfortunately, the visit was very disappointing.  Our salad, soup and deviled eggs took quite a while to come out but we didn't think too much of it.  Then the leek soup was very good but the salad was not.  The menu says baby greens but the lettuce used was bitter and tough in spots.  The dressing was lackluster and did not hide the bitterness of the lettuce. I have never had baby lettuce like that.  The eggs were good at least.  Then we waited and waited for our main course.  We estimate it was 45 min from when we place our order.  The restaurant was busy but not over capacity at all.  The rigatoni did not disappoint but the pasta with crab certainly did. The sauce was good but there were only about 3 bite sized pieces of crab.  The risotto with clams was very salty and not because of the clams.  There were barely any clams in the dish.  We don't plan to return.
First time. Food was good but not outstanding. Will give another try
Service was slow, but servers were pleasant.  Food was quite good. Burgers and Chicken entree were very good..  Salad starter was nothing special but fine and large enough for 2!
My first visit to Camper and it was lunch on a Wednesday, so it's hard to evaluate. My companion and I both had sandwiches that were very good. I will return for dinner.

Had a reservation but we still waited for the table. Kitchen and waitstaff were slow. Had to ask for bread. Some portions are small, some large. Depends what you order. All food was delicious. Atmospheric is odd and concept confusing. Noisy. Won’t return. Just meh.

Amazing lentils served with  double cut Lamp Chops.
Generous salad portion to share, dressed perfectly.
Burrata melts in your mouth.
Ribs need work.
Cod main dish so so, breaded?
The highlight for our table was burger/fries
Lively noise level, good for groups
I was looking forward to trying camper, menu wasn’t impressive and actual meal was nothing to write home about.

Went here for Xmas Eve dinner and waited almost an hour and a half for our entrees. The worst was the fact that they served only half the table and the other entrees came 15 minutes later after half the table finished their meals. Same thing happened to the table of 4 next to us. Will not be going here again even though we live just down the street and took a chance on a new place.

Enjoyable experience for our first time visit. At first we thought it would be too noisy, however it worked out ok.  The corkage fee was $25 however if you purchased one of their bottles on the menu, then the corkage fee was waived.  This worked out very well.  We had the flat iron steak, pasta bolognese, and cheese burger with little gem Caesar salads. All very good, not too heavy, and the meat was very tasty.  We enjoyed our experience and will return for another meal.
The cheeseburgers were off the charts.  Good service.   A good place for a business lunch

The food was overall very good. The cheese and charcuterie choices on the menu need a little improvement. They were very uninteresting and overpriced for what you received. The pasta was not exceptional . The chicken and cheeseburger choices were excellent. Good food but not outstanding. The ambiance and service was excellent

Interesting tastes and textures. Excellent cocktails. Very noisy. My only complaint is the notification that a 4% surcharge is added to the bill so that management can give employees benefits. All of us in business give our employees benefits but we don't "share" the burden with our customers. Instead we create prices that cover expenses and permit a profit. The surcharge ploy is an ingenuous scheme to make items appear less expensive. This detracts from an otherwise enjoyable dining experience.

Interesting menu.  Execution in the kitchen poor.
Loud. Hard to hear server much less companion across table.
Everything was great except for the noise level—very loud.
Awesome food and great service
Still craving the burrata with artichokes. Cauliflower in a pasta that was delicious. Patê was like a taste of Paris. Corn grit peach dessert was incredible.

We had an early reservation and the restaurant was packed. The service was slow and the noise level so high we could not have a conversation.  The cheeseburger was best option. I recommend sharing items instead of ordering full portions for each person
This is what Menlo Park needed. Great ingredients, prepared well and high quality service.
A great new addition to downtown Menlo Park! Excellent menu, attentive service, beautiful set up and a wonderful atmosphere: Cool, fun, yet also cozy and welcoming. Highly recommend!

FIRST RATE, EXCELLENT FOOD AND SERVICE.  NEED TO RETURN SOON, NEXT TWO WEEKS.
ONLY PROBLEM, NOISE LEVEL IS VERY HIGH, POOR ACOUSTICS.  HARD TO HEAR AND HAVE 
CONVERSATION.  STILL, WORTH IT.
Great service. Excellent food prep with high quality ingredients. Varied menu with delectable options.
The soup and salad to start were excellent. Then...the pasta was overcooked and the short ribs were essentially a blob of fat. Service was fair. We won't be back.

Service was very good.  Food was good but not great. Very loud, had to make reservations far in advance where I would expect a better meal with that condition. Corkage was too high for such a limited wine list
The food was phenomenal! We kept ordering more items and each one was better than the last!!

Our server let us know that he had only 3 days experience at the restaurant. But in my opinion, he still should have knowledge about the menu. He had no knowledge about the cheeses being offered and then took about 15 min to find out a description of each. 
The chicken liver app I had was good. Nothing special, just good. But the salad my date had: the little gems- tasteless. We had to take the cheese off the cheese app we ordered and use it in the salad in order to get any flavor.
I had the spicy bucatini which was pretty good; it was surprisingly very spicy. Often a restaurant will say something is spicy and it really isn’t. My date had the cod, which she thought tasted good. It was supposed to come with bok choy. I guess they felt like the 3 pieces in the plate was worthy enough. For the price the fish dish was- I think they could’ve put a few more pieces of inexpensive bok choy. 
I don’t think we’ll be returning. 
I wish them the best of luck.

This was my second visit, and I liked it less than the first time.  I think it partly comes down to personal taste.  The ingredients and presentation are good, but some of the flavors just don't work for me.  For example, my salad was permeated with a strong flavor, maybe an herb or other ingredient in the dressing, that I didn't care for.  My husband's bucatini pasta was similarly overpowering, with a strong smoky taste.  The best part of my meal was the chicken dumpling soup, which had good, rich broth and interesting presentation, but which ultimately left me tired of sipping spoonful after spoonful of broth.  It was a lot of liquid and a small spoon!  I ended the meal with a cappuccino, which was scalded and bitter.  Couldn't finish it.  Service was fine, not remarkable.  Noise level was very high.
the food is pretty good, the service is a work in progress, but the noise level is so high that it  could cause permanent brain damage  - if you are over 30 and can still hear, forget about it
Awful in every way.   Service was horrible.  Took forever for food to come.  It was wrong and very salty.  Second time I have tried this place and will not go again.

Work in progress.  Wait staff missed on both of our orders (specified "no onions" came piled with onions), both dishes were undercooked.  Pretty expensive for "energetic", a bit cramped, and nowhere near perfect on the food front.  Sure it's hard to find good wait staff, but a comparison to another new Menlo Park restaurant (Oak + Violet) where the wait staff are much more knowledgeable, available, and get it right the first time.  And the $18 for a <6 ounce pour of an Oregon Pinot (served in the wrong kind of glass) is just too much, scares people away.  We'll try it again for the pastas and cocktails which sounded great, but this was not a good first impression.
noisy, slow service, overpriced, chicken came out ice cold, pasta was tasteless

I assume the service side will be worked out within a few more weeks, but the food is not so good either. We were 4 people, and one plate came out more than 5 minutes before the others. The actual fish was good, but it was thrown over the oddest selection of veggies and so much mint.
Points to the owners for not running completely full while they train staff up, but it was so loud at 3/4 capacity.
I had hopes that Menlo Park could get a good restaurant, but this one really missed the mark.

The new trendy spot in town, complete with overpriced food  in tiny portions. Yes, the food combos are creative, but to the point of trying to be too clever. The craft cocktails are inventive, but in a tiny highball glass (and for $15) I want a real drink that's not watered down by 3/4 ice. The ambiance is boring/plain, with too small/too close tables. Restaurant has poor acoustics and is very loud; you have to shout to be heard by your meal companions. The only plus I’ll give it is the service, which was superb... up until the point  I was given regular coffee with dessert (vs decaf, as  I had ordered) and I was kept awake nearly all night long. I won’t be back.

I read about Camper in the Mountain View Voice and have been waiting a while to check it out. I think it's a good place to meet up for drinks, but would not recommend it for dinner.
The camper harvest salad was very basic, most spring mix with a few [pickled] carrots thrown in. The dressing was supposed to be an avocado vinaigrette, but it was mostly just salty. 
The tuna crudo was flavorless. The turnip slices added a nice crunch/texture, but there was almost no seasoning at all. 
I avoid dairy, and noted that when I made the reservation. However, when we asked the server which dishes could be done without dairy, it took another 10 minutes for him to check with the kitchen/chef. In the end, we went with one of the pastas without dairy. My pasta tasted freshly made. There was plenty of lamb [ragu?] but very few mushrooms. 
My husband got the short ribs which came with crispy kale and roasted potatoes. The crispy kale chips were the highlight. The short ribs were not tender (still quite chewy).  The side of brussel sprouts was under-cooked and tasted bitter. 
The highlight of the meal was our drinks. Both drinks (alcoholic & non-alcoholic) were well-made and delicious.

I really like this place and recommend it with a few reservations.  They don’t seem to manage the tables very well as there were quite a few empty tables by 7 pm which was surprising as non were listed on open table.  Secondly, they have a few gluten free options but I felt my waiter just didn’t want to deal with a GF diner so he pretty much gave me second class service while he fawned over my non-GF friend.  The food was excellent but over-priced. I guess that is to accommodate the ridiculous rents on the Peninsula. I would not recommend for someone with celiac disease.
noisy and burger was not great.  service was excellent

Food was very salty. Not good for price I can think of many other restaurants that are superior and less expensive. Very disappointing as had high expectations. Decor was nice and service was very good.
Amazing new restaurant. Menu changes daily and Chef has some amazing local connections for ingredient sourcing.
Way too much “smoke” on several dishes... felt like I was eating a campfire. Dry aged beef was almost inedible...
Loud environment, slow (Yet friendly) service, and very under seasoned food. Not worth the price.

We enjoyed our main dishes, but did not enjoy any of the starters. And the desserts were fine, but nothing special. Unfortunately, none of the dishes struck us as inventive or special. So at least they could have tasted good! :) At the end of the night we felt like we paid more than the experience was worth.
The food was good but at the prices they charge for the simple food they serve, I am not inspired to return.

Very disappointed 
Not great service 
Unfriendly sommelier
Very mediocre waiter and overall experience. 
No need to return
Popular, new spot. Later dining availability than usual, for Menlo Park.

New York steak was over-cooked, tough and full of gristel.  Everything else was very good.  Perfect martini.

Service was provided by what I initially thought was a busboy.  A nice fellow but definitely not a seasoned waitperson

I was so anxious to get into this place because it was so difficult to get a reservation for 4 ppl. My husband and I were able to snag a last minute reservation for 2 for date night. I was so excited. 

While the service was exceptional (the staff really takes pride in what they do - really). The food was either over-powering with way too much trying to be accomplished (alla deviled eggs) or underwhelming requiring more salt or seasoning (cauliflower/fish). We ordered more than our share to really sample the menu. The spicy sausage appetizer was average at best. 

We both travel extensively globally and split our time between the US and France. We are not novices to a good meal by and stretch. We dine from food trucks to 2 Michelin Star. I just don’t believe that what we spent was worth the amount. 

The wine list was well curated. Really nice selection - albeit small. Maybe it was a off night. There are so few good options in MP I’m trying to give it a chance. I will return 1 more time to try to taste the rest of the menu. I just highly recommend you downgrading expectation so that you are not disappointed. Hope this helps.
Some hit and miss on food - fries are amazing

This was our second try at Camper - they still have some bugs to work out. The service was good though I had to ask 4 times for ice in my water. Our order was taken promptly and the food arrived hot and quickly. The noise level is really high and 'clangy'. Don't try this if you want to have a conversation. Maybe the back room is better. The deviled eggs have an odd seasoning - a bit like Chinese 5 spice, and very strong aftertaste. The vegetable sides are all good as are some of the pastas. In general, the pastas are very strong tasting so you might want to share. The rigatoni with roast tomato sauce is good, though the sauce is very acidic and would benefit from oil or baking powder to balance the acid. The steak offerings are good - though we haven't tried those yet.  In general, we aren't in a hurry to go back.

The deviled egg appetizer wasn't what I expected (but I could tell work really went in to preparing it).  The Camper salad was different and interesting, however too much quantity.  The local cod was great!  My friend really liked the Peach sorbet!  We sat at 5:30pm with ~25% of the restaurant full and on leaving at ~7:00pm with near full, the noise level had risen to a very high level, way too much for my ears.  If I do decide to come back it would have to be with the outside seating.  A bit pricey, but I could see a lot of other people enjoying themselves for their money.

I hate to pan a new business. I think sometimes companies need to find their footing, and I like to give restaurants the benefit of the doubt that they'll improve as the establishment matures. With that caveat, I was disappointed in Camper. This place has food with San Francisco prices but San Jose quality and service.

We started with cocktails. I ordered the Adirondack Chair, which was delicious. My beau got the Pacifica, which tasted like pure lemon juice with a little bourbon. It was bad enough that he returned it, which we never do.

The menu has snacks, charcuterie, salads and starters, pasta, mains, premium mains, and sides. Since the items are broken out by course, I expected the food to be coursed out, but it wasn't. The server brought all of the food at once, so it got cold. I hope for these prices, that the servers know either to course it, or ask for a preference. 

The food was mediocre, most of it flavorless. The cornbread was cold as if it had been sitting. The chicken liver pate didn't have much salt in it. The deviled eggs had no flavor. The pasta dishes were tasty, but the raviolo was very undercooked, and the agnolotti was cold. The main dish we shared, the rock cod, was very flavorful and served hot.

At the end of the meal, the server asked if we wanted dessert but didn't offer a dessert menu or say anything else and just stood there. It was just awkward, and by the end of a very disappointing meal, I just wanted to leave.

I love the decor of this restaurant. Our server worked hard. The food sounded great, but the restaurant did not curate an enticing experience. I hope it's a one-off and the restaurant will get better. For everything we ordered, including three cocktails, the bill was $180, which is not bad for an excellent meal in San Francisco, but in Menlo Park with mediocre food, the price was not worth it.

We got the avocado dip, rigatoni, 45 day aged steak, and a side of squash. The steak and squash just didn't taste good, and in general we didn't have anything we would order again. Lots of style at this place, but seemingly no substance.
Delicious little bites and scrumptious steak! We also liked the stone fruit crumble with all the seasonal fruits.
Love the owners!  Food was exceptional. We will be back.

Slow service but plenty of people walking around wondering to take the food. Tasteless Tuna crudo. Smokey Beets just didn’t work. Poor combination. Undercooked pasta. Not even close to al dente. Over cooked Short Rib. And a ridiculous corkage fee ($35 - c’mon). This was written up to be an everyday neighborhood place. Not this neighborhood. You have to do better. Did I mention the corkage fee. $35. C’mon.
Excellent menu option,  very tasty, flavorful dishes,  well prepared and plated meals, a bit noisy. We'll visit again.
Great dinner with a great vibe. Highly recommend the agnolotti! The cocktails also were really interesting.

I liked the ambiance and decor. The food concepts are good but need more work on the execution. Shisitos: outside skin was chewy, needed salt. Braised short rib, somewhat tender and it wasn't warm when served. Leeks were chewy. Baked fruit for dessert needed to be baked for around 5 minutes longer, hard pieces of fruit. This place has potential but needs to step up their game.
We enjoyed the food and the atmosphere. Portions were a pleasing size and service was good. We will go back with friends.

Loud, louder and loudest.  We ate early and asked for a quiet table in the back.  I could not hear most of my companion's conversation.  A strange mix on the menu.  Our appetizers were good but does anyone need to eat pickled green strawberries?  Heavy on steaks and skinny fries.  We both had pasta.  My companion's dish had about six mini ravioli and mushrooms with a cup of white cream sauce poured over it, avoid it.  i had pasta with red meat sauce.  It was OK but needed herbs, seasoning and olive oil.  I would go back only for drinks and appetizers.  Be prepared to shout.

I really enjoyed my pasta dish - pimenton pasta with sausage and Jimmy Nardel peppers.  It was spicy, but delicious!  My boyfriend was not so impressed with his steak, but it came with lots of small potatoes and some greens.  We shared the pickled pumpkin salad, which was OK, not great.  The pumpkin and persimmons were good, but the pesto dressing was hardly a dressing.  It was just gummy bits in the lettuce.  The service was friendly, but the space is a little sterile and quite noisy.  The only saving grace was that the tables were spaced well, so you were able to carry on a conversation.

We had a good experience at Camper.  We ordered the burrata salad, which was more interesting than the usual dish given the slightly warmed and smoky tomatoes; anchovy starter; bucatini for my husband, which he found tasty and interesting; chicken for me, which was fine but not super exciting; and sliders and fries for our 9-year-old, which he enjoyed.  Wine selections by the glass were good although somewhat limited.  We were seated near the back of the restaurant.  On the one hand, this was good because it was a little quieter back there.  On the other hand, we felt disconnected from the main room and bustle of the restaurant.  Lighting was a little dead and dark in that back area.  We would return to try more of the menu.
More fine dining in Menlo Park. Great service and great food, but similar price as other local restaurants
Disappointing!  Very loud couldn’t have a conversation.  Food was very average for the price!

20 minutes passed between the time I was seated and when a server first served me. A staff member was chatting with nearby couple that had already been served extensively during this time. Completely unacceptable! 

The potatoes were bland, overcooked, and the shortrib was underseasoned . The roasted beets were very hard, they should have been softer. The pasta dish was too buttery, in a pool of it actually. 

I realize this is a brand new restaurant, but your service needs to improve first and foremost. The menu looked great, but the food was not unexecuted up to your potential.

Outstanding food.  Deviled Eggs = amazing.  Burrata and Heirloom tomatoes.  Blistered peppers.  Excellent.  Pasta = perfect.  Cornbread.  Simply prepared...nothing pretentious, yet unbelievably tasty.  The environment is perfect.  Clean, natural surfaces - great lighting.   Yes, it's noisy, sound dampening is in the works.  Chef Greg and Logan are a huge positive 'add' to Menlo Park.
Super fun neighborhood spot in Menlo Park. Come for the burgers, steaks or the ambitious appetizers, salads and pastas. Great kids menu and desserts (the caramel pudding was A+++).

Noise level very bad.  Hard to have a conversation or speak to staff.  Nduja sausage and tartar not special.
Sunday bolognese and short ribs very good.  Dulce de Leche Pudding terrible - sweet blob of chantilly cream - almost no dulce de leche - very disappointing.
Outstanding service! Food is beautifully prepared. VERY noisy!

Super-loud, super-busy. This new restaurant has quite the buzz. I hope it will succeed and attract more restaurants to downtown MP. Their food is very good. Although I thought the “smoked Greek yogurt” on my kale salad was weird. Burrata salad was terrific, as was the chicken entree and the tuna tartare. We tried two of the special cocktails (the Pescadero and the one with gin/cucumber). Both were tasty.

BUT. There is absolutely nothing to absorb sound in there. Wood floor, chairs and high-back benches with a few throw pillows, that’s all. Plus at this time, Camper had tons of diners. I had to project my voice so my husband could hear me across the table. It had a frenetic vibe, not relaxing after a long day.

Service is also a bit spotty. But this is probably because they’re so busy, and they may have employees who are still learning the ropes.

We’ll go back in a few weeks or months to see if things have settled down. I hope they will. We need more options in Menlo Park!

My wife & I shared the Deviled Eggs & each had a different Pasta as our main dish. The food was delicious although it did take a while to get the entrees. The wait staff was friendly & recommended a chocolate dessert which we also enjoyed. Check it out
The wait staff was a little inexperienced but overall great time!

Very very loud even when only half full. The focus is on guy food- steak with a few other selections. Odd side dishes- garbonzo beans with roast chicken?  The roasted chicken was moist and delicious, steak over cooked. Maybe they are still working out the kinks
Way too loud.  Abuse to ears. Very poor wine list.  Food just OK.  Tahini dressing too bitter.  Wait service friendly.

Very noisy--in fact, too noisy to have a conversation or to hear the waiter.  Very slow service--took forever to place a drink order and for the drinks to show-up.  Difficult to get waiter to show-up again for a food order.  Maybe eating outside would be quieter and more relaxing.  Food was uneven--some items good, others a complete "miss" or "boring" before being finished.  Prices are fairly high.   A "stressful" evening.

It was hard to choose what to have as there too many appealing menu choices which is always a nice challenge to have. Food was outstanding - flavors of the quality ingredients were allowed to shine.  Had a glass of rose with the "cioppino" and found it to be a food friendly wine (dry, not sweet). 

Our particular server could have been more polished and knowledgeable. Seems like he's new to fine dining. He'll need to learn fast.  Prices are very reasonable - don't know if this will continue after they're open a few months.  Will be back!

There were 4 of us in our group--local residents.  Initially, Camper turned me off because it is so loud.  It was difficult to have a conversation, and I think, why meet people here for dinner if you can barely hear each other?  Acoustics need to be looked at.  
The menu looked good and we ordered the eggplant toast and peppers as "bites", the potato dumplings with artichokes and the bucatini with pork ragu as "starters" and the chicken dish as our "mains".  We also all ordered specialty cocktails, and all were good.  I especially liked that they were in tall glasses that actually held something.  As far as the taste of the food, all were very good, with the BIG exception of the bucatini with pork ragu.  Very misleading--it was a small bowl of noodles in a mildly thick red sauce.  No ragu or condiments.  I did exchange it.
The biggest obstacle was their prices.  It was $150 for 2 of us, and I feel that is too high.  Cocktails were $14 each, "Bites" were $8 each, and starters and mains were in the $20-40 range.  The small bowl of bucatini was $24, which was ridiculous.  We won't go back anytime soon with those prices and noise.

We went in for dinner friday night 5:45 and it was pretty loud from the bar. The food wasn’t great and certainly nothing to get excited about (beet salad/burrata, rockfish, pork pasta). Really disappointing as we were looking forward to having a great restaurant in MP.

New restaurant that needs lots of refinement.  
First:  get some drapes to dampen the noise. the restaurant was 1/3 full, and one table with 6 (six) people talking drowned the rest of us.  it was so loud that we could not hear each when we seated four tables away.
second:  more communications between servers and beverage person.
third:  gotta improve consistency on the food and presentation.  My husband's Cod dish was good.  My seaweed pasta with cioppino sauce was "blah".  The broth was good but the shrimps were poorly cooked, and the presentation was not up to par.  Desert was good - a highlight of the meal!
I was very disappointed; especially, Chef Greg came from Per Se.

We drove down from SF to check out CAMPER on their opening night and were blown away by the offerings. Creative cocktails, exceptional handmade pasta, as well as perfect salads and top shelf meats. Some really excellent wines as well. Already planning a return trip to enjoy the rest of the incredible menu!
Cocktails were a highlight!
